ADJUSTMENTS

Body Service

Heat and the use of heavy-duty jacks must be controlled because of the 
gauges and types of steel used in a unitized body. It is possible to pull 
damaged areas back into alignment with the use of light-weight jacks and 
hydraulic equipment, without heating the metal. 

Rough-out badly damaged areas before taking measurements for squaring 
up a body. If necessary, remove the glass from the damaged area to prevent 
breakage. In severe cases, reinforcement brackets and other inner 
constructions may have to be removed or cut to permit restoration of the outer 
shell and pillars without excessive strain on the parts. Straighten, install, 
and secure all such parts in place before attempting to align the body. 

In cases of severe or sharp bends, it may be necessary to use heat. Any 
attempt to cold straighten a severely bent bracket may cause ruptures of the 
welds and may also cause cracks in the bent part. Never heat the area to more 
than a dull red. 

All welding should be done with Rotunda MIG Wire Feed Welder 106-00051 
or equivalent with welding wire meeting AWS-E-70S specifications.

Bump Work

of the repair.

ADJUSTMENTS

Body Misalignment Check 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to correct any serious misalignment with one jacking 
operation. 

To align or square-up a body, take two opposite diagonal measurements 
between the front, center, or rear body pillars. Take the measurements between 
reference points, such as crease lines or weld joints which are diagonally 
opposite each other on the two body pillars being measured. Since all 
measurements should be made from the bare metal, remove all interior trim from 
the checking points. 

Align each section proportionately until the proper dimensions are 
obtained. If body alignment is questionable, refer to the illustration for 
underbody dimensions.

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment, Unitized Body 

 CAUTION: In cases of severe or sharp bends, it may be necessary to use heat. Any 
attempt to cold-straighten a severely bent bracket may cause ruptures of the 
welds. It may also cause cracks in the bent part. Never heat the area to more 
than a dull red. 

 NOTE: Heat and the use of heavy-duty jacks must be carefully controlled 
because of the difference in the gauge of the metal in the side rails of a 
unitized body and the stress points in the unitized body. It is possible to 
pull damaged areas back into alignment with the use of lightweight jacks and 
hydraulic equipment without heating the metal. 

Rough out badly damaged areas before taking measurements for squaring 
up a body. If necessary, remove the glass from the damaged area to prevent 
breakage. In severe cases, remove or cut reinforcement brackets and other 
inner construction to permit restoration of the outer shell and body pillars 
without excessive strain on the parts. Straighten, install, and secure all 
such parts in place before attempting to align the body.

================================================================================
PAGE 1880
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 01-01: Underbody

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Welding

 CAUTION: Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301) before using any electrical 
welding equipment. 

Perform welding using Rotunda MIG Wire Feed Welder 106-00051 or 
equivalent, and welding wire meeting AWS-E-70 S-6 or equivalent specifications.

When performing oxyacetylene welding or brazing, protect the adjacent 
areas with heat insulation compound.

Because more extensive panel deformation results from oxyacetylene 
welding than from MIG welding or spot welding, perform sectional welding using 
MIG welding or spot welding equipment only.

Perform spot welding operations in locations that are inaccessible with 
spot welding tongs using the hole weld method. Drill or punch 5mm (0.2 inch) 
holes in one side of the flange and weld and add filler material.

Varying factors determine plate thickness, panel design, 
cross-sectionals and sizes, joining method, welding method, and welding 
locations during manufacturing. To apply the most suitable repair method, it 
is most important to completely understand the body design, concept, and 
construction.

In a monocoque body shell, the structural elements supporting the 
transaxle and suspension are welded to the bodywork. Every frame member and 
outer panel is designed to offer the maximum protection in the event of 
collision. It is very important that a repaired part meet the same standards 
as those installed on the new vehicle.

It is essential that repair welds, particularly on load-bearing parts 
or parts contributing to the strength of the assembly, are equivalent to the 
originals in size, type, and strength.

 Steel Components, Low Alloy 

 CAUTION: Disconnect the battery ground cable before using any electric welding 
equipment. 

All welding should be done with a Rotunda MIG Welder 106-00051 or 
equivalent, with welding wire meeting AWS-E-70 S-6 or equivalent 
specification. 

Because of associated high heat buildup, do not use oxyacetylene when 
welding high-tensile or high-strength, low alloy steel components. Use spot, 
MIG, or arc welding. During MIG or arc welding, use a temperature-indicating 
crayon to ensure that the temperature does not exceed 650°C 
(1200°F).

Replace spot-welded components by spot welding where possible. If spot 
welding equipment is not available, or if the location is not accessible, 
puddle weld the panels.

Use MIG welding rather than conventional arc welding when welding 
high-strength, high-tensile, or conventional mild steel. Use 0.8mm or 0.9mm 
diameter wire and conform to Classification AWS A5. 18-69 or E70 S-6. MIG 
welding is also known as GMAW (Gas Metal Arc Welding).

When cutting salvageable or repairable components, use a grinding disc, 
air chisel, or metal cutting saw.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hood Components

The hood (16612) is a front-opening type secured by a standard 
double-release hood latch. The hood latch control handle is located below and 
to the left of the steering column.

When the hood is opened, it pivots on the RH hood hinge (16796) and LH 
hood hinge (16797) and is propped open by a hood support rod (16826). The hood 
hinges are attached to the body by two bolts each and to the hood with two 
bolts each.

The hood can be aligned fore and aft and side to side by loosening the 
hood hinge-to-hood bolts.

A hood weatherstrip on the cowl side panel flange and three radiator 
support hood seals (16A238) located on the front inside edge of thehood seal 
the rear and front edges of the hood against the weather.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hood Latch Control Handle and Cable

 Removal 

 WARNING: THE BACKUP POWER SUPPLY ENERGY MUST BE DEPLETED BEFORE ANY AIR BAG 
COMPONENT SERVICE IS PERFORMED. TO DEPLETE THE BACKUP POWER SUPPLY ENERGY, 
DISCONNECT THE BATTERY GROUND CABLE (14301) AND WAIT ONE MINUTE. 

Disconnect the battery (10655) and wait one minute for the air bag

Remove the center air bag sensor and bracket bolt.

[FIGURE: N11234B.gif]

Remove the radiator grille support bracket-to-hood latch nut.

Remove the two hood latch bolts.

[FIGURE: N11235B.gif]

Disconnect the hood latch control cable from the hood latch (16700).

[FIGURE: N11351B.gif]

Attach mechanic's wire to the end of the hood latch control cable to 
ease installation.

Loosen the nut securing the hood latch control handle to the instrument 
panel (04320) inside the vehicle.

Remove the hood latch control handle from the instrument panel inside 
the vehicle.

From inside the vehicle, carefully pull the hood latch control cable 
out through the engine compartment and through the bulkhead. Pull through the 
mechanic's wire to assist in installation.

Remove the hood latch control handle and cable (16916).

 Installation 

Attach the end of the mechanic's wire to the new hood latch control 
cable.

Pull the new hood latch control cable through the bulkhead and through 
the engine compartment using the mechanic's wire.

Position the hood latch control handle onto the instrument panel and 
tighten the nut securely.

Connect the hood latch control cable to the hood latch.

Install the two hood latch bolts. Tighten the hood latch bolts to 8-11 Nm
 (71-97 lb-in).

Install the radiator grille support bracket-to-hood latch nut. Tighten 
the radiator grille support bracket-to-hood latch nut to 19-25 Nm
 (14-19 lb-ft).

Install the center air bag sensor and bracket bolt. Tighten the center 
air bag sensor and bracket bolt to 9-13 Nm (79-113 lb-in).

If necessary, adjust the hood latch. Refer to the procedure in this 
section.

ADJUSTMENTS

Hood Alignment

Verify that the hood (16612) can be closed easily and that there is no 
looseness in the hood hinges (16796). Replace the hood hinges if they can not 
be tightened. Refer to the procedure in this section.

 1.0mm (0.16 ± 0.04 inch) at point 1.

[FIGURE: N11364A.gif]

hood hinge-to-hood bolts and repositioning the hood.

[FIGURE: N11365A.gif]

Tighten the hood hinge to-hood bolts to 19-25 Nm 
(14-19 lb-ft).

Hood Latch

1997 Aspire

Section 01-03: Doors, Liftgate

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Doors

The front doors (20124) are attached to the body by two pin-type 
hinges. A sliding front door hinge check (22886), attached to the front door 
by two nuts and to the body by a hinge pin (43030), limits the travel of the 
door opening. A hollow rubber front door weatherstrip (20530) installed on the 
door opening flange prevents leaks between the front door and body. 

Inside the door are two serviceable side impact protection pads and two 
non-serviceable side impact pads on the back side of the front door trim panel 
(23942).

================================================================================
PAGE 1908
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 01-03: Doors, Liftgate

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Liftgate

The liftgate is attached to the body by two pin-type liftgate hinges 
(42900) bolted to the liftgate header. Two liftgate gas lifts on the liftgate 
aid in the opening of the liftgate and support it when open. A liftgate latch 
at the bottom center of the liftgate keeps the liftgate in the closed 
position. 

A liftgate weatherstrip installed on the liftgate flange prevents leaks 
between the liftgate and the body. The liftgate weatherstrip is held firmly in 
place by a moulded-in metal backing that fits over and grips the liftgate 
flange.

[FIGURE: GN0640A.gif]

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Door Inspection

Verify that the door can be closed easily and that there is no 
looseness in the door hinges. Replace the door hinges if they cannot be 
tightened. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Verify that there is no play when the door is closed. If play is 
evident, the door latch striker plate (22008) and/or the door hinges need to 
be adjusted. Refer to the Door Alignment procedure in this section.

Verify that the clearance between the body and the door is not 
excessive or uneven. If the clearance is excessive or uneven, the door latch 
striker plate and/or the door hinges need adjustment. Refer to the Door 
Alignment procedure in this section.

Section 01-03: Doors, Liftgate

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Door Alignment

 Door Hinge Check 

If the door-to-body clearance is uneven, loosen the door hinge-to-body 
bolts and nuts and adjust the door.

Tighten the front/rear door hinge-to-body bolts and nuts to 17-29 Nm
 (13-21 lb-ft).

 Striker Plate, Door Latch 

If there is excessive door play or excessive door-to-body clearance 
when the door is closed, loosen the door latch striker plate screws and adjust 
the door latch striker plate (22008).

[FIGURE: N11230A.gif]

Tighten the door latch striker plate screws to 18-26 Nm
 (13-19 lb-ft).

================================================================================
PAGE 1915
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 01-03: Doors, Liftgate

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment, Liftgate

Verify that the liftgate can be closed easily and that there is no 
looseness in the liftgate hinges. Replace the liftgate hinges if they cannot 
be tightened. Refer to the procedure in this section.

If there is excessive play when the liftgate is closed, the liftgate 
latch striker needs to be aligned.

Loosen the liftgate latch striker bolts and adjust the liftgate latch 
striker.

[FIGURE: N11020A.gif]

Tighten the liftgate latch striker bolts to 8-11 Nm 
(71-97 lb-in).

If the clearance between the liftgate and the body is excessive or 
uneven, loosen the liftgate hinge-to-liftgate nuts and reposition the liftgate.

When the clearance is satisfactory, tighten the liftgate 
hinge-to-liftgate nuts to 9-12 Nm (7-9 lb-ft).

Section 01-03: Doors, Liftgate

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

LUBRICATION

Lubricant

 Weatherstrip 

Use Silicone Lubricant C0AZ-19553-AA, D7AZ-19533-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A, on the front door weatherstrip (20530), 
rear door weatherstrip (25324), and liftgate weatherstrips. It is recommended 
that silicone lubricant be applied to the weatherstrips whenever necessary. 
Silicone lubricant helps avoid weatherstrip squeaks and retards excess 
weatherstrip wear caused by chafing between the door and the weatherstrip. 

 Hinge, Door 

Use Multi-Purpose Grease Spray D7AZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C106-B, to lubricate the front and rear 
door hinges.

 Hinge, Liftgate 

Use Multi-Purpose Grease Spray D7AZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C106-B, to lubricate the liftgate hinges.

Headlining, Roof

[FIGURE: R9932A.gif]

PAGE 1923
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 01-05: Trim, Interior

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Carpets, Floor

The floor carpet (13000) is a two-piece design. One piece covers the 
cargo area and the other covers the front and rear floor areas. The seam 
between the cargo area and the passenger compartment is secured to the rear 
floor pan (11215) with push-type retainers. Push-type retainers also anchor 
under the front seats. Except at the door openings, the perimeter of the floor 
carpet is concealed under the trim panels. At the door openings, the floor 
carpet is secured to the door jamb flanges by door scuff plate spacers (13204) 
and covered by the front door scuff plates (13209) and rear door scuff plates 
(13228) (on the 4-door models).

1997 Aspire

Section 01-08: Trim, Exterior

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mouldings, Exterior

 Body Side Protection 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Remove and replace one body side protection moulding at a time. 

COMPLETELY clean the sheet metal surface area around the body side 
protection moulding with isopropyl alcohol and a clean, soft cloth.

Use masking tape to mark the top and end locations of the body side 
protection moulding prior to removal.

 NOTE: Heating the body side protection moulding or sheet metal will increase 
adhesion and make it hard to remove. Cold temperatures of 0°C 
(32°F) and below allow easier removal.

Use a nylon wedge when removing body side protection mouldings. 
Position the nylon wedge between the body side protection moulding and sheet 
metal and pull the body side protection moulding away with steady tension. 

[FIGURE: N11211A.gif]

 NOTE: All of the adhesive tape will not come off with the body side 
protection moulding. White or gray acrylic tape can be removed by gently 
stretching it. 

Once a few inches of moulding are free, grip it with both hands and 
pull it slowly to remove. Be careful not to damage the paint or sheet metal.

Grip the adhesive tape at one end, lifting and pulling away slowly 
about 12.7mm (0.5 in) at a time. Small pieces can be removed by rolling with 
your thumb across the sheet metal surface.

 Installation 

After all the tape is removed, wipe the area with isopropyl alcohol and 
a clean soft cloth. Ensure that all tape residue and road dirt is removed from 
the area.

If the paint surface is damaged during body side protection moulding 
removal, repair as required. Refer to Section 01-00 . 

 NOTE: Body side protection mouldings should not be installed on vehicles 
unless sheet metal surface temperature exceeds 27°C (80°
F) and the body side protection moulding is at 21°
C (70°F) minimum.

Apply the new body side protection moulding by pulling back the 
adhesive tape protective cover about 76-101mm (3-4 inches) at the front edge 
of the body side protection moulding. Do not touch or contaminate the tape 
surface.

Align the new body side protection moulding with the masking tape 
applied during the removal procedure and gently press the body side protection 
moulding, removing the protective cover as you proceed.

Ensure that the body side protection moulding is aligned correctly; 
once the adhesive tape is applied to the vehicle surface, the body side 
protection moulding cannot be removed repositioned.

Remove the masking tape and wipe the area under the masking tape with 
isopropyl alcohol to remove the tape residue.

Press the body side protection moulding on with a hand roller, applying 
a minimum of 137.9 kPa (20 psi) of pressure to ensure proper adhesion.

Section 01-09: Mirrors, Rear View

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Mirror, Inside Rear View

 Manual 

The inside rear view mirror (17700) is mounted on an inside rear view 
mirror bracket (17698) located above the windshield glass (03100). The inside 
rear view mirror is secured to the inside rear view mirror bracket with one 
screw. The inside rear view mirror bracket is secured to the roof with two 
screws.

The inside rear view mirror has a day/night adjustment lever located at 
the bottom of the inside rear view mirror frame. In the day position, the 
inside rear view mirror provides a direct reflection. In the night position, 
the inside rear view mirror provides an indirect reflection that reduces the 
headlamp glare from other vehicles.

Mirrors, Outside 

 CAUTION: Outside rear view mirrors (17682) should not be cleaned with a dry

reflective surface may result.

================================================================================

1997 Aspire

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Latch, Manual

When the front seat back latch lever is lifted on the driver or 
passenger seat, the lock pawl disengages from the teeth on the gear quadrant 
to allow the front seat back cover and cushion (60136) to tilt. If the front 
seat back latch lever is operated while the seat is unoccupied, the large 
tension spring will automatically tilt the front seat back cover and cushion 
fully forward. If the seat is occupied, the front seat back cover and cushion 
can be pushed backward against spring pressure to whatever angle the seat 
occupant desires. When the front seat back latch lever is released, the lock 
pawl engages the gear quadrant and the lock pawl spring holds the lock pawl in 
the position selected.

1997 Aspire

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seat, Rear

 Fold Down Rear 

The rear seat is available in the following options:

One-piece fold (standard on 2-door)

One-piece flip fold (standard on 4-door)

50/50 split fold (optional on 4-door)

50/50 split flip fold (optional on 2-door)

The one-piece flip fold and 50/50 split flip fold rear seats are 
attached to the vehicle floor at the front of the rear seat cushion and cover 
(60030) by two hinges held to the vehicle floor by two bolts and nuts. Each 
hinge can be removed from the rear seat cushion and cover by removing the 
pivot pin and bushing.

When the rear seat back latch release buttons (62432) at the top of the 
rear seat back cover and cushion (60084) are lifted, the rear seat back 
release latch (61383) is disengaged, allowing the rear seat back cover and 
cushion to be folded forward.

To allow for upward movement of the rear seat cushion and cover, the 
flip fold rear seat back cover and cushions are attached at the outboard side 
of the rear seat cushion and covers by a rear seat back to cushion bolt and 
bushing. With this type of assembly, the entire rear seat can be folded 
forward against the front seats.

[FIGURE: R5361D.gif]

The 50/50 split flip fold rear seats incorporate a center hinge, 
secured by a center pin pivot stud and rear seat back pivot bushing (613B44). 
The center hinge is held to the vehicle floor by two bolts.

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Seat, Driver or Passenger 

 Removal 

Remove the four front seat cushion frame and spring bolts.

[FIGURE: R7528E.gif]

 CAUTION: To avoid possible damage to seat components, handle the front seat 
cushion frame and spring (63100) with care. 

Remove the seat and track assembly.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Before installing the seat and track assembly, ensure that the front 
seat back latch (62648), front seat slide lock knob (611A98) and the seat back 
release knob (passenger seat, 2-door models only) move smoothly and are not 
worn. 

 NOTE: Apply Ford Multi-Purpose Grease D7AZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specifications ESB-M1C106-B and ESR-M159-A to all moving parts prior to 
installation. 

Install the seat and track assembly.

ADJUSTMENTS

Seats, Front

If the front seat is moving inconsistently or not moving on the tracks 
at all when the front seat slide lock knob (611A98) is engaged, the front seat 
track cable may need adjustment. 

Refer to the following procedure:

Remove the driver or passenger seat. Refer to the procedure in this 
section.

Loosen the locknuts at both ends of the cable.

Tighten the locknuts at both ends of the cable until the front seat 
cushion and cover (60052) moves freely on the track when the front seat slide 
lock knob is pulled upward.

Install the driver or passenger seat. Refer to the procedure in this 
section.

Windshield Glass

The windshield glass (03100) is standard safety glass-plastic-laminate 
sandwiched between two sheets of glass. 

Urethane bonds the windshield glass to the windshield opening flange.

PAGE 1987

1997 Aspire

Section 01-11: Glass, Frames and Mechanisms

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Windows, Manual

Both front and rear door windows are manually operated as follows: 

A cable-operated window regulator moves the glass up and down. 

The cable loops around a drum attached to the window regulator handle 
(23342) by a regulator handle snap ring (23350) behind the window regulator 
handle. 

The cable extends from the regulator drum to a slider bracket that 
engages and rides on a slider bar. Smooth operation is ensured by nylon 
inserts serving as bearing surfaces between the slider bar and the slider 
bracket. 

When the window regulator handle is rotated counterclockwise to lower 
the door window glass, the continuous cable rolls around a drum in the 
regulator handle housing and pulls the slider bracket downward along the 
slider bar. 

When the window regulator handle is turned clockwise the window is 
raised in a similar manner.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Window Glass, Door

The bottom of the door glass is mounted on a slider bracket that is

stabilizers (22380) provide attachment points for the glass and prevent direct 
contact between the glass and the slider bracket.

Window Glass, Rear Quarter

The quarter window glass (29710) is a standard safety glass and is 
installed with a urethane bond in the quarter window opening flange. The 
quarter window extends from the rear door to the liftgate in the rear body 
pillar on each side of the vehicle on the 4-door model only.

The rear quarter window glass extends from the center body pillar to 
the rear body pillar on each side of the vehicle on the 2-door model only.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Window, Heated Back

The back window glass (42006) may come as an optional heated back 
window glass which is identified by thin orange grid lines on the inside of 
the back window glass running side to side. Care must be taken when loading 
and unloading the luggage area, closing the liftgate, and cleaning so as not 
to scratch the grid lines and damage the heated back window glass. Refer to 
the procedure in this section to repair the grid lines on the heated back 
window glass. The back window glass is a standard safety glass.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Switch and Light, Heated Back Window 

The heated back window switch and light (18C621) is located in the 
center of the instrument panel (04320), next to the light switch rheostat 
resistor (11691). To engage the heated back window glass (42006), the heated 
back window switch and light button must be depressed. This will activate the 
yellow indicator on the instrument cluster and the button will light up. Push 
the heated back window switch and light button to release the button to 
disengage the heated back window glass. The heated back window switch and 
light must be manually disengaged; it will not turn off automatically.

Inspection and Verification — Heated Back Window System

Verify the customer concern by operating the heated back window system.

Visually inspect the components of the heated back window system for 
breakage, or corrosion.

20A DEFOG

Damage to wiring harness

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Test — Heated Back Window System

 Heated Back Window Switch and Light 

Key OFF.

Disconnect instrument cluster C210.

Key ON.

Measure the voltage between the instrument cluster pin C210-1 (BK/R) 
and ground.

With the heated back window switch in the ON position the voltage 
should be approximately 10 volts.

With the heated back window switch in the OFF position there should be 
less than 1 volt.

Measure the resistance between the instrument cluster pin C210-13 (BK) 
and ground.

The resistance should be less than 5 ohms.

If the heated back window switch indicator light circuits are not 
within specification, repair circuit(s) that does not match specifications.

If the heated back window switch indicator light circuits are within 
specification, refer to Section 13-01 to diagnose the instrument cluster.

 Heated Back Window Grid Wire Test 

Key ON.

Turn on the heated back window switch.

Measure the voltage between the center of each heated back window grid 
filament and ground.

The voltages should be approximately 5 volts ± 1 
volt at the center of each filament.

If the heated back window grid does not operate as specified, repair 
the filament(s) in question by referring to the back window grid wire service 
procedure in this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Windshield Glass

The following tools are recommended to properly remove and install the 
windshield glass (03100):

Rotunda Sealant Dispensing Gun 164-R3154 or equivalent

Rotunda Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent

Razor blade knife

Installation Kit E0AZ-19562-A or equivalent

Alcohol free glass cleaner in a spray bottle

Latex gloves

EC7784 lubricant in a spray bottle or equivalent

 Removal 

Remove the windshield wiper pivot arms (17526) by removing the 
windshield wiper pivot arm nut and pulling straight up.

[FIGURE: K20828A.gif]

Pull up to unsnap and remove the lower windshield outside moulding 
(03148). 

Pull up at the bottom corner and peel back the upper windshield outside 
moulding (03144) to remove.

[FIGURE: N11090D.gif]

 WARNING: TO PREVENT GLASS SPLINTERS FROM ENTERING EYES OR CUTTING HANDS, WEAR 
SAFETY GLASSES AND HEAVY GLOVES WHEN CUTTING GLASS FROM THE VEHICLE. 

Pull down the interior trim moulding from the front door opening at the 
front body pillar and remove the interior trim panel from the front body pillar.

 NOTE: Lubricate the urethane sealant to be cut with water to aid the Rotunda 
Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent, when cutting 
the urethane sealant.

Use Rotunda Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or 
equivalent, to cut the urethane sealant around the windshield glass.

[FIGURE: N10576E.gif]

Insert the inflatable pump bag at the top of the windshield glass and 
gently push the windshield outward 12.7mm (0.5 inch) from the inside of the 
vehicle to ensure the urethane seal is broken. Use the razor blade knife to 
cut any urethane sealant that may be holding down the windshield glass.

[FIGURE: GN0541A.gif]

Remove the windshield glass.

Trim the remaining old urethane on the pinch weld to within 1.0 - 1.5 
mm (0.04 - 0.06 inch) thickness using a suitable tool. When completed, the old 
urethane surface should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination.

[FIGURE: N10577C.gif]

Check the pinch weld for damaged sheet metal, raised sheet metal at the 
spot welds, rust or foreign material which may cause glass damage. Service the 
pinch weld sheet metal as necessary. Refer to Section 01-00 .

If the same windshield glass is to be installed, remove all the old 
urethane from the windshield glass. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Always wear nitrile gloves when using the chemicals for installation. 

 NOTE: Keep glass and body surfaces free of dirt, water, and oil. Do not touch 
coated surfaces with hands.

Thoroughly clean the inside of the windshield glass with an alcohol 
free glass cleaner. Then dry set the windshield glass into the opening and use 
tape on all four sides to mark the proper setting position of the glass, then 
remove the windshield glass.

 NOTE: Wipe off the Urethane Glass Prep (part of E0AZ-19562-A), or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M5B280-C, immediately after application because 
it flash dries. The Urethane Glass Prep must be applied twice.

Apply Urethane Glass Prep (part of E0AZ-19562-A) or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSB-M5B280-C, in a 15mm (0.6 inch) wide application around 
the entire outer edge of the inside of the windshield glass. Immediately wipe 
the cleaner off the windshield glass. Repeat the application and immediately 
wipe off glass.

[FIGURE: N10578C.gif]

 WARNING: IF PRIMER GETS ON YOUR HANDS, REMOVE IT IMMEDIATELY. 

Using the supplied wool applicator, apply Urethane Glass Primer (part 
of E0AZ-19562-A) or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G314-B, in a 
15mm (0.6 inch) wide application around the entire outer edge of the inside of 
the windshield glass. Allow 10 minutes drying time for the primer.

[FIGURE: N10578C.gif]

Using the supplied wool applicator, apply Urethane Metal Primer or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G234-C, to the pinch weld of the 
vehicle. Allow approximately 10 minutes drying time for the primer.

Install open cell Vinyl Foam Tape C6AZ-19627-A or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESB-M3G77-A, to the pinch weld. Start the vinyl foam tape 
at the center of the bottom pinch weld 8mm (0.310 in) and lay it around the 
entire pinch weld from the inside edge. Cut the tape and butt the ends together.

[FIGURE: N10178D.gif]

Cut the nozzle of the urethane canister so that it lays a bead of 
urethane 16mm (0.625 inch) high and 8mm (0.310 inch)wide.

[FIGURE: N10516C.gif]

Starting at the bottom center of the pinch weld, lay a uniform bead of 
urethane along the entire outside edge of the open cell vinyl foam tape 16mm 
(0.625 inch) in height and 8mm (0.310 inch) wide. Ensure that the bead of 
urethane is smooth and even. If necessary, reshape the bead with a suitable 
tool taking care not to trap air in the bead.

[FIGURE: N10551D.gif]

Open the windows to prevent the windshield glass from being pushed out 
by air pressure if a door is closed. 

Lift and center the windshield glass into position and push in lightly 
to compress the urethane. 

Clean any excess urethane from the windshield glass or pinch weld. 

 CAUTION: The windshield outside moulding must be installed before the urethane 
sealant has hardened. 

 CAUTION: Use only Urethane/Adhesive (part of E0AZ-19562-A), or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G316-B to service water and air leaks of the 
urethane sealant. 

 CAUTION: After replacing the urethane installed glass, the vehicle should not be 
driven until the urethane has cured. The curing time at temperatures above 13°
C (55°F) and relative humidity above 50% is 
12-24 hours (decreasing cure at higher temperatures and lower humidities). 
Refer to the detailed instructions provided by the manufacturer in the kit. 
Inadequate curing of the urethane may adversely affect the strength of the 
urethane sealant bond. 

Press in the upper windshield outside moulding starting at a bottom 
corner and firmly pressing the moulding into the urethane in between the 
windshield glass and the body. Snap the lower windshield outside moulding into 
place. 

Install the windshield wiper pivot arms. Adjust the windshield wiper 
pivot arms as necessary, refer to Section 01-16 . Tighten the windshield wiper 
pivot arm nuts to 10-15 Nm (8-11 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Window Glass, Back

The following tools are recommended to properly remove and install the 
back window glass (42006):

Rotunda Sealant Dispensing Gun 164-R3154 or equivalent

Rotunda Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent

Razor blade knife

Installation Kit E0AZ-19562-A, or equivalent

Alcohol free glass cleaner in a spray dispenser

Latex gloves

EC7784 lubricant in spray bottle or equivalent

 Removal 

Remove the liftgate door trim panel (46404). Refer to Section 01-03 for 
the removal procedure.

Disconnect the heated back window glass electrical connector.

Remove the interior back window opening moulding from the pinch weld.

Remove the rear spoiler. Refer to Section 01-08 for the removal 
procedure.

Remove the top exterior moulding by pulling up at one end and peeling 
it back.

Remove both side back window mouldings by sliding them off of the side 
of the liftgate.

Using the Rotunda Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or 
equivalent, after lubricating the urethane by spraying it with water cut the 
urethane bond on each side of the back window glass.

Install inflatable pump bag and gently lift the back window glass from 
the top of the liftgate pinch weld. Using a razor blade knife separate any 
urethane still holding the back window glass.

[FIGURE: GN0542A.gif]

Remove the back window glass.

If reinstalling the same back window glass, remove all of the urethane 
from the back window glass.

Trim the remaining old urethane on the pinch weld to within 1.0 - 1.5 
mm (0.04 - 0.06 inch) thickness using a suitable tool. When completed, the old 
urethane surface should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination.

[FIGURE: N10577C.gif]

Check the pinch weld for damaged sheet metal, raised sheet metal at the 
spot welds, rust or foreign material which may cause glass damage. Service the 
pinch weld sheet metal as necessary. Refer to Section 01-00 .

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Always wear nitrile gloves when using the chemicals for installation. 

 NOTE: Keep glass and body surfaces free of dirt, water, and oil. Do not touch 
coated surfaces with hands.

Thoroughly clean the inside of the back window glass with an alcohol 
free glass cleaner.

 NOTE: Wipe off the Urethane Glass Prep (part of E0AZ-19562-A), or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M5B280-C, immediately after application because 
it flash dries. The Urethane Glass Prep must be applied twice.

Apply Urethane Glass Prep (part of E0AZ-19562-A) or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSB-M5B280-C, in a 25mm (1 inch) wide application around 
the entire outer edge of the inside of the back window glass. Immediately wipe 
the cleaner off of the back window glass. Repeat the application of the 
Urethane Glass Prep.

[FIGURE: N10181C.gif]

 WARNING: IF PRIMER GETS ON YOUR HANDS, REMOVE IT IMMEDIATELY. 

With the supplied wool applicator, apply the Urethane Glass Primer or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G314-B, in a 25mm (1 inch) wide 
application around the entire outer edge of theback window glass. Allow 10 
minutes drying time for the primer.

[FIGURE: N10181C.gif]

With the supplied wool applicator, apply Urethane Metal Primer or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G234-C, to the liftgate pinch 
weld. Allow approximately 10 minutes drying time for the primer.

Install open cell Vinyl Foam Tape C6AZ-19627-A or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESB-M3G77-A, to the pinch weld. Start the vinyl foam tape 
at the center of the bottom of the pinch weld and lay it around the entire 
pinch weld 8mm (0.310 inch) from the inside edge.

[FIGURE: N10178D.gif]

Cut the nozzle of the urethane canister so that it lays a bead of 
urethane 16mm (0.625 inch) high and 8mm (0.310 inch) wide.

[FIGURE: N10516C.gif]

Lay a uniform bead of urethane along the entire outside edge of the 
vinyl foam tape 16mm (0.625 inch) in height and 8mm (0.310 inch) wide. Ensure 
that the bead of urethane is smooth and even. If necessary, reshape the bead 
with a suitable tool, taking care not to trap air in the bead.

[FIGURE: N10551D.gif]

Open the vehicle windows to prevent the back window glass from being 
pushed out by air pressure if a door is closed.

 CAUTION: The windshield outside moulding (03144) must be installed before the 
urethane sealant has hardened. 

 CAUTION: Use only Urethane Adhesive (part of E0AZ-19562-A), or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G316-B to service water and air leaks of the 
urethane sealant. 

 CAUTION: After replacing the urethane installed glass, the vehicle should not be 
driven until the urethane has cured. The curing time at temperatures above 13°
C (55°F) and relative humidity above 50% is 
12-24 hours (decreasing cure at higher temperatures and lower humidities). 
Refer to the detailed instructions provided by the manufacturer in the kit. 
Inadequate curing of the urethane may adversely affect the strength of the 
urethane sealant bond. 

Place the back window glass into position and push in lightly to 
compress the urethane.

Clean any excess urethane from the back window glass and the pinch weld.

Install the side and top back window mouldings.

Install the rear spoiler. Refer to Section 01-08 for the installation 
procedure.

Install the interior back window moulding onto the pinch weld.

Connect the heated back window glass electrical connector.

Install the liftgate door trim panel. Refer to Section 01-03 for the 
installation procedure.

Window Glass, Rear Quarter — 4 Door

The following tools are recommended to properly remove and install the 
quarter window glass (29710):

Rotunda Sealant Dispensing Gun 164-R3154 or equivalent

Rotunda Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent

Razor blade knife

Installation Kit E0AZ-19562-A or equivalent

Alcohol free glass cleaner in a spray dispenser

Latex gloves

EC7784 lubricant in a spray bottle or equivalent

 Removal 

Remove the package tray panel.

Remove the two package tray upper trim panel support screws, and the 
four push pins.

Remove the package tray upper trim panel support (46809).

Pull out the luggage compartment side cover (45422) to detach from the 
clips. Remove the luggage compartment side cover.

Remove the rear safety belt guide bolt from the rear body pillar.

[FIGURE: N11093A.gif]

Pull out and remove the upper quarter trim panel. 

Remove the three quarter window glass nuts.

[FIGURE: N11094B.gif]

Use the Rotunda Interior Auto Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or 
equivalent, after lubricating the urethane by spraying it with water in a 
spray bottle to cut the urethane sealant.

Push gently from inside of the quarter window glass, using the razor 
blade knife to cut any remaining urethane holding thequarter window glass in 
place.

Remove the quarter window glass.

Trim the remaining old urethane on the pinch weld to within 1.0 - 2.0mm 
(0.04 - 0.06 inch) thickness using a suitable tool. When completed, the old 
urethane surface should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination.

[FIGURE: N11601A.gif]

Check the pinch weld for damaged sheet metal, raised sheet metal at the 
spot welds, rust or foreign material which may cause glass damage. Service the 
pinch weld sheet metal as necessary. Refer to Section 01-00 .

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Always wear nitrile gloves when using the chemicals for installation. 

Thoroughly clean the inside of the quarter window glass with an alcohol 
free glass cleaner.

 NOTE: Wipe off the Urethane Glass Prep (part of E0AZ-19562-A), or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M5280-C, immediately after application because 
it flash dries. The Urethane Glass Prep must be applied twice.

Apply the Urethane Glass Prep (part of E0AZ-19562-A) or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M5280-C, in a 25mm (1 inch) wide application 
around the entire outer edge of the inside of the quarter window glass. 
Immediately wipe the cleaner off of the quarter window glass. Repeat the 
application of the Urethane Glass Prep.

[FIGURE: N10181C.gif]

 WARNING: IF PRIMER GETS ON YOUR HANDS, REMOVE IT IMMEDIATELY. 

Using the supplied wool applicator, apply the Urethane Glass Primer or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G314-B, in a 25mm (1 inch) wide 
application around the entire outer edge of the inside of the quarter window 
glass. Allow 10 minutes drying time for the primer.

[FIGURE: N10181C.gif]

Using the supplied wool applicator, apply the Urethane Metal Primer or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSB-M2G234-C, to the quarter window 
pinch weld. Allow approximately 10 minutes drying time for the primer.

Install the open cell Vinyl Foam Tape C6AZ-19627-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M3G77-A to the quarter window pinch weld. Start 
the vinyl foam tape at the center of the bottom of the pinch weld and lay it 
around the entire pinch weld 8mm (0.310 inch) from the inside edge.

[FIGURE: N10178D.gif]

Cut the nozzle of the urethane canister so that it lays a bead of 
urethane 16mm (0.625 inch) high and 8mm (0.310 inch) wide.

[FIGURE: N10516C.gif]

Lay a uniform bead of urethane along the entire outside edge of the 
vinyl foam tape 16mm (0.625 inch) high and 8mm (0.310 inch) wide. Ensure that 
the bead of urethane is smooth and even. If necessary, reshape the bead with a 
suitable tool.

[FIGURE: N10551D.gif]

Open the vehicle windows to prevent the quarter window glass from being 
pushed out by air pressure if a door is closed.

 CAUTION: Use only Urethane Sealant (part of E0AZ-19562-A), or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSB-M2G316-B to service water and air leaks of the urethane 
sealant. 

 CAUTION: After replacing the urethane installed glass, the vehicle should not be 
driven until the urethane has cured. The curing time at temperatures above 13°
C (55°F) and relative humidity above 50% is 
12-24 hours (decreasing cure at higher temperatures and lower humidities). 
Refer to the detailed instructions provided by the manufacturer in the kit. 
Inadequate curing of the urethane may adversely affect the strength of the 
urethane sealant bond. 

Place the quarter window glass in position and press lightly to 
compress the urethane.

Install the three quarter window glass nuts at the corners of the 
quarter window glass. Tighten the quarter window glass nuts to 2.5-3.5 Nm
 (24-30 lb-in).

[FIGURE: N11094B.gif]

Install the upper quarter trim panel.

Install the rear safety belt guide bolt in the rear body pillar. 
Tighten the rear safety belt guide bolt to 38-78 Nm (28-57 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: N11093A.gif]

Install the luggage compartment side cover.

Install the three package tray upper trim panel support screws and the 
two push pins.

Install the package tray panel.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Window Glass, Rear Quarter — 2 Door

The following tools are recommended to properly remove and install the 
quarter window glass (29710):

Rotunda Sealant Dispensing Gun 164-R3154 or equivalent

Razor blade knife

Installation Kit E0AZ-19562-A, or equivalent

Alcohol free glass cleaner in a spray dispenser

Latex gloves

 Removal 

Remove the package tray panel.

Remove the three package tray upper trim panel support screws and the 
two push pins. 

Remove the package tray upper trim panel support (46809).

Remove the five push pins and remove the luggage compartment side cover 
(45422).

Remove the rear safety belt guide cover and the rear safety belt guide 
bolt from the rear body pillar.

[FIGURE: R9021B.gif]

Remove the three push pins and pull down to remove the quarter trim 
panel (31012) from the rear body pillar.

Remove the front seat shoulder strap boot and the front safety belt 
guide bolt from the center body pillar.

[FIGURE: R10008C.gif]

Pull out to detach and remove the center body pillar inside upper 
finish panel (24357) from the center body pillar.

Remove the quarter window glass center body pillar moulding by pulling 
out at the center to detach the center clip and continue to pull out to slide 
out of the top retainer. Be careful not to crimp or damage the quarter window 
glass center body pillar moulding. Slide the bottom of the quarter window 
glass center body pillar moulding out of the bottom retainer and remove the 
quarter window glass center body pillar moulding.

Using the two handle knife, cut the urethane bond around the quarter 
window glass.

[FIGURE: GN0543A.gif]

Gently push the quarter window glass from the inside and use the razor 
blade knife to cut any remaining urethane bond.

Remove the quarter window glass.

If reinstalling the same quarter window glass, remove all of the old 
urethane from the quarter window glass.

Trim the remaining old urethane on the pinch weld to within 1.0 - 2.0mm 
(0.04 - 0.06 inch) thickness using a suitable tool. When completed, the old 
urethane surface should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination.

[FIGURE: N10577C.gif]

Check the pinch weld for damaged sheet metal, raised sheet metal at the 
spot welds, rust or foreign material which may cause glass damage. Service the 
pinch weld sheet metal as necessary. Refer to Section 01-00 .

Apply the Urethane Metal Primer or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSB-M2G234-C, to any exposed metal on the quarter window pinch 
weld. Allow approximately 10 minutes drying time for the primer.

[FIGURE: N11097C.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Always wear nitrile gloves when using the chemicals for installation. 

Thoroughly clean the inside of the quarter window glass.

Apply the Urethane Glass Prep (part of E0AZ-19562-A) or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSB-M5280-C, in a 25mm (1 inch) wide application 
around the entire outer edge of the inside of the quarter window glass. 
Immediately wipe the cleaner off of the quarter window glass because it flash 
dries. Repeat the application.

[FIGURE: N10181C.gif]

 WARNING: IF PRIMER GETS ON YOUR HANDS, REMOVE IT IMMEDIATELY. 

Apply the Urethane Glass Primer or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSB-M2G314-B, in a 25mm (1 inch) wide application around the 
entire outer edge of the inside of the quarter window glass.

[FIGURE: N10181C.gif]

Install the open cell Vinyl Foam Tape C6AZ-19627-A or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M3G77-A, to the quarter window pinch weld. 
Start the vinyl foam tape at the center of the bottom of the pinch weld and 
lay it around the entire pinch weld 8mm (0.310 inch) from the inside edge.

[FIGURE: N10178D.gif]

Cut the nozzle of the urethane canister so that it lays a bead of 
urethane 16mm (0.625 inch) high and 8mm (0.310 inch) wide.

[FIGURE: N10516C.gif]

Starting at the bottom center of the pinch weld, lay a uniform bead of 
urethane along the entire outside edge of the vinyl foam tape 16mm (0.625 
inch) high and 8mm (0.310 inch) wide. Ensure that the bead of urethane is 
smooth and even. If necessary, reshape the urethane with a suitable tool, 
taking care not to trap air in the bead.

[FIGURE: N10551D.gif]

Open the vehicle windows to prevent the quarter window glass from being 
pushed out by air pressure if a door is closed.

 CAUTION: The windshield outside moulding (03144) must be installed before the 
urethane has hardened. 

 CAUTION: Use only Urethane (part of E0AZ-19562-A), or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSB-M2G316-B to service water and air leaks of the urethane 
sealant. 

 CAUTION: After replacing the urethane installed glass, the vehicle should not be 
driven until the urethane has cured. The curing time at temperatures above 13°
C (55°F) and relative humidity above 50% is 
12-24 hours (decreasing cure at higher temperatures and lower humidities). 
Refer to the detailed instructions provided by the manufacturer in the kit. 
Inadequate curing of the urethane may adversely affect the strength of the 
urethane bond. 

Place the quarter window glass into position and push in lightly to 
compress the urethane.

Clean any excess urethane from the quarter window glass and the pinch 
weld.

Install the quarter window glass center body pillar moulding by sliding 
the bottom into the plastic clip and gently pulling out the center to slide 
the quarter window glass center body pillar moulding into the top clip, being 
careful not to crimp or bend the quarter window glass center body pillar 
moulding. Push and secure the center plastic clip to hold down the quarter 
window glass center body pillar moulding.

Install the center body pillar inside upper finish panel.

Install the front safety belt guide bolt to the center body pillar. 
Tighten the front safety belt guide bolt to 38-78 Nm (28-57 
lb-ft).

Install the quarter trim panel.

Install the three push pins on the rear body pillar.

Install the rear safety belt guide bolt to the rear body pillar.Tighten 
the rear safety belt guide bolt to 38-78 Nm (28-57 lb-ft).

Install the five luggage compartment cover push pins.

Install the package tray upper trim panel support.

Install the three package tray upper trim panel support screws and the 
two push pins. 

Install the package tray panel.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Grid Wire, Back Window Glass

Breaks in the heated back window grid wires can be successfully 
repaired by using the following procedure:

Obtain the following service kit:

Service Kit Order Number 50-25-0584-0029

Marketing East Company

#10 Liberty Street

North Andover, MA 01845

Attn: Sales

Phone: (978) 689-9565

The service kit consists of five individual kits which include the 
following pieces:

One epoxy adhesive bi-pack

One application stick

One grid line mask

One set of instructions

 Surface Preparation 

 NOTE: A single break or any breaks that total 25mm (1 inch) in one grid 
cannot be repaired. The rear window must be replaced. For breaks totalling 
less than 25mm (1 inch) long, use the following procedure.

The vehicle should be brought inside and permitted to reach 16°
C (60°F) or above.

Clean the repair area with denatured alcohol.

 Mixing 

Ensure the repair material is not beyond the expiration date. If the 
hardener has crystallized, immerse packet in hot water until hardener liquifies.

Prepare the epoxy bi-pack:

Remove the separation clamp.

Thoroughly mix the resin and hardener together by kneading.

Cut a corner off the epoxy bi-pack.

 Application 

Place the grid line mask over the break in the grid line, aligning the 
cut out slots on either side of the repair area.

[FIGURE: N11755A.gif]

Apply the epoxy to the repair area using the application stick.

[FIGURE: N11756A.gif]

Carefully remove the mask without disturbing the epoxy.

Use Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent to heat the repair area 
for 1 to 2 minutes at a distance of about 25-50mm (1-2 inches). This procedure 
should heat the repair area to approximately 149°C (300°
F).

[FIGURE: N11757B.gif]

 Curing 

The heated back window may be energized immediately after the repair. 
Optimum hardness and adhesion will occur after 24 hours, and care should be 
taken not to disturb the repaired area until that time.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Lead Window Terminal Service

A bond separation of the bus bar terminal can be successfully repaired 
by using the following procedure:

Obtain the following service kit:

Service Kit Order Number 50-25-0584-0029

Marketing East Company

#10 Liberty Street

North Andover, MA 01845

Attn: Sales

Phone: (978) 689-9565

The service kit consists of five individual kits which include the 
following pieces:

One epoxy adhesive bi-pack

One application stick

One grid line mask

One set of instructions

The vehicle should be brought inside and permitted to reach 16°
C (60°F) or above.

Clean the repair area with denatured alcohol.

[FIGURE: N11758A.gif]

Ensure the repair material is not beyond the expiration date. If the 
hardener has crystallized, immerse packet in hot water until hardener liquifies.

Prepare the epoxy bi-pack:

Remove the separation clamp.

Thoroughly mix the resin and hardener together by kneading.

Cut a corner off the epoxy bi-pack.

Apply the epoxy to the repair area using the application stick.

Hold the pigtail terminal in place on the bus bar with an appropriate 
tool.

Use Rotunda Heat Gun 107-00300 or equivalent to heat the repair area 
for 1 to 2 minutes at a distance of about 25-50mm (1-2 inches). This procedure 
should heat the repair area to approximately 149°C (300°
F).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cigar Lighter and Ash Receptacle

The cigar lighter knob and element (15052) is located in the center 
accessory panel, below the radio chassis (18806), to the left of the 
instrument panel ash receptacle (04810).

[FIGURE: R9032A.gif]

The cigar lighter knob and element has a low-resistance heating coil 
which operates similarly to the coil in a portable heater. When the cigar 
lighter knob and element is pushed in, an electric circuit is completed and 
current flows through the cigar lighter knob and element coil to ground, 
generating heat in the coil. The cigar lighter knob and element is held in the 
closed-circuit position by the spring tension of retaining fingers. When the 
coil heat reaches a preset limit, the expansion of the heating coil overcomes 
the spring tension of the retaining fingers, and the cigar lighter knob and 
element pops out of the retaining fingers.

SERVICE PRECAUTIONS

Handling Air Bag Modules

 WARNING: SAFE HANDLING OF AIR BAG MODULES REQUIRES FOLLOWING THE PROCEDURES 
DESCRIBED BELOW FOR BOTH LIVE AND DEPLOYED AIR BAGS. 

LIVE AIR BAGS: 

ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHEN SERVICING AN AIR BAG VEHICLE, AND WHEN 
HANDLING AN AIR BAG.

WHEN CARRYING A LIVE AIR BAG, MAKE SURE THE BAG AND TRIM COVER ARE 
POINTED AWAY FROM YOUR BODY. IN THE UNLIKELY EVENT OF AN ACCIDENTAL 
DEPLOYMENT, THE BAG WILL THEN DEPLOY WITH MINIMAL CHANCE OF INJURY.

IN ADDITION, WHEN PLACING A LIVE AIR BAG ON A BENCH OR OTHER SURFACE, 
ALWAYS FACE THE BAG AND TRIM COVER UP, AWAY FROM THE SURFACE. THIS WILL REDUCE 
THE MOTION OF THE MODULE IF IT IS ACCIDENTALLY DEPLOYED.

DEPLOYED AIR BAGS: 

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS MUST ALSO BE OBSERVED WHEN HANDLING A DEPLOYED AIR 
BAG.

ALWAYS WEAR GLOVES AND SAFETY GLASSES WHEN HANDLING A DEPLOYED AIR BAG.

AFTER DEPLOYMENT, THE AIR BAG SURFACE MAY CONTAIN DEPOSITS OF SODIUM 
HYDROXIDE, A PRODUCT OF THE GAS GENERANT COMBUSTION THAT IS IRRITATING TO THE 
SKIN.

WASH YOUR HANDS WITH MILD SOAP AND WATER AFTERWARDS.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lock, Child Safety 

The child safety lock, when activated, prevents the rear door (24630) 
from being opened by the inside door handle (22600) regardless of the position 
of the door latch control rod knob (21850). The child safety lock has been 
designed into the door latch bellcrank levers and a decal has been placed 
above the child safety latch to indicate the location of the child safety 
latch. This latch is manually moved up to lock and down to unlock the system. 
Once the system is put into the locked position and the rear door is closed, 
the rear door can only be opened from the rear door outside handle (26604). 
The child safety lock does not lock the rear door from the outside; it is 
still necessary to push the door latch control rod knob down to lock the rear 
door from the outside.

Section 01-16: Wiper and Washer Systems

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wiper System, Windshield

The windshield wiper system includes:

Windshield window wiper pivot arms and blades

Windshield window wiper motors

Windshield window wiper/washer switch 

Windshield washer reservoir and windshield washer pump

Windshield washer nozzle jets and brackets.

The windshield wipers are operated by an electric windshield wiper 
motor (17508) mounted in the left rear corner of the engine compartment. The 
windshield wiper motor is attached to an access plate that in turn is attached 
to the bulkhead. To prevent metal-to-metal contact and the transmission of 
vibrations to the body, the windshield wiper motor is mounted on rubber 
insulators. 

The rotary motion of the windshield wiper motor is transferred to the 
windshield wiper pivot arms (17526) through windshield wiper mounting arm and 
pivot shafts (17566). The windshield wiper arm pivots extend through the cowl 
top panel and are held in position with windshield wiper pivot shaft cowl nuts 
(17481). The ends of the windshield wiper pivot shafts are serrated and 
cone-shaped to prevent the windshield wiper pivot arm from slipping on the 
windshield wiper pivot shaft. 

The windshield wiper pivot arms are installed on the windshield wiper 
pivot shafts and are held in position with windshield wiper pivot arm nuts. 
The ends of the windshield wiper pivot arms and the windshield wiper pivot arm 
nuts are concealed under the windshield wiper output arm cover (17C526). Slide 
clips attach the windshield wiper blade refills (17593) to the windshield 
wiper blade frames.

[FIGURE: GK2206A.gif]

 Off/Low/High Speed 

The windshield wipers operate with two speeds. Move the windshield 
wiper/washer to LO for slow wiping or to HI for faster wiping. To operate the 
windshield wipers the ignition switch (11572) must be in either the ON or ACC 
position.

 Interval 

Interval windshield wipers are optional on the vehicle. When the 
windshield wipers are in the interval mode (INT), the windshield wipers make 
single wipes. There is a 10-second pause between the wipes. In the interval 
mode, a slight ticking sound may be heard. This is normal and is caused by the 
interval relay.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Washer System, Windshield 

The windshield and rear window washer systems each consist of:

Washer reservoirs

Washer pumps

Washer nozzle jets and brackets

Hoses

The windshield wiper/washer switch is located on the windshield wiper 
control lever, an integral part of the multi-function switch (13K359). When 
the windshield wiper control lever is pulled toward the steering wheel (3600), 
washer fluid sprays on the windshield glass (03100). When it is released, 
spring pressure will return the windshield wiper control lever to its original 
position.

The windshield washer reservoir (17618) is mounted in the front corner 
of the left front fender (16005). A windshield washer pump (17664) is mounted 
on the windshield washer reservoir.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer concern by operating the wiper and washer system.

Visually inspect the components of the wiper and washer system.

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Binding windshield wiper pivot arms

Damaged windshield wiper motor

Damaged wiper switch

Wiper link improperly connected to windshield wiper motor

Low washer fluid level

Plugged or damaged hoses and/or windshield washer nozzle jet

Blown fuse:

20A WIPER

Loose or corroded connectors

Damaged windshield wiper motor or windshield washer pump

Damaged windshield wiper or washer switch

Check windshield wiper pivot arms for proper adjustment and proper 
connection to the motor shaft.

Check hoses for proper routing and connections.

Inspect the wiper or washer system wiring harnesses and connectors for 
obvious signs of damage.

If the fault is not visually evident, determine the symptom and proceed 
to the Symptom Chart.

PINPOINT TEST A: WINDSHIELD WASHER INOPERATIVE

 A1 CHECK WINDSHIELD WASHER PUMP 

Key OFF. 

Locate and disconnect the windshield washer pump

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Windshield Wiper 

 Mounting Arm and Pivot Shaft 

 Removal 

Remove the windshield wiper motor (17508). Refer to the procedure in 
this section. 

Remove the windshield wiper pivot arms (17526). Refer to the procedure 
in this section. 

Remove the windshield wiper pivot shaft mounting caps (17C582).

 NOTE: Hood shown removed for clarity.

[FIGURE: K20829B.gif]

Remove the windshield wiper pivot shaft cowl nuts (17481).

 NOTE: Hood shown removed for clarity.

[FIGURE: L5821C.gif]

Reach through the access opening to hold the windshield wiper mounting 
arm and pivot shafts (17566) in position.

Remove the windshield wiper pivot shaft mounting spacers (17514).

 NOTE: Hood shown removed for clarity.

[FIGURE: L6118E.gif]

Remove the windshield wiper mounting arm and pivot shafts through the 
access opening.

[FIGURE: L6124C.gif]

 Installation 

To install, reverse the removal procedure.

 Pivot Arm 

 Removal 

Remove the windshield wiper output arm cover (17C526).

[FIGURE: K20827A.gif]

Remove the windshield wiper pivot arm nut.

[FIGURE: K20828A.gif]

Carefully pry on the windshield wiper pivot arm to disengage it from 
the tapered splines on the windshield wiper pivot shaft. 

Remove the windshield wiper pivot arm.

 Installation 

Turn the ignition switch (11572) to the ON position. 

 NOTE: The on/off cycling of the windshield wiper motor will locate the 
windshield wiper mounting arm and pivot shaft in the park position. 

Turn the windshield wiper motor on. Allow it to cycle several times and 
turn it off.

Turn the ignition switch to the OFF position. 

Install the windshield wiper pivot arm onto the windshield wiper pivot 
shaft. 

Install the windshield wiper pivot arm nut. Tighten the windshield 
wiper pivot arm nut to 16-20 Nm (12-14 lb-ft). 

Check and, if necessary, adjust the park position. Refer to the 
procedure in this section.

Install the windshield wiper output arm cover.

 Wiper Blade 

 Removal 

Rotate the windshield wiper blade (17528) so it is perpendicular with 
the windshield wiper pivot arm. 

Use a screwdriver to press the tab to release the hooked end of the 
windshield wiper pivot arm from the windshield wiper blade holder.

[FIGURE: K20941B.gif]

Disengage the hooked end of the windshield wiper pivot arm by pulling 
down on the windshield wiper blade frame.

[FIGURE: K20942B.gif]

Separate the windshield wiper blade from the windshield wiper pivot arm.

 Installation 

To install, reverse the removal procedure. 

 Wiper Motor 

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301).

Disconnect the windshield wiper motor electrical connector.

Remove the two exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) solenoid vacuum valve 
bracket nuts and slide the intake manifold vacuum outlet fitting and cap 
(9A474) off of the access plate.

[FIGURE: K20858B.gif]

Remove the two access panel nuts.

[FIGURE: K20859B.gif]

Loosen the four windshield wiper motor bolts.

[FIGURE: K20860A.gif]

Pull the windshield wiper motor and the access panel away from the 
bulkhead.

Disengage the windshield wiper linkage pivot from the windshield wiper 
motor output arm.

[FIGURE: K20861B.gif]

Separate the windshield wiper motor from the access panel.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Ensure the ground wire is installed with the top left windshield wiper 
motor bolt.

To install, reverse the removal procedure.

Tighten the windshield wiper motor bolts to 7-10 Nm 
(62-88 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Washer Nozzle Jet and Bracket

 Removal 

 NOTE: The windshield washer nozzle jet and brackets (17603) are each held 
tightly against the sheet metal by a two-pronged spring clip that is part of 
the windshield washer nozzle jet and bracket. 

To remove a windshield washer nozzle jet and bracket, disconnect the 
hose (17543) and then the clip must be collapsed before it will pass through 
the hole in the sheet metal. In most cases, the clip will be damaged during 
removal. 

 Installation 

Ensure a replacement windshield washer nozzle jet and bracket is 
available before attempting to remove a windshield washer nozzle jet and 
bracket. Snap in the new windshield washer nozzle jet and bracket in the sheet 
metal so that the jet is aiming at the windshield glass (03100).

Section 01-18: Body Stripes (Tape) and Vinyl Films

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Body Stripes (Tape)

This section provides information on the dry and wet methods of tape 
striping.

Tape stripes are made from a tough, durable, weather-resistant, solid 
vinyl with a pressure-sensitive adhesive back. The pressure-sensitive adhesive 
back is protected by a liner paper which is easily peeled away during 
installation. During shipment and storage, the face is protected with an 
easy-release pre-mask paper.

================================================================================
PAGE 2075
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 01-18: Body Stripes (Tape) and Vinyl Films

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Tape Striping

 CAUTION: Be careful when using solvents because of possible damage to painted 
surfaces. To determine if a solvent is harmful to body paint, test it on a 
hidden area of the vehicle. 

 Dry Method Installation — Small or Thin Stripes 

 NOTE: Freshly painted surfaces must be thoroughly dry. Residual solvents in 
fresh paint may cause the tape stripe to blister.

Clean the painted surface (including wraparound flanges on door 
openings) with Extra Strength Tar and Road Oil Remover B7A-19520-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M5B106-A. Wipe the surface with a 
clean cloth and allow to dry.

Position the tape stripe to the vehicle and align the character lines 
and locators (if equipped) on the tape stripe to the contour of the vehicle. 
Use masking tape to tape the striping into place.

Remove the liner paper from the stripe one-half the distance of the 
panel and tear off the liner paper.

 NOTE: Use of hands or fingers to smooth on the striping will result in 
creases and air bubbles.

Stretch the striping in place but do not push the striping to the 
vehicle. Using a plastic squeegee, start from the center of the panel and 
press the striping in place, moving toward the end of the panel.

Peel off the remainder of the liner paper and press the striping into 
place using a plastic squeegee.

Remove the pre-mask by pulling it at a 180 degree angle away from the 
stripe. After removal, inspect the striping for bubbles. If necessary, remove 
the bubbles. Refer to the service procedure in this section.

Mold the decal into recessed areas using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or 
equivalent, and a soft, clean cloth.

 Wet Method Installation — Large Areas, Decal 

Mix 4.9ml (1 teaspoon) of liquid dishwashing detergent in 3.79L (1 
gallon) of water. Fill a spray bottle with the solution.

Remove the liner paper from the decal one-half the distance of the 
panel, and tear off the liner paper.

Wet the pressure-sensitive side of the decal and the area on the 
vehicle to be serviced with the detergent solution.

Position the decal on the vehicle and align character lines and 
locators (if equipped) on the decals to the contour of the vehicle.

Using the squeegee and firm overlapping pressure, begin from the center 
of the decal and squeegee toward the sides and then toward the front. The 
decal can be easily lifted and reapplied if air bubbles are present.

After the decal is completely in place and squeegeed, remove the 
pre-mask. Have an assistant help remove the pre-mask from large areas. Wetting 
the pre-mask on large decals may assist in removal.

Using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent, mold the decal into 
recessed areas and dry any moisture from the wrapped area with a soft, clean 
cloth.

PAGE 2076
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 01-18: Body Stripes (Tape) and Vinyl Films

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Body Stripes (Tape)

 CAUTION: Avoid using pointed or sharp tools as they may damage the painted 
surface. 

Service small nicks or scratches with touch-up paints mixed to blend 
with the affected area.

Service blisters or air bubbles by piercing them with a sharp needle or 
pin at one end of the bubble. Work the trapped air out through the pinhole by 
moving the thumb toward the pinhole and pressing the stripe firmly against the 
panel. It may be necessary to preheat the panel slightly to soften the 
adhesive. Heat may also be used to remove small wrinkles or irregularities.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Bumpers

The front bumper assembly is of a three-piece construction consisting 
of a:

Front bumper cover (17D957)

Front bumper cover support (17C947)

Front bumper (17757)

The rear bumper assembly is of a three-piece construction consisting of 
a:

Rear bumper cover (17K835)

Rear bumper cover support (17E855)

Rear bumper (17906)

The bumper covers are made of polypropylene plastic and are reinforced 
by energy absorbing foam bumper cover supports. The bumper covers and bumper 
cover supports are secured by plastic fasteners and bolts to reinforced steel 
bumpers. The steel bumpers are secured to a pair of bumper isolator and 
brackets (plus spacers for front bumper assemblies) that are secured to the 
body with nuts that attach to threaded studs on the bumper isolator and 
brackets (plus spacers for front bumper assemblies).

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Bumper 

 Front 

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: Place the front bumper assembly on a clean, covered working area to 
prevent scratching the front bumper cover (17D957).

If equipped, remove the two front license plate mounting bracket bolts 
and the front license plate mounting bracket (17A385).

[FIGURE: N11064B.gif]

Remove the four side marker lamp screws and the two side marker lamps.

[FIGURE: N11066C.gif]

Remove the seven front bumper cover bolts securing the front bumper 
cover to thefront bumper (17757).

Separate the front bumper, front bumper cover support (17C947) and the 
front bumper cover.

Remove the two front license plate mounting bracket reinforcement 
fasteners and the front license plate mounting bracket reinforcement.

Remove the four bumper isolator and bracket spacer nuts and remove the 
two bumper isolator and bracket spacers (17765).

 Assembly 

To assemble, reverse the disassembly procedure.

Tighten the two front license plate mounting bracket bolts to 0.98-1.20 Nm
 (9-10 lb-in).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Occupant Restraint System

 WARNING: ALL VEHICLE OCCUPANTS, INCLUDING PREGNANT WOMEN, SHOULD WEAR SAFETY 
BELTS FOR MAXIMUM PROTECTION IN THE EVENT OF AN ACCIDENT. ENSURE THAT THE LAP 
BELT IS FITTED SNUGLY AND AS LOW AS POSSIBLE AROUND THE HIPS, NOT AROUND THE 
WAIST. USE THE SHOULDER BELT ON THE OUTSIDE SHOULDER ONLY. NEVER WEAR THE 
SHOULDER BELT UNDER THE ARM OR SWING IT AROUND THE NECK OVER THE INSIDE 
SHOULDER. NEVER USE A SINGLE SAFETY BELT FOR MORE THAN ONE PERSON OR ACROSS 
MORE THAN ONE SEATING POSITION. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE PRECAUTIONS MAY 
INCREASE THE CHANCE AND/OR SEVERITY OF INJURY IN THE EVENT OF AN ACCIDENT. 
WHEN USING ANY INFANT OR CHILD RESTRAINT SYSTEM IT IS IMPORTANT TO FOLLOW THE 
INSTRUCTIONS PROVIDED BY THE MANUFACTURER CONCERNING ITS INSTALLATION AND USE. 
ACCORDING TO ACCIDENT STATISTICS, PROPERLY RESTRAINED CHILDREN ARE SAFER IN 
THE REAR SEAT THAN IN THE FRONT SEAT. CHILD RESTRAINT USE IS REQUIRED BY LAW. 

 WARNING: THE SAFETY BELT PROVIDES THE MAXIMUM PROTECTION WHEN THE SEAT BACK IS 
UPRIGHT AND THE OCCUPANT IS SITTING UPRIGHT IN THE SEAT. THE LAP BELT SHOULD 
FIT SNUGLY AND AS LOW AS POSSIBLE AROUND THE HIPS. THE SHOULDER BELT SHOULD BE 
WORN ON THE OUTSIDE SHOULDER ONLY AND FIT SNUG AGAINST THE CHEST. THE 
OCCUPANTS KNEES SHOULD BE STRAIGHT FORWARD. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE 
PRECAUTIONS MAY INCREASE THE CHANCE AND/OR SEVERITY OF INJURY IN THE EVENT OF 
AN ACCIDENT.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Belt, Lap/Shoulder — Front

The active restraints on the front seats are three-point safety belt 
systems. Manual fastening of the continuous safety belt employs both the lap 
and shoulder restraint. Safety belts should always be worn by the driver and 
passenger(s). The active restraint system of each seating position has:

Front safety belt buckle end (61202)

Safety belt tongue

Continuous safety belt webbing

Locking retractor mechanism

Safety belt guide

Anchor hardware

The safety belt system allows freedom of movement, locking only on hard 
braking, hard cornering, or impacts of approximately 8 km/h (5 mph) or more.

 CAUTION: Do not disassemble the buckles or the safety belt retractors. 

The safety belt retractors are an emergency locking retractor (ELR). 
When the vehicle slows suddenly during heavy braking, a small weight swings a 
locking pawl into position against teeth on the harness reel.

[FIGURE: R5362A.gif]

The front passenger seat combination lap/shoulder belt has an automatic 
locking retractor (ALR) mode for child seat installation. This mode is 
activated whenever all of the belt webbing is pulled out of the retractor. 
While in this mode, the belt will retract (tighten) but cannot be pulled back 
out to obtain more length. The automatic locking mode can be disengaged by 
unbuckling the belt and allowing the webbing to retract fully.

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Belt, Lap/Shoulder — Rear

The rear safety belts have a three-point design. Folding the rear seat 
forward allows service access for the rear safety belts.

The rear seat shoulder safety belt extends from a safety belt retractor 
mounted to the vehicle structure underneath the luggage compartment side cover 
(45422), up to a rear safety belt guide located on the rear body pillar. The 
safety belt is angled downward at the proper angle over the occupant's 
shoulder and chest to the lap belt buckle. The safety belt then continues 
through the safety belt tongue to the lower quarter panel anchorage on the 
outboard side which acts as a lap belt. 

[FIGURE: R6865C.gif]

The safety belt retractors are an emergency locking retractor (ELR). 
When the vehicle slows suddenly during heavy braking, a small weight swings a 
locking pawl into position against teeth on the harness reel.

[FIGURE: R5362A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not disassemble the buckles or the safety belt retractors. 

Always replace the safety belt assemblies in a matched set of a rear 
safety belt and buckle (60044) and a rear safety belt retractor and tongue 
(611B68), as received. The manufacturer's identification on the label of the 
retractor webbing must match the manufacturer's identification on the buckle 
base. Never interchange any part of a safety belt assembly between vehicle 
models. If any part of the safety belt assembly must be replaced, always 
replace the entire safety belt assembly. 

Always replace the entire safety belt assembly if the assembly has been 
subjected to loading by use during a collision.

The rear combination lap/shoulder belts have an automatic locking 
retractor (ALR) mode for child seat installation. This mode is activated 
whenever all of the belt webbing is pulled out of the retractor. While in this 
mode, the belt will retract (tighten) but cannot be pulled back out to obtain 
more length. The automatic locking mode can be disengaged by unbuckling the 
belt and allowing the webbing to retract fully.

 Safety Belt Extension Assembly 

A safety belt assembly that is too short when fully extended over the 
lap of a stocky vehicle occupant can be lengthened approximately 200mm (8 
inches) with a safety belt extension assembly which is available at no charge 
from Ford dealers. The safety belt extension assembly is only available with 
black webbing and standard buckle and must be of the same manufacture as the 
safety belt system to which it is attached.
