SERVICE PROCEDURES

Crankshaft Main or Connecting Rod Bearings — Fitting

 Plastigage Method 

Clean the crankshaft journals. Inspect the journals and thrust faces 
for nicks, burrs, or roughness that would cause premature bearing wear. 

Install the upper bearings to be checked. 

 NOTE: Do not rotate the crankshaft (6303) when measuring the oil clearances. 

Position the crankshaft into the cylinder blocks (6010). 

 NOTE: An unsupported crankshaft and counterweight will compress the 
Plastigage D81L-6002-B and cause an erroneous reading. 

If performed in-vehicle, leave at least two bearing caps installed at 
the proper torque specification of 54-59 Nm (40-43 lb-ft) to 
avoid false readings.

Position Plastigage D81L-6002-B or equivalent in the axial direction on 
a bearing that is properly installed in the appropriate main bearing cap.

Install the main bearing cap and tighten the main bearing cap bolts to 
54-59 Nm (40-43 lb-ft) in the order shown.

[FIGURE: A20654A.gif]

Remove the main bearing cap and measure the crankshaft main 
bearing-to-journal clearance. The clearance should be 0.018-0.036mm 
(0.0007-0.0014 inch). The limit is 0.10mm (0.0039 inch). If the clearance is 
over the limit, grind the crankshaft and install oversize bearings.

[FIGURE: A10959C.gif]

If measuring the connecting rod bearing-to-journal clearance, install 
the lower connecting rod bearing (6211) in the connecting rod cap. Position 
Plastigage in the axial direction on the connecting rod bearing. Install the 
connecting rod cap and the connecting rod nuts (6212). Tighten the connecting 
rod nuts to 15-17 Nm (11-13 lb-ft).

Remove the connecting rod caps and measure the connecting rod 
bearing-to-journal clearance. The clearance should be 0.024-0.042mm 
(0.0009-0.0017 inch). The limit is 0.10mm (0.0039 inch). If the clearance is 
over the limit, grind the crankshaft and install oversize bearings.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Crankshaft 

 Cleaning 

Clean the crankshaft (6303) with hot or cold commercial tank solutions, 
solvents and brushing, or by steam cleaning. Be sure to clean the drilled oil 
passages that connect the main and connecting journals.

 Inspection 

After cleaning, the crankshaft must be inspected to determine if it 
should be reused, reconditioned, or replaced.

If the crankshaft has been subjected to or will be subjected to 
high-stress operation, consider a magnetic inspection of the crankshaft for 
cracks that cannot be seen with the eye. This service is available through 
most automotive machine shops.

[FIGURE: A8475B.gif]

 Crankshaft Runout 

Support the crankshaft in V-blocks on the end main bearing journals. 
Set up Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to read on the 
center main bearing journal.

[FIGURE: A21552A.gif]

Be sure that the journal surfaces are smooth. Rotate the crankshaft one 
revolution. Note the maximum variation of the indicator reading. This is the 
runout of the crankshaft in the center or amount of bow. Consider out-of-round 
journals when measuring runout. Mark the crankshaft at its high or low reading 
position. Then support the crankshaft on the center and on one end journal. 
Repeat the above procedure, taking the reading on the unsupported end journal. 
Record this reading. 

Repeat the last set-up on the opposite end journal. 

Study the above readings and marks, to know if, where, and how much the 
crankshaft is bent. Most automotive machine shops are equipped to straighten 
crankshafts. 

Journal runout limit is 0.04mm (0.0016 inch) when inspected with a dial 
indicator with the crankshaft in V-blocks. 

 Crankshaft End Play 

Apply a liberal amount of clean engine oil to the crankshaft main 
bearing (6333), crankshaft thrust bearing, and main journals. 

Be sure that the bearings are in their proper position. Install the 
crankshaft and crankshaft main bearing caps and tighten the main bearing cap 
bolts to 54-59 Nm (40-43 lb-ft) in the order shown.

[FIGURE: A20654A.gif]

Install the Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent so 
the contact point rests against the crankshaft with the indicator axis 
parallel to the crankshaft axis.

Pry the crankshaft towards the rear of the engine (6007).

[FIGURE: A20655B.gif]

Zero the dial indicator.

Pry the crankshaft forward and note the reading on the dial.

The crankshaft end play should be 0.080-0.282mm (0.0031-0.0111 inch). 
If the end play exceeds 0.30mm (0.012 inch), grind the crankshaft and install 
an oversize crankshaft thrust bearing or replace the crankshaft and crankshaft 
thrust bearing. 

 Crankshaft Main Journal and Connecting Rod Journals 

Measure the main and connecting rod journals. Measure the journals in 
eight locations. Write down the figures on a sketch to give a profile of each 
journal.

[FIGURE: A8472A.gif]

A study of the readings will tell if the crankshaft is usable as is, if 
it must be reground, or if it must be replaced. 

The main bearing journal diameter specification is 49.938-49.956mm 
(1.9661-1.9668 inches). 

The connecting rod journal diameter specification is 39.940-39.956mm 
(1.5742-1.5731 inches). 

The main and connecting rod journal out-of-round limit is 0.05mm (0.002 
inch). 

 Journals, Refinishing 

 CAUTION: Failure to maintain the original fillet radius at the line where the 
journal meets the counterweight of the crankshaft can result in crankshaft 
damage. 

Crankshaft grinding is necessary to straighten and restore journals to 
a round condition. Crankshaft grinding should be done only by experienced 
professionals.

[FIGURE: A8951A.gif]

The grinding limit is 0.75mm (0.030 inch). Undersize bearings are 
available in 0.25mm (0.010 inch), 0.50mm (0.020 inch) and 0.75mm (0.030 inch) 
sizes. The fillet radius must be maintained at 3mm (0.12 inch). 

Also be sure the crankshaft is polished and recleaned (especially the 
oil passages) after grinding it and before installing it in the engine. 

 Crankshaft Sprocket 

Inspect the crankshaft sprocket (6306) for warping, chipping, or 
abnormal wear. Inspect the crankshaft sprocket teeth for wear, deformation, 
chipping, or other damage. If necessary, replace the crankshaft sprocket as 
explained in Section 03-01 .

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Pistons, Piston Pins and Piston Rings 

 Cleaning 

Clean the ring grooves with Piston Ring Groove Cleaner D81L-6002-D or 
equivalent. Do not cut into the piston metal. 

[FIGURE: A21820A.gif]

Carbon may be cleaned from the top of the piston (6108) with a wire 
brush or wheel. Do not use a wire wheel on the piston ring grooves or lands. 
Clean the oil drain holes in the oil ring grooves. Do not drill additional oil 
drain holes. Clean the remainder of the piston with solvent and a brush. Do 
not use a caustic (lye base) or acid cleaning solution. 

 Inspection 

Inspect the piston for scores, cracks, excessively worn piston pin 
bores, pitted or eroded dome, worn piston ring grooves, and piston skirt 
diameter. 

Carefully inspect the pistons for fractures at the ring lands, skirts, 
and pin bosses. Check for scuffed, rough, or scored skirts. If the lower inner 
portion of the ring grooves have high steps, replace the piston. This step 
will interfere with piston ring operation and cause excessive piston ring side 
clearance.

Spongy, eroded areas near the top of the piston are usually caused by 
detonation or premature ignition. A shiny thrust surface, offset from the 
centerline between the piston pin holes, can be caused by a bent connecting 
rod (6200). Replace pistons showing signs of excessive wear, irregular or 
fractured ring lands, or damage from detonation and premature ignition.

Inspect the outer circumferences of all pistons for seizure or scoring. 
Replace the piston if damaged.

 Pistons — Fitting

 Piston-to-Cylinder Clearance 

The piston-to-cylinder wall clearance limit is 0.15mm (0.006 inch). 
Oversize pistons and piston rings are available in 0.25mm (0.10 inch) and 
0.50mm (0.020 inch) sizes.

[FIGURE: A20660A.gif]

 Piston Rings — Fitting 

Install an oil ring spacer in the bottom ring groove of the piston. The 
ends of the oil ring spacer must butt one another and not overlap. 

Start the end of an oil ring into the oil ring groove above the spacer. 
The end gap must be approximately 25mm (1 inch) away from the spacer ends. 
Finish installing the oil ring by spiraling it on the remainder of the way. 
Repeat the oil ring installation with the other oil rail. Its gap must be 
approximately 25mm (1 inch) on the other side of the spacer ends. 

Stagger the ring end gaps so that no ring gap is aligned with either 
the spacer gap or the other ring gap.

[FIGURE: A20658A.gif]

 Piston and Piston Pin Fit 

The piston pin-to-piston clearance should be 0.0076-0.0127mm 
(0.0003-0.0005 inch). The connecting rod should fall by its own weight when 
held horizontally by the piston.

[FIGURE: A10500C.gif]

 Piston Pin-to-Piston Clearance 

Inspect the pin-to-piston clearance. The standard pin-to-piston 
clearance is 0.0076-0.0127mm (0.0003-0.0005 inch). If the clearance exceeds 
the specification, replace the piston.

 Piston Outer Diameter 

 NOTE: Measure the piston outer diameter at a right angle (90 degrees) to the 
piston pin and below the oil ring groove. 

Measure the outer diameter of each piston, and ensure the clearance 
between the piston and cylinder bore is correct.

[FIGURE: A8963C.gif]

Standard size piston diameter is 70.954-70.974mm (2.793-2.794 inches). 

 Piston Rings 

Inspect the piston rings for abnormal wear or damage. Replace if 
necessary. 

 Piston Ring-to-Groove Clearance 

Measure the ring-to-groove clearances. The top and second ring 
clearance is 0.03-0.065mm (0.001-0.003 inch). The limit is 0.15mm (0.006 inch).

[FIGURE: A10502C.gif]

 Piston Pin Hole Diameter 

The piston pin hole diameter is 13.309mm (0.524 inch).

 Piston Pin Diameter 

The piston pin outside diameter is 19.980mm (0.7866 inch).

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Connecting Rods

 Piston Pin Clearance 

An interference fit of 0.00-0.26mm (0.0000-0.0102 inch) should exist 
between the piston pin outer diameter (OD) and the connecting rod inner 
diameter (ID).

 Cleaning 

Connecting rods (6200) may be cleaned in hot or cold commercial 
tank-type cleaners. They may also be cleaned with automotive parts cleaning 
solvents or steam cleaned.

 Inspection 

The connecting rod should be carefully inspected for conformance to 
specifications. Various forms of engine wear can be readily identified as 
follows:

A shiny surface on the pin boss side of the piston (6108) usually 
indicates that a connecting rod is bent or a piston pin hole is not in proper 
relation to the piston skirt and ring grooves.

Abnormal connecting rod bearing wear can be caused by either a bent 
connecting rod, an improperly machined journal, or a tapered connecting rod 
bore.

Twisted connecting rods will not create an easily identifiable wear 
pattern. Badly twisted connecting rods will disturb the entire action of the 
piston, pin and piston ring, and connecting rod assembly and may be the cause 
of excessive oil consumption. 

 NOTE: It is not necessary to ream or hone the pin bore in the connecting rod 
bearing (6211). Replace any damaged connecting rod nuts and bolts. Check the 
connecting rod for bends or twists on a suitable alignment fixture. Follow the 
manufacturer's instructions for the specific alignment fixture being used. If 
the bend and/or twist exceeds the specifications, the connecting rod must be 
replaced.

Inspect the connecting rods for signs of fractures and the bearing 
bores for out-of-round and taper. If the bore exceeds the recommended limits 
and/or if the connecting rod is fractured, it should be replaced. Measure the 
diameter of the connecting rod piston pin bore.

Assemble the piston, piston pin, and connecting rod following the 
procedures outlined.

 Connecting Rod Bending Clearance 

The connecting rods should be inspected for proper piston pin bore 
diameter, crankshaft bearing bore diameter, length, bend, and twist.

[FIGURE: A10503C.gif]

Use a bending fixture and a feeler gauge to inspect the connecting rod 
bending clearance.

The bend limit is 0.04mm (0.0016 inch) per 100mm (3.94 inches).The 
twist limit is 0.04mm (0.0016 inch) per 100mm (3.94 inches).

[FIGURE: A10504C.gif]

Camshaft and Cylinder Head Journals

 Cleaning 

The camshaft (6250) may be cleaned by tank cleaning, solvents, or by 
steam cleaning.

Remove light scuffs, scores, or nicks from the camshaft machined 
surfaces with a smooth oil stone. Clean the camshaft in solvent and wipe it dry.

 Inspection 

Perform the following inspections.

 Camshaft Runout 

Check the camshaft runout with Dial Indicator with Bracketry 
TOOL-4201-C or equivalent. The limit at the center journal is 0.03mm (0.0012 
inch).

[FIGURE: A10515D.gif]

Item

 Cam Lobes 

Inspect the camshaft lobes for scoring and signs of abnormal wear. Lobe 
pitting, except in the general area of the lobe toe, is not detrimental to the 
operation of the camshaft. Do not replace the camshaft unless the lobe lift 
loss has exceeded specification or pitting has occurred in the lobe lift area.

 Cam Lobe Heights 

Inspect the camshaft lobe heights at the points shown. 

[FIGURE: A20662A.gif]

The standard intake lobe height is 36.124mm (1.4222 inches). The 
minimum height is 35.624mm (1.4025 inches).

The standard exhaust lobe height is 36.404mm (1.4332 inches). The 
minimum height is 35.904mm (1.4135 inches).

 Camshaft Journal Oil Clearance 

Measure the camshaft bores in the cylinder head (6049). 

[FIGURE: A10520A.gif]

The front and rear camshaft bore diameter should be 43.495-43.525mm 
(1.7124-1.7135 inch). 

The center camshaft bore diameter should be 43.500-43.525mm 
(1.7126-1.7135 inch).

Measure the journal diameters. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Subtract the camshaft bearing journal outer diameter from the cylinder 
bore inner diameter to obtain the oil clearance.

The front and rear bearing bore oil clearance specification is 
0.035-0.085mm (0.0014-0.0033 inch). 

The center bearing oil clearance is 0.065-0.115mm (0.0026-0.0045 inch). 

The limit is 0.15mm (0.0059 inch). 

If the oil clearance exceeds the limit, replace the cylinder head and 
camshaft.

 Camshaft Journal Diameters 

Measure the bearing journals. Standard diameter of the front and rear 
journals is 43.440-43.465mm (1.7103-1.7112 inches). The center journal is 
43.410-43.435mm (1.7079-1.7100 inches).

[FIGURE: A10514C.gif]

The out-of-round limit on all journals is 0.05mm (0.002 inch). 

The front oil seal contact surface is 29.961-30.000mm (1.1796-1.1811 
inches). 

 Camshaft End Play 

 NOTE: Measure the camshaft end play with the camshaft thrust plate (6269) in 
position. 

Install Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent, so the 
contact point rests against the end of the camshaft with the indicator axis 
parallel to the camshaft axis.

Pry the camshaft towards the rear of the cylinder head.

[FIGURE: A10516A.gif]

Zero the dial indicator.

Pry the camshaft forward and note the reading on the dial indicator.

Standard end play is 0.05-0.18mm (0.002-0.007 inch) with a limit of 
0.20mm (0.008 inch). If the end play exceeds the limit, replace the camshaft 
thrust plate or the camshaft.

 Camshaft Sprocket 

Inspect the camshaft sprocket (6256) for warping or abnormal wear. 
Inspect the camshaft sprocket teeth for wear, deformation, chipping, or other 
damage. If damaged, replace the camshaft sprocket. Refer to Section 03-01 for 
the removal and installation procedure.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Oil Pump

 Cleaning 

Wash all parts in a solvent and dry them thoroughly with compressed 
air. Use a brush to clean the inside of the oil pump housing and the relief 
valve chamber. Ensure all dirt and metal particles are removed.

 Inspection 

Perform the following inspections. 

 Tooth Tip Clearance 

Use a feeler gauge to inspect the tooth tip clearance. 

Measure the inner gear tip to outer gear tip clearance. The clearance 
should be 0.198mm (0.0078 inch) maximum. 

[FIGURE: A20692A.gif]

 Outer Rotor-to-Pump Body Clearance 

Inspect the oil pump body for scoring in the outer gear bore. Disregard 
light scoring. Measure the body (housing) to outer gear clearance with a 
feeler gauge. The outer race-to-housing clearance should be no more than 
0.22mm (0.0087 inch). 

[FIGURE: A20667A.gif]

 Inner Rotor Side Clearance 

Use a feeler gauge and Straight Edge D83L-4201-C or equivalent, to 
measure the inner rotor side clearance. 

[FIGURE: A10525D.gif]

The limit is 0.14mm (0.0055 inch). 

If the above clearance is out of limits, replace the oil pump (6600). 
Clean the relief valve and check for scores, burrs, or sticking. Replace the 
oil pump as necessary.

 Outer Rotor Side Clearance 

Use a feeler gauge and Straight Edge D83L-4201-C or equivalent, to 
measure the outer rotor side clearance. 

[FIGURE: A10525D.gif]

The limit is 0.14mm (0.0055 inch). 

If the above clearance is out of limits, replace the oil pump. Clean 
the relief valve and check for scores, burrs, or sticking. Replace the oil 
pump as necessary.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Oil Pan

 Cleaning 

Scrape any dirt or metal particles from the inside of the oil pan 
(6675). Scrape all old oil pan gasket material from the gasket surface. Wash 
the oil pan in a solvent and dry it thoroughly. Ensure all foreign particles 
are removed.

 Inspection 

Check the oil pan for cracks, holes, or damaged oil pan drain plug 
threads. Check the gasket surface for damage caused by over-tightened oil pan 
bolts. Replace the oil pan if damaged.

[FIGURE: A11660F.gif]

 Cleaning 

The cylinder head (6049) may be cleaned with commercial hot or cold 
tank-type cleaners, with automotive parts cleaning solvents, or by steam 
cleaning. Clean the intake and exhaust ports with a small wire wheel and a 
drill motor. Be careful not to allow the drill chuck to contact the valve 
seats. Remove all gasket material from the valve cover gasket surface, head 
gasket surface, the exhaust and intake manifold surfaces, and the water outlet 
connection surface. 

Use a valve guide cleaning tool and a small bristle brush to clean the 
valve guide bores. 

Clean the cylinder head oil passages. 

Clean the deposits from the intake valves (6507) and exhaust valves 
(6505) with a wire wheel. 

 CAUTION: If the valve springs (6513) are painted, do not use a wire brush or 
paint remover to clean them. They could rust, become pitted, and break. 

Remove deposits from the valve springs and valve spring retainers (6514).

 Inspection 

Inspect the cylinder head for cracks in valve seats and ports, at 
coolant passage holes, and between combustion chambers. 

 Spark Plug Thread Service 

Damaged spark plug threads in the cylinder head can be serviced using 
Rotunda Metric Thread Repair Set Kit 107-R0902 or equivalent. 

The procedure involves cutting new threads in the spark plug hole. 
After the rethreading operation, a tapered sleeve will be installed in the 
cylinder head. The sleeve is threaded on the inside and outside. The outside 
threads screw into the cylinder head while the inside threads are for the 
spark plug (12405). 

This thread service is permanent and will have no affect on cylinder 
head or spark plug life. 

 CAUTION: Do not use power or air-driven tools to install the inserts. 

 CAUTION: The cylinder head must be removed from the engine (6007) before 
installing an insert. The service procedure includes a thread cutting process 
which produces metal chips. Performing this procedure while the cylinder head 
is on the engine will cause metal chips to fall into the cylinder. Once in the 
cylinder, these chips can damage the cylinder wall when the engine is started. 

Thoroughly clean the spark plug counterbore, seat, and threads of all 
dirt or other foreign material. 

Start the tap into the spark plug hole, being careful to keep it 
properly aligned. As the tap begins cutting the new threads, apply aluminum 
cutting oil to the tap. 

Continue cutting threads and applying oil until the stop ring bottoms 
against the spark plug seat. 

Remove the tap. Remove all metal chips using compressed air. 

Coat the threads of the mandrel with cutting oil. Thread the insert 
onto the mandrel until one thread of mandrel extends beyond the insert. 

[FIGURE: A20669B.gif]

 NOTE: A properly installed insert will be flush to one millimeter below spark 
plug gasket seat. 

Thread the insert into the tapped spark plug hole using a torque 
wrench. Continue tightening the mandrel until the torque wrench indicates 61 Nm
 (45 lb-ft). 

To loosen the mandrel for removal, hold the mandrel stationary and turn 
the mandrel body approximately one-half turn. Remove the mandrel. 

 Cylinder Head Flatness 

Check the cylinder head for flatness on the head gasket surface. The 
cylinder head must be within 0.15mm (0.006 inch) over the entire cylinder head 
gasket surface.

[FIGURE: A10507A.gif]

 Valve Seat Runout 

Before installing the intake valves and exhaust valves into the 
cylinder head, check the valve seat runout.

The seat face runout should not exceed 0.0406mm (0.0016 inch).

 Valve Stem-to-Valve Guide Clearance 

Check the valve stem-to-valve guide clearance of each valve in its 
respective valve guide with Valve Stem Clearance Tool TOOL-6505-E and Dial 
Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent. Use a flat-end indicator 
point.

[FIGURE: A9337C.gif]

Install the tool on the valve stem until the lip is fully seated, and 
tighten the knurled set screw firmly. Permit the valve to drop away from its 
seat until the tool contacts the upper surface of the valve guide. 

Position the dial indicator on the cylinder head. Move the valve back 
and forth 90 degrees from the dial indicator shaft. Divide the measurement by 
two to determine the actual guide clearance.

The intake clearance is 0.025-0.060mm (0.0010-0.0024 inches). The 
exhaust clearance is 0.030-0.065mm (0.0012-0.0026 inches).

The maximum stem-to-valve guide clearance is 0.20mm (0.008 inch).

If the clearance exceeds specification, replace the valve and/or valve 
guide.

 Valve Seats, Refacing 

Cylinder head valve seats must be round, have the correct seat angle, 
face width, and be free of pits or burned areas. 

The valve seat angle is 45 degrees. The valve seat face width is 
1.1-1.7mm (0.043-0.067 inch).

[FIGURE: A21618B.gif]

If necessary, grind the valve seats to a 45 degree angle. Follow the 
instructions of the seat grinding equipment manufacturer. Be sure to use a 
tight fitting, straight pilot in the valve guide. Do not remove more metal 
than necessary to clean the valve seat. 

After grinding the valve seats, check the valve seat wear. This 
dimension will affect valve spring-load (pressure). With the valve on the 
seat, measure the distance from the lower spring seat surface on the cylinder 
to the end of the valve stem. Use the following specifications to determine if 
replacement is necessary:

[FIGURE: A10519A.gif]

If the dimension is 38.6-39.1mm (1.520-1.539 inches), then use valve 
and seat as is. 

If dimension is 39.2-40.1mm (1.539-1.579 inches), then insert a spring 
seat shim of between 0.25mm (0.010 inch) and 1.5mm (0.060 inch) between the 
valve spring and the cylinder head. 

If dimension is more than 40.1mm (1.579 inches), replace the cylinder 
head or valve seat. The valve seats must be replaced by a qualified machine 
shop facility.

 Valves 

Perform the following valve inspections and service procedures as needed.

 Valves, Inspection 

Inspect each valve for damaged or bent stems, a rough or damaged face, 
and damaged or unevenly worn stem tips.

 Valves, Refacing 

If necessary, reface the valves to a 45 degree angle following the 
valve grinding equipment manufacturer's recommendations. Remove as much stock 
from the end of the valve stem as the total removed from the valve seat and 
valve face. Bevel the edge of the valve stem end after grinding the end of the 
valve stem.

[FIGURE: A21571A.gif]

 Valve Seat Contact Width 

The center of the valve face should contact the valve seat in 
approximately the center.

Lower the valve seat as required with a 15 degree or 30 degree stone 
valve seat cut. If contact is correct but the valve seat is too wide, trim the 
bottom of the valve seat with a 60 degree or 70 degree stone. After grinding, 
the valve seat will almost always be too wide, so some narrowing is usually 
necessary. 

The final valve seat width should be 1.1-1.7mm (0.043-0.067 inch). 

[FIGURE: A20673A.gif]

 Valve Guide Height 

Measure the height of each valve guide (6510).

[FIGURE: A21688B.gif]

The height of each valve guide should be within 13.2-13.8mm 
(0.520-0.543 inch). The valve guide height limit is 13-14mm (0.518-0.5512 
inches).

 Valve Guide Inner Diameter 

Inspect the valve guide bores for proper size. A telescoping gauge and 
a 25.4mm (1 inch) micrometer should be used.The intake and exhaust guide bores 
should be 7.01-7.03mm (0.276-0.277 inch). Intake and exhaust valve 
stem-to-guide service limit clearance is 0.20mm (0.008 inch).

[FIGURE: A10508C.gif]

 Valve Stem Diameter 

Measure the valve stem diameters. The intake valve stems are 
6.970-6.985mm (0.2744-0.2750 inch) and the exhaust valve stems are 6.965 to 
6.980mm (0.2742 to 0.2748 inch). 

[FIGURE: A10509A.gif]

If the clearance is greater than specified, replace the valve or valve 
guide, or both, depending on the dimension that is causing the excess clearance.

 Valve Head Margin Thickness 

Inspect the valve head margin thickness of each valve. 

[FIGURE: A20672A.gif]

The exhaust valve head margin thickness is 1.0mm (0.039 inch). 

The intake valve head margin thickness is 1.30mm (0.051 inch).

 Valve Spring Length Inspection 

Measure the free length of the valve spring. The limit is 43.6mm (1.717 
inches).

[FIGURE: A21817A.gif]

 Valve Spring Squareness 

Check the valve springs for squareness. The maximum out-of-square is 
1.5mm (0.059 inch).

[FIGURE: A10512B.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine

The 1.3L engine is an in-line four cylinder gasoline engine. The engine 
employs a 9.7:1 compression ratio to help supply better fuel economy and 
performance. The cylinder head (6049) is a single overhead camshaft design 
that utilizes hydraulic lash adjusters (HLA) (6C501) to reduce engine noise 
and eliminate periodic adjustment.

Engine intake air flows through the throttle body (9E926) into the 
intake manifold (9424). To enhance efficiency, tuned ports are used to channel 
the air into the aluminum cylinder head. Fuel is supplied to the cylinders 
through the use of sequential multiport fuel injection (SFI).

The cylinder blocks (6010) is cast-iron with five crankshaft main 
bearings (6333) supporting the crankshaft (6303). The crankshaft front seal 
(6700) and crankshaft rear oil seals (6701) are a one-piece design. Piston 
pins are pressed into the small end of the connecting rod (6200) and float in 
the piston (6108). The large end of the connecting rod has replaceable insert 
bearings. Grooves at the connecting rod and cap parting face provide oil to 
lubricate the cylinder walls and cool the pistons. 

Pressurized oil is supplied by an oil pump (6600) that is driven by the 
crankshaft . The oil pump draws oil from the oil pan (6675). The oil is routed 
through the oil pump screen cover and tube (6622), oil pump, oil filter (6731), 
crankshaft main bearings and connecting rod bearings (6211), to the camshaft 
bearings and rocker arms (6564).

================================================================================

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Identification

The U.S. Motor Vehicle Theft Law Enforcement Act of 1984 requires 
identification of certain high theft vehicles to reduce the National Auto 
Theft Rate. This federal law requires Ford Motor Company to affix the vehicle 
identification number (VIN) on specific parts. In addition, the service 
replacement parts must also be identified as service parts. These components 
are: 

Bumpers.

 Front fenders (16005).

Hood (16612).

Front and rear doors.

Quarter panels.

Liftgate.

Engine (6007).

Transaxle.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Induction System

The air/fuel mixture necessary for proper combustion in the cylinders 
is provided by the sequential multiport fuel injection (SFI) system. Refer to 
 Section 03-04 for description and operation of the SFI system.

Fuel is supplied from the fuel tank (9002) by a high-pressure fuel pump 
mounted in the fuel tank. The fuel is sent from the fuel pump (9350), through 
an in-line fuel filter (9155), to the fuel injection supply manifold (9D280). 
The fuel is sent from the fuel injection supply manifold to the individual 
fuel injectors (9F593) and then through the fuel pressure regulator (9C968). 
Any amount of fuel in excess of demand, supplied to the fuel injection supply 
manifold is returned by the fuel pressure regulator to the fuel tank through 
the fuel tube hose (9324).

PAGE 2188
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 03-01: Engine

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Crankshaft

The crankshaft (6303) is positioned on the bottom of the cylinder 
blocks (6010). The crankshaft is supported by five two-bolt main bearing caps, 
the crankshaft main bearings (6333), and the crankshaft thrust bearings. The 
crankshaft thrust bearings are located with the No.4 crankshaft main bearings. 
The crankshaft thrust bearings limit the crankshaft end play and absorb thrust 
loads applied to the crankshaft ends. A camshaft sprocket (6256), a timing 
chain/belt (6268) and a crankshaft sprocket (6306) connect the crankshaft to 
the camshaft (6250).

================================================================================
PAGE 2189
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 03-01: Engine

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Camshaft

The camshaft (6250) is installed in the cylinder head (6049) and is 
supported by five main journals. The distributor (12127) is directly driven 
from the end of the camshaft. The camshaft sprocket (6256), which is located 
at the front of the camshaft, a timing chain/belt (6268), and a crankshaft 
sprocket (6306) connect the camshaft to the crankshaft (6303).

================================================================================

Section 03-01: Engine

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Valve Train

Hydraulic lash adjusters (HLA) (6C501) provide automatic lash 
adjustment. The HLAs ride between the rocker arms (6564) and the top of the 
valve stems. Any clearance between the rocker arms and the valve stems is 
taken up by the hydraulic expansion of each HLA. The HLAs are designed to 
maintain 0mm (0 inch) clearance between the rocker arms and the valve stems.

Positive Crankcase Ventilation System

The 1.3L engine is equipped with a closed-type positive crankcase 
ventilation system which recycles the crankcase vapors to the intake manifold 
(9424). Refer to Section 03-08 for additional engine emission information.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Lubrication System

The engine oil lubrication system and the lubrication components are 
designed for lubrication efficiency and engine noise reduction. The oil pump 
(6600) is crankshaft-driven and draws the oil from the oil pan (6675) through 
the oil pump screen cover and tube (6622). The oil pump then sends the oil to 
the oil filter (6731), where it is directed to the crankshaft main bearings, 
connecting rod bearings, camshaft bearings and rocker arms (6564). The oil 
then drains, back into the oil pan. 

 Engine Lubrication System 

[FIGURE: A10443B.gif]

 Oil Pump 

The oil pump is bolted to the front of the cylinder blocks (6010) and 
is crankshaft driven. A full-flow oil filter is mounted to the cylinder 
blocks. Under normal operating conditions, all of the engine oil will pass 
through the oil filter. If this oil filter becomes clogged or blocked, the oil 
will be routed through a bypass valve, directly to the engine (6007).

 Oil Pan 

Theoil pan is bolted to the bottom of the cylinder blocks. Engine oil 
is pulled up from the oil pan through the oil pump screen cover and tube and 
delivered to the oil pump where it is then circulated through the other various 
engine components.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Cooling System

 WARNING: TO AVOID THE POSSIBILITY OF PERSONAL INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE, 
DO NOT OPERATE THE ENGINE WITH THE HOOD OPEN UNTIL THE FAN BLADE HAS BEEN 
FIRST EXAMINED FOR POSSIBLE CRACKS AND SEPARATION. 

 WARNING: THE ELECTRIC COOLING FAN WILL OPERATE WHENEVER THE KEY IS ON AND THE 
COOLANT IS HOT (ABOVE 97°C [207°
F]), EVEN THOUGH THE ENGINE MAY NOT BE RUNNING. AVOID 
PLACING HANDS, CLOTHING, TOOLS, OR OTHER OBJECTS IN THE FAN BLADES AT ANY 
TIME. THE FAN BLADE WILL ALSO OPERATE IF THE ENGINE COOLANT TEMPERATURE (ECT) 
SENSOR IS DISCONNECTED. 

Engine cooling is provided by a water pump (8501) mounted on the front 
end of the cylinder blocks (6010). A water thermostat (8575) controls coolant 
temperature and is located in the water hose connection (8592) at the 
transaxle end of the cylinder head (6049). 

An engine cooling fan motor (8K621) is mounted on the rear side of the 
radiator (8005). The engine cooling fan motor is controlled by the engine 
coolant temperature (ECT) sensor.

Drive Belt System

The generator (GEN) (10346) is driven by a drive belt (8620) that also 
drives the water pump (8501). If the vehicle is equipped with air conditioning 
and power steering, the A/C compressor (19703) and power steering pump (3A674) 
are driven by a multi-groove drive belt.

The generator drive belt is adjusted using the generator bolt and the 
generator adjustment bolt. The A/C compressor/power steering pump drive belt 
is adjusted through either the power steering pump or a separately mounted 
idler pulley.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Rocker Arms and Rocker Arm Shafts

 Removal 

Remove the valve cover (6582).

Remove the 10 rocker arm bolts and rocker arm seats (6A528) in the 
sequence shown.

[FIGURE: A21657A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17975B.gif]

Remove the rocker arm and shaft assemblies.

 NOTE: Mark rocker arms (6564) and rocker arm spacers so that they can be 
installed in the exact place from which they were removed. 

Remove the rocker arms and the rocker arm spacers from the rocker arm 
shafts (6563).

[FIGURE: A20686A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: The intake and exhaust rocker arm shafts are identified by the larger 
dimension of distance A compared to distance B in the illustration below.

Assemble the rocker arm spacers and rocker arms to obtain the proper 
arrangement for the rocker arm shaft assemblies. 

[FIGURE: A21655B.gif]

Install the 10 rocker arm bolts and rocker arm seats. Tighten the 
rocker arm bolts to 22-28 Nm (16-21 lb-ft) in the sequence 
shown.

[FIGURE: A10523D.gif]

Install the valve cover. Install the six valve cover bolts and tighten 
to 5-9 Nm (44-80 lb-in).

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Valve Spring, Valve Spring Retainer and Valve Stem Seal

 NOTE: If the valve or valve seat has not been damaged, valve springs (6513) 
and valve stem seals (6571) may be replaced by holding the affected valve 
against its seat using compressed air. Use a compressed air line and an 
adapter installed in a spark plug hole. A minimum of 965 kPa (140 psi) line 
pressure is required. If air pressure does not hold the valve shut, the valve 
is damaged or burnt and the cylinder head (6049) must be removed and serviced. 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Seal Replacer

T87C-6510-B

Valve Spring Compressor

T81P-6513-A

Valve Spring Compressor Set

T87C-6565-A

 Removal 

Remove the valve cover (6582). 

Remove the rocker arm shafts (6563). Refer to the removal procedure in 
this section.

 NOTE: The appropriate piston must be at top dead center (TDC) to prevent the 
valves from falling down into the cylinder.

Turn the crankshaft (6303) until the piston (6108) of the cylinder to 
be worked on is at the TDC.

Remove the appropriate spark plug (12405) and install a pressurized air 
line fitted with the proper adapter. Apply a minimum of 965 kPa (140 psi) of 
compressed air.

Use Valve Spring Compressor T81P-6513-A and Valve Spring Compressor Set 
T87C-6565-A to compress the valve spring and remove the valve spring retainers 
(6514).

[FIGURE: A10958E.gif]

Remove the upper valve spring retainer, valve spring and the lower 
valve spring retainer.

[FIGURE: A11664D.gif]

 NOTE: If air pressure has forced the piston to the bottom of the cylinder, 
any loss of air pressure will allow the valves to fall into the cylinder. A 
rubber band, tape, or string wrapped around the end of the valve stem will 
prevent this condition and will still allow enough travel to check the valve 
for binds. 

Remove the valve stem seal. 

[FIGURE: A11665B.gif]

 Installation 

Install a new valve stem seal using Valve Seal Replacer T87C-6510-B.

[FIGURE: A10950D.gif]

[FIGURE: A10951E.gif]

Install the lower valve spring retainers, valve spring, and upper valve 
spring retainers.

Use Valve Spring Compressor T81P-6513-A and Valve Spring Compressor Set 
T87C-6565-A to compress the valve spring and install the valve spring retainer 
key (6518). 

Turn off the compressed air. Remove the air line and adapter and 
install the spark plug. Tighten spark plug to 20-30 Nm (15-22 
lb-ft).

Repeat steps 1 through 3 as required. 

Install the rocker arm shafts. Refer to the installation procedure in 
this section.

Install the valve cover. Install the six valve cover bolts and tighten 
to 5-9 Nm (44-80 lb-in).

Timing Chain/Belt

 Removal 

Remove the upper and lower engine front covers (6019). Refer to the 
removal procedure in this section.

Remove the timing chain/belt tensioner spring (6L273), spring cover, 
and timing belt tensioner bolt.

[FIGURE: A10926C.gif]

[FIGURE: A10928C.gif]

Mark the direction of rotation on the timing chain/belt (6268).

[FIGURE: A10929A.gif]

Remove the timing chain/belt.

 Installation 

Align the camshaft sprocket (6256) and crankshaft sprocket (6306) with 
the timing marks on the cylinder head (6049) and the oil pump (6600).

[FIGURE: A10996A.gif]

Install the timing chain/belt making sure the direction mark faces the 
same way as noted in removal. Use a counterclockwise motion to install the 
timing chain/belt. Start at the crankshaft (6303) and move up to the camshaft 
sprocket. There can be no slack between the crankshaft sprocket and the 
camshaft sprocket.

[FIGURE: A11657C.gif]

Install the timing chain/belt tensioner spring and spring cover on the 
timing chain/belt tensioner (6K254).

[FIGURE: A10927C.gif]

Position the timing chain tensioner and timing belt tensioner spring 
assembly on the engine (6007) and install the timing belt tensioner bolt. Do 
not tighten the timing belt tensioner bolt. 

Install the timing chain/belt tensioner spring on the anchor. 

Rotate the crankshaft two turns in the direction of normal rotation and 
align the timing marks. Ensure all marks are still correctly aligned.

Tighten the timing belt tensioner bolt to 19-26 Nm 
(14-19 lb-ft). 

Install the upper engine front cover and lower engine front cover. 
Refer to the installation procedure in this section.

Intake Manifold 

 Upper 

 Removal 

Release the fuel system pressure. Refer to Section 10-01 for the fuel 
pressure relief procedure.

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301). 

Drain the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 for the draining 
procedure. 

Remove the intake manifold support bolts and the upper intake manifold 
(9424). 

Disconnect the accelerator cable (9A758) from the throttle control 
lever (9A776). 

Remove the air cleaner to intake manifold tube (9B697). Refer to 
 Section 03-12 for the removal procedure.

Remove the coolant hoses from the upper intake manifold.

Tag and disconnect the necessary wiring and vacuum hoses. 

Remove the upper intake manifold to lower intake manifold bolts. 

Remove the upper intake manifold and intake manifold upper gasket 
(9H486).

 Installation 

Clean all traces of gasket material from the upper and lower intake 
manifold gasket surfaces. 

Place a new intake manifold upper gasket onto the gasket surface of the 
lower intake manifold. 

Install the upper intake manifold to lower intake manifold bolts. 
Tighten the intake manifold bolts to 19-26 Nm (14-20 lb-ft). 

Connect the coolant hoses to the upper intake manifold.

Connect the vacuum hoses and wiring as tagged during removal. 

Install the air cleaner to intake manifold tube. Refer to Section 03-12 .

Connect the accelerator cable to the throttle control lever. 

Install the intake manifold support (9J444) bolts. Tighten the intake 
manifold support bolts to 31-46 Nm (22-34 lb-ft). 

Fill the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 for the filling 
procedure. 

Connect the battery ground cable.

 Lower 

 Removal 

Release the fuel system pressure. Refer to Section 10-01 for the fuel 
pressure relief procedure.

Disconnect the battery ground cable. 

Drain the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 for the draining 
procedure. 

Remove the intake manifold support bolts and the intake manifold 
support. 

Disconnect the accelerator cable from the throttle control lever. 

Remove the air cleaner to intake manifold tube. Refer to Section 03-12 
for the removal procedure.

Remove the coolant hoses from the intake manifold.

Tag and disconnect the necessary wiring and vacuum hoses. 

Remove the intake manifold to cylinder head bolts and nuts. 

Remove the intake manifold and intake manifold gasket (9439).

 Installation

intake manifold. 

Position a new intake manifold gasket and the intake manifold on the 
cylinder head. 

Install the intake manifold to cylinder head bolts and nuts. Tighten 
the intake manifold bolts and nuts to 19-26 Nm (14-20 lb-ft). 

Connect the vacuum hoses and wiring as tagged during removal. 

Connect the coolant hoses to the intake manifold.

Install the air cleaner to intake manifold tube. Refer to Section 03-12 
for the installation procedure.

Connect the accelerator cable to the throttle control lever. 

Install the intake manifold support and intake manifold support bolts. 
Tighten the intake manifold support bolts to 31-46 Nm (22-34 
lb-ft).

procedure.

Oxygen Sensor (O2S) Wrench (EGO Sensor Wrench)

T79P-9472-A

 Removal 

Raise and support the vehicle. 

Remove the exhaust inlet pipe-to-exhaust manifold nuts and washers. 

Remove the muffler pipe bracket bolts. 

Lower the vehicle. 

Remove the air cleaner to intake manifold tube (9B697). Refer to 
 Section 03-12 for the removal procedure.

[FIGURE: U2514E.gif]

[FIGURE: A10903C.gif]

Remove the exhaust manifold (9430).

(5246).

Remove the exhaust manifold gasket (9448) from the cylinder head (6049).

[FIGURE: A10901C.gif]

 Installation 

Clean all traces of exhaust manifold gasket material from cylinder head 
and exhaust manifold.

Position a new exhaust manifold gasket on the cylinder head studs.

Install the exhaust manifold, three exhaust manifold nuts and four 
exhaust manifold bolts. Tighten the four exhaust manifold bolts to 16-23 Nm
 (12-17 lb-ft). Tighten the three exhaust manifold nuts to 
16-23 Nm (12-17 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: U2512E.gif]

 NOTE: Before installing the upstream O2S, make sure the exhaust manifold is 
in position. 

Use Oxygen Sensor (O2S) Wrench (EGO Sensor Wrench) T79P-9472-A to 
install the upstream O2S.

Position the exhaust manifold shield and install the exhaust manifold 
shield bolts. Tighten the exhaust manifold shield bolts to 16-23 Nm
 (12-17 lb-ft). 

Connect the upstream O2S electrical connector and install the connector 
in the routing bracket. 

Install the air cleaner to intake manifold tube. Refer to Section 03-12 .

Raise and support the vehicle. 

Position a muffler inlet pipe gasket on the exhaust manifold studs. 

Push the exhaust inlet pipe upward onto the exhaust manifold studs.

Install the exhaust inlet pipe-to-exhaust manifold nuts and washers. 
Tighten the exhaust inlet pipe-to-exhaust manifold nuts to 31-46 Nm
 (23-34 lb-ft). 

Position the muffler pipe bracket (5277) and install the muffler pipe 
bracket bolts. Tighten the muffler pipe bracket bolts to 38-56 Nm
 (28-41 lb-ft).

Lower the vehicle. 

Start the engine (6007) and inspect for leaks.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Crankshaft Main Bearings

 Removal 

Remove the oil pan (6675). Refer to the removal procedure in this 
section. 

 CAUTION: If crankshaft main bearings (6333) are to be replaced with the engine 
(6007) in the vehicle, keep at least two crankshaft main bearing caps tight 
while servicing the others. 

Remove the crankshaft main bearing cap bolts.

[FIGURE: A10935C.gif]

Remove the crankshaft main bearing caps and the lower crankshaft main 
bearings.

[FIGURE: A8448E.gif]

 CAUTION: Always turn the crankshaft (6303) clockwise. The timing chain/belt 
(6268) is designed to turn in its original direction of installation. 

Remove the upper crankshaft main bearings, using a bearing removal tool 
or bent cotter pin. Insert the tool or pin into the crankshaft journal oil 
hole and turn the crankshaft in the normal direction of rotation to remove the 
upper crankshaft main bearing.

[FIGURE: A8447A.gif]

[FIGURE: A11651C.gif]

 Installation 

Measure the crankshaft main bearing-to-journal clearance. Refer to 
 Section 03-00 for the procedure.

 CAUTION: Always turn the engine in the normal direction of rotation to prevent 
damage to the crankshaft main bearings. 

Use a bearing installing tool or bent cotter pin to help install the 
upper crankshaft main bearings.

Install the new lower crankshaft main bearings in the main bearing 
caps. Match the crankshaft main bearing tangs with the notch in the main 
bearing cap .

Be sure the crankshaft main bearings are in their proper position by 
observing numbers and/or arrows on the main bearing cap. Install the main 
bearing caps and tighten the crankshaft main bearing cap bolts to 54-59 Nm
 (40-43 lb-ft) in the order shown.

[FIGURE: A20654A.gif]

After each crankshaft main bearing cap bolt is tightened, be sure that 
the crankshaft can be rotated clockwise by hand. If not, remove that 
crankshaft main bearing cap and investigate for the source of interference. 
Tighten all crankshaft main bearing cap bolts and check again for proper 
crankshaft rotation.

Install the oil pan. Refer to the installation procedure in this section.

Pistons and Connecting Rods

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Cylinder Ridge Reamer

T64L-6011-EA

 Removal 

[FIGURE: A10479D.gif]

Remove the cylinder head (6049). Refer to the removal procedure in this 
section. 

Remove the oil pan (6675). Refer to the removal procedure in this 
section. 

Turn the crankshaft (6303) clockwise until the piston (6108) to be 
removed is at bottom dead center (BDC). 

 NOTE: Following the manufacturer's directions on the ridge reamer, remove the 
ridge until the bore is straight to the top edge of the cylinder. 

If necessary, remove the carbon from the upper portion of the cylinder 
bore using Cylinder Ridge Reamer T64L-6011-EA. 

[FIGURE: A10478B.gif]

Remove the connecting rod nuts (6212). 

Remove the bearing cap and lower connecting rod bearing (6211).

[FIGURE: A10943B.gif]

To prevent scratching of the crankshaft journal surface, install a 
piece of rubber hose on the connecting rod studs.

[FIGURE: A10942A.gif]

Use a hammer handle or piece of wood to tap the connecting rod (6200) 
and piston upward until the piston rings (6149) clear the top of the cylinder 
blocks (6010).

 NOTE: If removing more than one piston and connecting rod, mark each with the 
applicable cylinder number to aid in installation. 

Remove the connecting rod and piston assembly from the top of the 
cylinder bore.

[FIGURE: A8460B.gif]

 Installation 

Install the connecting rod bearing into the connecting rod and coat it 
with engine oil. 

Properly space the piston ring gaps. Dip the piston in engine oil and 
install and tighten Piston Ring Compressor D81L-6002-C or equivalent.

[FIGURE: A21569A.gif]

Slip two pieces of snug-fitting rubber hose over the connecting rod 
studs to prevent bolt-to-crankshaft journal contact during installation.

 NOTE: Cylinder numbering starts at the front of the engine (6007). 

Start the connecting rod/piston assembly into the cylinder bore, 
keeping the F mark on the piston toward the front of the engine. Be sure the 
connecting rod number and the cylinder bore number match.

[FIGURE: A10484A.gif]

Use a hammer handle or piece of wood to tap the piston/rod assembly 
into the cylinder bore. Guide the connecting rod studs over the crankshaft 
journal. Remove the rubber hose from the connecting rod studs.

[FIGURE: A10941F.gif]

Measure the connecting rod bearing-to-journal clearance. Refer to 
 Section 03-00 for the procedure.

Insert the proper size connecting rod bearing into the connecting rod 
cap. Install the connecting rod cap, making sure that the number on the 
connecting rod cap and connecting rod are on the same side and that they match.

[FIGURE: A10943B.gif]

[FIGURE: A8461A.gif]

Install the connecting rod nuts. Tighten the connecting rod nuts evenly 
to 15-17 Nm (11-13 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A10945C.gif]

Repeat steps 1 through 8 as necessary on the remainder of the 
rod/piston assemblies. Tighten the connecting rod nuts to 29-34 Nm
 (22-25 lb-ft). 

Check the connecting rod side clearance. The clearance is 0.110-0.262mm 
(0.0043-0.0103 inch) with a limit of 0.30mm (0.012 inch). 

Install the oil pan. Refer to the installation procedure in this 
section. 

Install the cylinder head. Refer to the installation procedure in this 
section.

Connecting Rod Bearings

 Removal 

Remove the oil pan (6675). Refer to the removal procedure in this 
section.

Turn the crankshaft (6303) clockwise, until the connecting rod (6200) 
and the piston (6108) assembly to be removed are at bottom dead center (BDC).

Remove the connecting rod nuts (6212).

Remove the bearing cap and lower connecting rod bearing (6211).

[FIGURE: A10943B.gif]

To prevent scratching of the crankshaft journal surface, install a 
piece of rubber hose on the connecting rod studs.

[FIGURE: A10942A.gif]

 NOTE: Push the piston up into the cylinder bore slightly to provide clearance 
for the upper connecting rod bearing removal.

Remove the upper connecting rod bearing.

 Installation 

Thoroughly clean the connecting rod bearings, connecting rod cap, and 
connecting rod.

Clean the crankshaft journal and lubricate with clean, heavy engine oil.

Install the upper connecting rod bearing in the connecting rod, then 
pull the connecting rod down until it seats on the crankshaft.

Install the lower connecting rod bearing in the connecting rod cap. 
Remove the two pieces of rubber hose from the connecting rod studs and install 
the connecting rod cap.

Install the connecting rod nuts. Tighten the connecting rod nuts to 
15-17 Nm (11-13 lb-ft). Tighten the connecting rod nuts a 
second time to 29-34 Nm (22-25 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A10945C.gif]

Check the connecting rod side clearance. The clearance is 0.110-0.262mm 
(0.0043-0.0103 inch) with a limit of 0.30mm (0.012 inch).

Install the oil pan. Refer to the installation procedure in this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Engine — Automatic Transaxle

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Differential Plugs

T87C-7025-C

 Removal 

 WARNING: FUEL IN THE FUEL SYSTEM REMAINS UNDER HIGH PRESSURE EVEN WHEN THE 
ENGINE IS NOT RUNNING. TO AVOID INJURY OR FIRE, RELEASE THE FUEL PRESSURE FROM 
THE FUEL SYSTEM BEFORE DISCONNECTING ANY FUEL LINE. 

Relieve the fuel system pressure. Refer to Section 10-01 for the fuel 
pressure relief procedure.

Disconnect the battery to starter relay cable (14300) and battery 
ground cable (14301).

Remove the battery tray (10732) and battery (10655). Refer to Section 14-01 for the removal procedure.

Mark the hood hinge location and remove the hood (16612). Refer to 
 Section 01-02 for the removal procedure.

Remove the engine air cleaner (ACL) (9600) and air cleaner to intake 
manifold tube (9B697). Refer to Section 03-12 for the removal procedure.

Remove theradiator (8005) and electric cooling fan. Refer to Section 03-03 for the removal procedure.

Disconnect the accelerator cable (9A758) from the throttle body 
(9E926). Remove the two accelerator shaft bracket bolts from the valve cover 
(6582). Remove the accelerator cable bracket (9728).

Disconnect the speedometer cable (17260) from the transaxle.

 NOTE: Plug the fuel hoses to prevent fuel leakage and contamination.

Disconnect the fuel tube hose (9324) and fuel hose from the fuel 
injection supply manifold (9D280). 

Disconnect the heater water hoses (18472) from the heater core.

Disconnect the power brake booster vacuum hose.

[FIGURE: A13206B.gif]

Disconnect the vacuum modulator hose and governor vacuum hose.

Disconnect all engine harness electrical connectors and grounds.

Disconnect the park/neutral position switch (PNP switch) (7A247), 
kickdown solenoid electrical connector, and transaxle ground.

Remove the shift-to-manual shaft bolt.

Disconnect the shift cable and bracket (7E395) from the transaxle. See 
 Section 07-05 for removal procedure.

Remove the accessory drive belts (8620). Refer to Section 03-05 for the 
removal procedure.

If equipped, disconnect the power steering lines from the engine (6007).

Raise and support the vehicle.

Drain the engine oil. Refer to the draining procedure in this section.

Drain the transmission fluid. Refer to Section 07-01 for the draining 
procedure.

Remove the front tire and wheel assemblies.

Remove the RH front splash shield (16A266) and LH front splash shield 
(16A267).

Remove the front suspension lower arm clamp bolts and nuts. Pull the 
front suspension lower arms (3078) downward, separating the front suspension 
lower arms from the front wheel knuckles (3K185).

[FIGURE: E7604C.gif]

Remove the RH front wheel driveshaft and joint (3B436) and LH front 
wheel driveshaft and joint (3B437) and install Differential Plugs T87C-7025-C 
into the differential side gears (4236). Refer to Section 05-04 for the 
removal procedure.

If equipped, remove the two power steering pump bolts and separate the 
power steering pump (3A674) from the engine.

If equipped, remove the A/C compressor. Refer to Section 12-03A for the 
removal procedure.

Remove the exhaust inlet pipe (5246). Refer to Section 09-00 for the 
removal procedure.

Remove the starter motor (11002). Refer to Section 03-06 for the 
removal procedure.

Remove the two rear transaxle support insulator nuts.

[FIGURE: N11418B.gif]

Remove the two front transaxle support insulator nuts.

Remove the two muffler pipe bracket bolts. Remove the muffler pipe 
bracket (5277).

Remove the six transmission case to cylinder block front bracket and 
case rear bracket bolts. Remove the transmission case to cylinder block front 
bracket (7E234) and case rear bracket (7E235).

Remove the engine rear plate bolt. Remove the engine rear plate (7007).

Remove the four flywheel-to-torque converter nuts.

Lower the vehicle.

Disconnect the vacuum lines from the intake manifold vacuum outlet 
fitting and cap (9A474) and the evaporative emission (EVAP) canister.

Attach lifting hooks to the engine lifting eyes and remove any slack in 
the chains.

[FIGURE: A20690A.gif]

Remove the engine support insulator through bolt and nut from engine 
support insulator.

[FIGURE: N11421A.gif]

Raise and remove engine and transaxle assembly from vehicle.

Remove the four engine-to-transaxle bolts.

Separate the transaxle from the engine.

Remove the flywheel. Refer to the removal procedure in this section.

Mount the engine on an engine stand.

Remove the lifting hooks from the engine lifting eyes.

 Installation 

Attach lifting hooks to the engine lifting eyes and remove any slack in 
the chain.

Remove the engine from the engine stand.

Install the flywheel. Refer to the installation procedure in this 
section.

Connect the transaxle to the engine.

 Cylinder Head 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

T81P-6513-A

 Disassembly 

Remove the cylinder head (6049). Refer to the removal procedure in this 
section.

Support the cylinder head assembly with the head gasket surface facing 
upward on a table or bench. Use blocks or pins to prevent valve or camshaft 
parts from contacting the table or bench. 

Clean the combustion chamber deposits with a wire wheel and a drill 
motor. Leave the valves in place to prevent damage to the valves or valve 
seats. 

Turn the cylinder head with the camshaft side facing upward and remove 
the 10 rocker arm bolts in the order shown. Remove the rocker arm and shaft 
assemblies. 

[FIGURE: A21657A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17975C.gif]

Remove the camshaft thrust plate (6269) and camshaft (6250).

[FIGURE: A21558A.gif]

Drive the camshaft oil seal through the cylinder head with a suitable 
tool. 

[FIGURE: A22980A.gif]

 NOTE: Mark the valves or keep the valves matched to their original locations. 

Compress the valve springs (6513) using Valve Spring Compressor 
T81P-6513-A and Valve Spring Compressor Set T87C-6565-A to remove the valve 
spring retainer keys (6518), upper valve spring retainer (6514), valve 
springs, lower valve spring retainer, valves, and valve stem seals (6571). 

[FIGURE: A21560A.gif]

Remove the oil passage plugs from the ends of the cylinder head.

Remove the engine block plug (6026) from the rear of the cylinder head 
by drilling a hole in it and prying it out with a drift or pointed bar. 

 Assembly 

Clean the cylinder head thoroughly with detergent and hot water or 
solvent.

Install the valve stem seal using Valve Seal Replacer T87C-6510-B.

[FIGURE: A21561A.gif]

Assemble the valves, lower valve spring retainer, shims (if used), 
valve springs, upper valve spring retainer, and valve spring retainer keys in 
their original locations. 

Install the camshaft and camshaft thrust plate. 

Install the front camshaft oil seal with Dust Boot Replacer T87C-5493-A.

[FIGURE: A10953E.gif]

 NOTE: The intake and exhaust rocker arm and shaft assemblies are identifiable 
by the difference between A and B dimensions in illustration below.

Install the two rocker arm and shaft assemblies.

[FIGURE: A21655B.gif]

Bolt the two rocker arm and shaft assemblies onto the cylinder head. Be 
sure the oil holes face down. Tighten the 10 rocker arm bolts evenly to 22-28 Nm

ADJUSTMENTS

Camshaft Timing 

Set the crankshaft (6303) to top dead center (TDC) by aligning the TDC 
yellow timing mark on the crankshaft pulley (6A312) with the white timing mark 
on the engine front cover (6019). To align the timing marks, turn the 
crankshaft pulley bolt (6A340) clockwise.

[FIGURE: A21562A.gif]

Disconnect the mass airflow (MAF) electrical connector. 

Remove the MAF sensor and air cleaner to intake manifold tube (9B697). 
Refer to Section 03-12 for the removal procedure.

Remove the drive belts (8620). Refer to Section 03-05 for the removal 
procedure.

Use Strap Wrench D85L-6000-A or equivalent and remove the three water 
pump pulley bolts.

Remove the water pump pulley (8509).

Remove the four upper engine front cover bolts and the upper engine 
front cover.

[FIGURE: A10918C.gif]

Ensure that the timing mark on the camshaft sprocket (6256) aligns with 
the pointer on the cylinder head (6049).

[FIGURE: A10920B.gif]

If the camshaft mark is not in sight, turn the crankshaft one complete 
revolution and check the camshaft timing mark alignment. 

If the timing marks are aligned, the camshaft (6250) is properly timed 
to the crankshaft. 

If the timing marks are not aligned, continue this adjustment procedure.

Remove the timing chain/belt (6268). Refer to the removal procedure in 
this section. 

Remove the spark plugs (12405). Refer to Section 03-07 for the removal 
procedure. 

Turn the crankshaft to align the timing mark on the crankshaft sprocket 
(6306) with the timing mark on the oil pump housing. 

[FIGURE: A21563A.gif]

Turn the camshaft to align the timing mark on the camshaft sprocket 
with the timing mark on the cylinder head.

[FIGURE: A10996A.gif]

Install the timing chain/belt. Refer to the installation procedure in 
this section. 

Install the spark plugs. Refer to Section 03-07 for the installation 
procedure. 

Install the upper engine front cover. Tighten the upper engine front 
cover bolts to 8-11 Nm(71-97 lb-in).

Install the water pump pulley. 

Use a Strap Wrench D85L-6000-A or equivalent to install the three water 
pump pulley bolts. Tighten the water pump pulley bolts to 49-61 Nm
 (36-45 lb-ft).

Install the drive belts. Refer to Section 03-05 for the installation 
procedure.

Install the MAF sensor and air cleaner to intake manifold tube. Refer 
to Section 03-12 for the installation procedure.

Connect the MAF sensor connector.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Recovery System

Included in the engine cooling system is a separate radiator coolant 
recovery reservoir (8A080). It is located beside the radiator (8005) and aids 
in maintaining the correct volume of coolant in the system by storing the 
excess coolant during engine operation. The excess coolant is drawn, or 
sucked, back into the system during engine cool down by vacuum from natural 
coolant contraction.

================================================================================
PAGE 2238
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 03-03: Engine Cooling

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Conditioner

In production, the cooling system is filled with a 50/50 mixture of 
Ford Premium Cooling System Fluid E2FZ-19549-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESE-M97B44-A, and water. This mixture is formulated to prevent 
corrosion, maintain system cleanliness, and provide anti-freeze protection in 
ambient temperatures to -37°C (-35°F). The 
50/50 mixture of antifreeze and water will also minimize the potential for 
overheating during hot weather. 

For the most effective cooling system operation, the specified mixture 
should be maintained all year round and in all climates.

 CAUTION: All vehicles use an aluminum radiator and require a 
corrosion-inhibiting coolant formula to avoid radiator damage. 

If Ford Premium Cooling System Fluid E2FZ-19549-AA is not available, 
use only a permanent antifreeze meeting Ford specification ESE-M97B44-A, 
diluted with tap water. Do not use alcohol or methanol antifreeze. Use of the 
wrong coolant may cause radiator (8005) and/or engine (6007) damage and may 
void any applicable engine warranty. 

Ordinary tap water may be used in an emergency (except in areas where 
the water is known to be exceptionally hard or to have a high alkali content) 
but should be replaced with the proper mixture of antifreeze and water as soon 
as possible. 

To avoid possible overheating in very hot weather, do not use mixtures 
with more than 50 percent antifreeze except in areas where antifreeze 
protection below -40°C (-40°F) is required. 
In this case, refer to the coolant mixture chart on the Ford Premium Cooling 
System Fluid container, but in no case exceed 60 percent antifreeze/water 
mixture.

A standard ethylene glycol hydrometer or Rotunda Battery/Anti-Freeze 
Tester 014-R1060 or equivalent can be used to check the protection level of 
the coolant. 

To prevent damage to the cooling system or engine during periods of 
below freezing when water or antifreeze is added to the radiator separately, 
always drive the vehicle (or operate the engine at fast idle for 30 minutes) 
before letting the vehicle stand with the engine OFF for prolonged periods. 
This will produce a uniform mixture throughout the cooling system and prevent 
damage.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Radiator

 Aluminum Core, Downflow 

Hot coolant flows out of the open water thermostat (8575) into the top 
portion of the radiator (8005). Coolant flows through the radiator tubes and 
is cooled by air passing through the fins.

PAGE 2240
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 03-03: Engine Cooling

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling Fan, Electric

 WARNING: WHEN WORKING IN THE ENGINE COMPARTMENT, STAY CLEAR OF THE FAN BLADE. 
BECAUSE IT IS ELECTRIC AND TEMPERATURE SENSITIVE, IT CAN START AT ANY TIME IF 
THE IGNITION IS ON. 

The electric cooling fan is an electro-drive type. Its operation 
depends upon engine temperature and ignition switch (11572) position. If 
engine coolant temperature reaches 97°C (207°
F) and the ignition switch is in the ON position, the engine coolant 
temperature sensor (ECT sensor) (12A648) sends a signal to the powertrain 
control module (PCM) (12A650) which turns the engine cooling fan motor (8K621) 
and fan blade assembly on. Because it cannot operate unless the ignition 
switch is ON, the engine cooling fan motor and fan blade assembly does not 
operate after engine shutdown. 

The fan control relay (FC relay) is located in the LH front corner of 
the engine compartment, between the battery (10655) and the headlamp assembly. 
Circuit protection is provided by a 30A fuse labeled COOLING FAN in the main 
fuse junction panel to the left of the battery.

If the vehicle is equipped with air conditioning, an additional relay 
is installed in the circuit. The A/C clutch control relay (19D572) bypasses 
the engine temperature portion of the circuit. The bypass circuit allows the 
engine cooling fan motor to operate whenever the A/C switch is engaged.

================================================================================
PAGE 2241
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 03-03: Engine Cooling

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Thermostat, Water

When coolant temperature is cold, the water thermostat (8575) is in the 
closed position and the coolant flow is restricted to the cylinder blocks 
(6010), cylinder head (6049), intake manifold (9424) and heater core (18476). 
As the coolant temperature increases, the water thermostat opens, allowing a 
portion of the coolant to pass into the radiator (8005). The coolant flows 
through the radiator tubes and is cooled by air passing over the cooling fins. 
Coolant is then circulated from the lower radiator outlet through the water 
pump (8501) and into the cylinder blocks to complete the circuit.

[FIGURE: Q3975C.gif]

Coolant circulation is provided by a conventional centrifugal water 
pump which discharges into the front of the cylinder blocks. The water pump is 
driven by a drive belt (8620) that is driven by the crankshaft (6303).

================================================================================
PAGE 2242
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 03-03: Engine Cooling

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Block Heater

 NOTE: The block heater (6A051) is standard equipment on Canadian vehicles.

The block heater warms the engine coolant, providing improved starting. 
The block heater also warms up the engine (6007) faster and allows the 
heater-defrost system to responded more quickly. Block heaters are recommended 
where winter temperatures are consistently -29°C (-20°
F) or below. The block heater should be plugged in at least 
three hours before starting the vehicle.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

 The powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) controls the engine 
cooling fan motor (8K621) while receiving information from the engine coolant 
temperature sensor (ECT sensor) (12A648). If a malfunction occurs with the ECT 
sensor, the engine cooling fan motor will run continuously. Refer to Section 3B
 in the Powertrain Control/Emissions 
Diagnosis Manual for diagnosis and testing of the PCM before proceeding. 

Verify the customer concern by operating the vehicle.

Visually inspect the following components of the engine cooling system. 

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Coolant level and condition

Condition of the upper radiator hose and lower radiator hose and the
inlet and outlet heater hoses

Fan blade condition and mounting

Blown fuse(s):

30A COOLING FAN

10A ENGINE

Damage to wiring harness

Corroded connections

Look for obvious shorts, opens, or damage in the wiring harness for the 
engine cooling fan motor.

Check the water thermostat (8575) for proper spring tension. Also check 
the water thermostat to make sure that there is not a large gap between the 
valve plate and the thermostat housing.

If fault is not visually evident, proceed to the Symptom Chart.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests — Engine Cooling System

 Pressure Test 

If no problem is found with the vehicle inspection and the radiator cap 
(8100) testing, and there is a coolant loss, the Pressure Test should be 
performed.

Make sure the engine (6007) is cool before performing the test.

Connect Rotunda Cooling System Adapter 014-R1062 to the Rotunda 
Radiator/Heater Core Pressure Tester 014-R1069 or equivalent, using the quick 
disconnect fitting.

Connect the filler neck adapter to the radiator cap pressure test 
adapter.

Connect the adapter to the radiator filler neck.

[FIGURE: Q3965B.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not pressurize the system above the given specification. 

Pressurize the cooling system to 103 kPa (15 psi).

Observe the pressure gauge for approximately two minutes.

Release the system pressure by depressing the relief valve on the 
underside of the tester.

If the system does not hold pressure, service the system for leaks. If 
no external leaks are present, refer to Section 03-01 for engine disassembly 
and inspection procedures. 

 Radiator Cap Pressure Test 

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CONDITIONS WHILE THE ENGINE IS 
OPERATING. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS COULD RESULT IN PERSONAL 
INJURY AND/OR DAMAGE TO THE COOLING SYSTEM OR ENGINE. TO AVOID HAVING SCALDING 
HOT COOLANT OR STEAM BLOW OUT OF THE RADIATOR, USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING 
THE RADIATOR CAP FROM A HOT RADIATOR. WAIT UNTIL THE ENGINE HAS COOLED, THEN 
WRAP A THICK CLOTH AROUND THE RADIATOR CAP AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST 
STOP. STEP BACK WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN 
YOU ARE CERTAIN ALL THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, PRESS DOWN ON THE RADIATOR 
CAP (WITH A CLOTH), TURN, AND REMOVE. 

Inspect both sides of the radiator cap rubber seal and the vacuum valve 
seat. Check for particles of rust or dirt that could impair sealing. Flush 
away any foreign material with warm tap water. Also check the sealing shoulder 
on the filler neck and wipe out any foreign material present.

[FIGURE: Q2635A.gif]

Remove the radiator cap.

Install Rotunda Cooling System Adapter 014-R1062 or equivalent, onto 
the filler neck adapter.

Use tap water to clean the radiator cap rubber seal and vacuum relief 
valve.

Install the radiator cap onto the radiator cap pressure test adapter.

Connect the female quick disconnect fitting of Rotunda Radiator/Heater 
Core Pressure Tester 014-R1069 or equivalent to the male quick disconnect 
fitting of the filler neck adapter.

[FIGURE: Q3966B.gif]

 NOTE: If the plunger of the tester is depressed too fast, a false pressure 
reading will result.

Slowly depress the plunger of the tester until the pressure gauge 
reaches 74 kPa (11 psi).

Verify the radiator cap maintains pressure.

Release the pressure by depressing the relief valve on the underside of 
the tester.

Repeat the test at least twice to verify that the pressure reading is 
acceptable and consistent. If the radiator cap pressure is less than the 
specified value, replace the radiator cap. 

 Thermostat, Water 

Overheating or failure to reach normal operating temperature can 
indicate improper water thermostat (8575) operation. The water thermostat must 
be removed from the vehicle and temperature-tested. 

Suspend the water thermostat and an accurate thermometer in a suitable 
container. Do not allow the test pieces to touch the bottom.

[FIGURE: Q3967A.gif]

Fill the container with water to completely cover the water thermostat.

Heat the water until boiling, and observe the thermometer temperature. 

 NOTE: Fully open means the water thermostat lifts a distance of 8.5mm (0.33 
inch) or more. 

The water thermostat should initially open at 86.5-89.5°
C (187.7-193.1°F), and be fully open at 100°
C (212°F).

[FIGURE: Q3968A.gif]

Start to cool the water thermostat.

The water thermostat should be closed at 83°C (181.4°
F).

If the water thermostat does not operate as indicated, replace the 
water thermostat. 

To check for low temperature leakage, cool the water thermostat to room 
temperature and hold it up against a lighted background. Check for light 
visible between the valve and the valve seat. If light is visible, replace the 
water thermostat. 

 Radiator Leak Test, Removed From Vehicle 

 CAUTION: Do not leak test the aluminum radiator (8005) in the same water that 
copper/brass radiators are tested in. Flux and caustic cleaners may be present 
in the tank and will affect the aluminum. A separate clean test tank is 
necessary, if possible, for aluminum radiators. If conditions do not allow for 
a separate test tank, clean the test tank thoroughly each time before testing 
an aluminum radiator. 

Clean the radiator before leak testing it to prevent contamination of 
the test tank.

Leak test the radiator in clean water with 137 kPa (20 psi) of air 
pressure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Thermostat, Water

 Water Thermostat Mounting — Exploded View 

[FIGURE: Q2811E.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301).

Remove the radiator cap (8100) from the radiator filler neck.

[FIGURE: Q3979A.gif]

Drain the coolant to a level that is below the upper radiator hose 
(8260). Refer to the procedure in this section.

Disconnect the upper radiator hose at the water hose connection (8592).

Remove the water hose connection bolt and nut securing the water hose 
connection to the cylinder head (6049).

Remove and discard the water hose connection gasket (8255). 

Remove the water thermostat (8575).

 Installation 

Thoroughly clean all gasket material from the water hose connection and 
cylinder head mating surfaces. 

Install the water thermostat in the cylinder head, with the valve end 
first and the subvalve at the top. 

Coat a new gasket with Perfect Seal Sealing Compound B5A-19554-A or 
F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M4G115-A.

Position the water hose connection gasket on the cylinder head with the 
bolt hole and threaded stud correctly aligned. 

Position the water hose connection on the cylinder head, using care to 
align the bolt hole and not to shift the position of the water hose connection 
gasket.

 NOTE: Ensure that the thermostat flange is properly seated into the recess in 
the water hose connection before tightening the bolts. 

Install the water hose connection bolt and nut. Tighten the water hose 
connection bolt and nut to 19-26 Nm (14-19 lb-ft).

Connect the upper radiator hose to the water hose connection. 

Fill the cooling system to the specified level with the recommended 
antifreeze/water mixture. Refer to the procedure in this section. 

Install the radiator cap on the radiator filler neck. 

[FIGURE: Q3979A.gif]

Connect the battery ground cable.

Warm up the engine (6007) and check for cooling system leaks.

 Aluminum Core, Downflow 

 Removal 

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES WHILE THE ENGINE 
IS RUNNING. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS INSTRUCTION COULD RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY 
AS WELL AS DAMAGE TO THE COOLING SYSTEM AND ENGINE. TO PREVENT SCALDING

Disconnect the engine cooling fan motor electrical connector.

[FIGURE: Q3979A.gif]

[FIGURE: Q3981B.gif]

Disengage the wiring harness from the routing clamps on the fan shroud

[FIGURE: Q3983A.gif]

[FIGURE: Q3985A.gif]

[FIGURE: Q3986A.gif]

Remove the radiator and fan shroud as an assembly from the engine 
compartment. 

[FIGURE: Q3987A.gif]

If necessary, remove the fan shroud from the radiator. For vehicles
