DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests 

 Transmission Fluid Level Check 

Apply the parking brake and ensure that the vehicle is in a level 
position. 

Run the engine (6007) at normal idle speed. If the transmission fluid 
is cold, run the engine at fast idle speed (about 1200 rpm) for several 
minutes. When the transmission fluid is warm, slow the engine down to normal 
idle speed. 

Apply the brakes firmly and shift the gearshift lever (7210) through 
all the gear positions. Place the gearshift lever in the PARK (P) position. Do 
not shut off the engine during the transmission fluid level checks. 

 NOTE: Clean all dirt from the oil level indicator cap before removing the 
fluid level indicator (7A020) from the transmission oil filler tube (7A228).

Pull the fluid level indicator out of the oil filler tube, wipe it 
clean, and push it completely back into the oil filler tube. Ensure that the 
fluid level indicator is properly seated in the oil filler tube.

[FIGURE: D7454A.gif]

[FIGURE: D7453E.gif]

Pull the fluid level indicator out of the oil filler tube and check the 
transmission fluid level. The transmission fluid level should be between the L 
and F marks.

If necessary, add enough transmission fluid to the transaxle through the 
oil filler tube to bring the transmission fluid level between the L and F 
marks on the fluid level indicator. Do not overfill the transaxle.

Install the fluid level indicator in the oil filler tube.

 Transmission Fluid Condition Check 

Make the normal transmission fluid level check. Refer to the procedure 
in this section. 

Observe the color and odor of the transmission fluid. It should be red; 
not brown or black. Odor can sometimes indicate an overheating condition, 
clutch disc (7550), or band failure. 

Use an absorbent white facial tissue to wipe the fluid level indicator. 
Examine the stain for evidence of solids (specks of any kind) and for 
antifreeze signs (gum or varnish on the fluid level indicator).

 NOTE: During disassembly and assembly, all overhaul checks and adjustments of 
clearances and end play must be made. 

If specks are present in the transmission fluid or there is evidence of 
engine coolant, the transmission fluid pan (7A194) must be removed for further 
inspection. If transmission fluid contamination or transaxle failure is 
confirmed by further evidence of coolant or excessive solids in the 
transmission fluid pan, the transaxle must be disassembled, completely cleaned 
and serviced. This includes cleaning the torque converter (7902) and 
transmission fluid cooling system. Do not perform any further checks before 
cleaning and servicing the transaxle.

 Transmission Fluid Leakage Checks 

Clean the transaxle case and operate the vehicle to warm the 
transmission fluid to normal operating temperature.

Inspect the areas of the transaxle indicated in the illustration for 
signs of leakage.

 Transaxle Fluid Leakage Check Points 

[FIGURE: CD9309H.gif]

If no visual sign of leakage is found, it may be necessary to use oil 
soluble aniline or fluorescent dyes to find the leak. Use the Rotunda Oil Leak 
Detector 164-R0756 or equivalent to check for transmission fluid leaks. Test 
the transaxle for leaks following the procedures supplied with the leak tester.

If any sign of leakage is found, repair as necessary.

 Fluid Leakage in Torque Converter Area 

In diagnosing and correcting transmission fluid leaks in the torque 
converter area, use the following procedures to locate the exact cause of the 
leakage. Leakage at the front of the transaxle, as evidenced by transmission 
fluid around the torque converter housing, may have several sources. By 
careful observation it is possible in many instances to pinpoint the source of 
the leak before removing the transaxle from the vehicle. The paths which the 
transmission fluid can take to reach the bottom of the torque converter 
housing are as follows:

 Possible Converter Area Leak Points 

[FIGURE: D12435C.gif]

Transmission fluid leaking by the torque converter impeller hub seal 
lip will tend to move along the torque converter impeller hub and onto the 
back of the impeller housing. Except in the case of a total seal failure, 
transmission fluid leakage by the lip of the seal will be deposited on the 
inside of the torque converter housing only, near the outside diameter of the 
housing.

Transmission fluid leakage by the outside diameter of the torque 
converter hub seal and the case will follow the same path which the leaks by 
the inside diameter of the seal follow.

Transmission fluid leakage from the torque converter to the flywheel 
stud weld will appear at the outer diameter of the torque converter on the 
back face of the flywheel (6375), and in the torque converter housing only 
near the flywheel. If a torque converter-to-flywheel stud leak is suspected, 
remove the torque converter and perform the torque converter checks in this 
section.

 Torque Converter Leakage Check 

If welds on the torque converter indicate leakage, remove the torque 
converter and make the following check:

Assemble Rotunda Torque Converter Leak Tester 014-R1075 or equivalent 
to the torque converter. Test the torque converter for leaks, following the 
directions supplied with the kit. 

[FIGURE: GD2710A.gif]

 Engine Idle Speed Check 

Warm the engine up until normal operating temperature is reached.

Place the gearshift lever in the PARK (P) position.

Run the engine between 2,500 and 3,000 rpm for three minutes and then 
return the engine to idle.

Connect a Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent to the 
vehicle to monitor engine speed.

Ground the engine self-test terminal (Pin 11) in the data link connector.

The idle speed should be within 750 ±50 rpms. Refer 
to Section 03-04 for the idle speed adjustment procedures if the idle speed is 
not within specification, 

 Stall Test 

Check the engine coolant level, the oil level and the transmission 
fluid level. 

Connect Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent, to the 
vehicle to monitor engine speed. 

Apply the parking brake and block the wheels to prevent the vehicle 
from rolling. 

Warm the engine until the transmission fluid temperature reaches normal 
operating temperature 50°-80°C (122°
-176°F). 

Depress the brake pedal (2455). 

Place the gearshift lever in REVERSE (R). 

Steadily increase engine speed to its maximum, quickly read the engine 
speed, and release the accelerator. 

Repeat the test for each of the gearshift lever ranges: DRIVE (D), 2, 
and 1. Followed by cooling the transmission fluid by idling the engine in 
NEUTRAL (N) for at least two minutes. 

Use the following stall test evaluation chart to verify the test results.

 STALL TEST EVALUATION CHART

Gradually increase the engine rpm and apply vacuum slowly to the vacuum 
throttle valve diaphragm. 

Record the governor pressure when the control pressure drops abruptly.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Transmission Fluid Drain 

 NOTE: The transaxle cannot be drained completely through the drainplug 
opening. For complete draining, also remove the transmission fluid pan (7A194).

Refer to Section 00-03 for information concerning the maintenance 
schedule(s). If a major repair, such as a clutch, band, or bearing replacement 
is required, the transaxle will have to be removed for service. At this time 
the torque converter (7902) and the oil cooler hoses must be thoroughly 
flushed to remove any foreign particles.

The following procedures are for a complete drain and refill for an 
in-vehicle service operation.

Raise and support the vehicle. 

Place a suitable container under the transaxle.

 CAUTION: Avoid spilling the transmission fluid. The fluid may be hot. 

Remove the transmission fluid drainplug and drain the transmission 
fluid into the container.

Remove the 16 transmission oil pan bolts and carefully remove the 
transmission fluid pan.

Thoroughly clean the transmission fluid pan and oil filter. Replace the 
oil filter if necessary. 

Install the oil filter. Tighten the oil filter bolts to 3-4 Nm
 (26-35 lb-in).

 NOTE: Do not over tighten the bolts. DO NOT use any type of gasket sealer, 
RTV, etc., on the transmission fluid pan or oil pan to case gasket (7A191). If 
necessary, soak the gasket in clean ATF. 

Place a new oil pan to case gasket on the transmission fluid pan and 
install the transmission fluid pan on the transaxle. Install the transmission 
oil pan bolts and tighten to 5-8 Nm (43-69 lb-in).

Install a new washer on the transmission fluid drainplug. Install the 
transmission fluid drain plug and tighten the transaxle fluid drain plug to 
39-54 Nm (29-40 lb-ft).

Lower the vehicle.

Section 07-01: Transaxle, Automatic

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Transmission Fluid Fill

If the automatic transaxle has been completely drained, remove the 
fluid level indicator (7A020) and add 2.8L (3 qts) of the specified 
transmission fluid through the oil filler tube (7A228).

If the automatic transaxle has been disassembled, and the torque 
converter (7902) has been drained, remove the fluid level indicator and add 
5.7L (6.0 quarts) of the specified transmission fluid through the oil filler 
tube.

Check the transmission fluid. Refer to the procedure in this section.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Transmission Fluid Check

Apply the parking brake and ensure that the vehicle is in a level 
position. 

Run the engine (6007) at normal idle speed. If the transmission fluid 
is cold, run the engine at fast idle speed (about 1200 rpm) for several 
minutes. When the transmission fluid is warm, slow the engine down to normal 
idle speed. 

Apply the brakes firmly and shift the gearshift lever (7210) through 
all the gear positions. Place the gearshift lever in the PARK (P) position. Do 
not shut off the engine during the transmission fluid level checks. 

 NOTE: Clean all dirt from the oil level indicator cap before removing the 
fluid level indicator (7A020) from the transmission oil filler tube (7A228).

Pull the fluid level indicator out of the oil filler tube, wipe it 
clean, and push it completely back into the oil filler tube. Ensure that the 
fluid level indicator is properly seated in the oil filler tube.

[FIGURE: D7454A.gif]

[FIGURE: D7453E.gif]

Pull the fluid level indicator out of the oil filler tube and check the 
transmission fluid level. The transmission fluid level should be between the L 
and F marks.

If necessary, add enough transmission fluid to the transaxle through the 
oil filler tube to bring the transmission fluid level between the L and F 
marks on the fluid level indicator. Do not overfill the transaxle.

Install the fluid level indicator in the oil filler tube.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Main Control Valve Body 

 Removal 

Raise and support the vehicle. 

Remove the front fender splash shield (16102) and front splash shield 
(16A267) to gain access to the transaxle.

 WARNING: AVOID SPILLING THE TRANSMISSION FLUID. THE FLUID MAY BE HOT. 

Drain the transmission fluid. Refer to the procedure in this section.

 NOTE: Be careful not to lose the throttle control valve rod (7A380) or the 
check ball and detent spring (7D017) used for the torque converter relief 
valve. 

 NOTE: Note the position of each main control valve body bolt for installation 
reference.

Remove the nine main control valve body bolts from the main control 
valve body (7A100) and carefully remove the main control valve body.

[FIGURE: D9345B.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: The check ball is inserted first, then the detent spring is installed. 
Use petroleum jelly, if necessary, to retain the detent spring and check ball. 

Install the throttle control valve rod into its hole in the transaxle 
case. Install the check ball and detent spring into the slotted hole in the 
transaxle case.

[FIGURE: D7464C.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not overtighten the main control valve body bolts. Overtightening 
may result in component failure. 

Install the main control valve body, mating the manual valve groove 
with the shift rod driving pin. Match the dowels in the transaxle case with 
the mating holes in the main control valve body. Tighten the main control 
valve body bolts to 8-11 Nm (71-97 lb-in).

[FIGURE: D7061B.gif]

 NOTE: Do not use any type of gasket sealer, RTV, etc., on the transmission 
fluid pan (7A194) or oil pan to case gasket (7A191). If necessary, soak the

Install the transmission fluid pan using a new oil pan to case gasket. 
Install the 16 transmission oil pan bolts and tighten to 5-8 Nm
 (43-69 lb-in).

Install the front fender splash shield and front splash shield.

With the vehicle on level ground, check the transmission fluid and add 
fluid as necessary. Refer to the procedure in this section. 

Ensure that there are no fluid leaks.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Intermediate Servo

 Removal 

Raise and support the vehicle. 

Remove the LH front wheel and tire assembly. 

Drain the transmission fluid. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Remove the main control valve body (7A100). Refer to the procedure in 
this section.

Remove the front stabilizer bar bracket nuts and the stabilizer bar 
bracket (5486), then remove the three stabilizer bar support bracket bolts and 
the stabilizer bar support bracket.

[FIGURE: E7603C.gif]

Remove the front wheel driveshaft and joint (3B436). Refer to Section 05-04 for the removal procedure.

Loosen the band adjusting stop (7C492) and band adjusting stop nut 
(7Z114).

[FIGURE: D13178A.gif]

Remove the band strut. 

Use a C-clamp and a socket to compress the servo piston into the 
transaxle case.

[FIGURE: D7469A.gif]

 WARNING: TO AVOID PERSONAL INJURY, WEAR EYE PROTECTION DURING THE FOLLOWING 
PROCEDURE. 

Use a screwdriver to remove the servo piston retaining snap ring (7381). 

Remove the servo retainer, servo piston, and servo piston spring 
(7D028) by slowly loosening the C-clamp.

[FIGURE: D7045A.gif]

Remove the servo piston spring and the servo piston large seal (7D024).

[FIGURE: D7470B.gif]

 Installation 

Lubricate the servo piston with the specified transmission fluid. 
Assemble the servo retainer, servo piston, servo piston large seal and servo 
piston spring and insert them into the transaxle case. 

Use a C-clamp and socket to compress the assembly. 

[FIGURE: D7469A.gif]

Install the servo piston retaining snap ring to the snap ring groove. 
Remove the C-clamp. 

Install the band strut to the intermediate band. 

Install the band adjusting stop to the intermediate band and tighten to 
12-15 Nm (9-10 lb-ft). Loosen the band adjusting stop three 
turns.

[FIGURE: D7468B.gif]

Install and tighten the band adjusting stop nut to 55-80 Nm
 (41-59 lb-ft). Do not allow the band adjusting stop to 
turn while tightening the band adjusting stop nut.

Install the front wheel driveshaft and joint. Refer to Section 05-04 
for the installation procedure.

Install the main control valve body. Refer to the procedure in this 
section.

Install the front stabilizer bar support bracket and bolts. Tighten the 
stabilizer bar support bracket bolts to 43-52 Nm (32-38 lb-ft).

Install the stabilizer bar bracket and nuts. Tighten the front 
stabilizer bar bracket nuts to 43-52 Nm (32-38 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: E7603C.gif]

Install the LH wheel and tire assembly and the lug bolts (1107). 
Tighten the lug bolts to 88-118 Nm (65-87 lb-ft). 

Lower the vehicle. 

Check the transmission fluid level and fill as needed. Refer to the 
procedure in this section. 

Ensure that there are no fluid leaks.

Vacuum Throttle Valve Diaphragm 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Vacuum Diaphragm Rod Gauge

T87C-77000-A

 Removal 

Drain the transmission fluid. Refer to the procedure in this section. 

Disconnect the vacuum hose from the vacuum throttle valve diaphragm 
(7A377).

Unscrew the vacuum throttle valve diaphragm by hand or use pliers on 
the flange and remove the throttle valve diaphragm gasket (7B426) and the 
throttle control valve rod (7A380) from the transaxle case.

 NOTE: The throttle control valve rod is a selective component. If the vacuum 
throttle valve diaphragm is being replaced, use the procedure that follows to 
select the correct throttle control valve rod from the chart. 

Clean the vacuum throttle valve diaphragm mounting hole and Vacuum 
Diaphragm Rod Gauge T87C-77000-A to ensure there is no transmission fluid on 
these surfaces.

[FIGURE: D7459C.gif]

With the beveled side out, insert Vacuum Diaphragm Rod Gauge 
T87C-77000-A into the vacuum throttle valve diaphragm mounting hole until the 
tool bottoms out. 

Place the rod (part of T87C-77000-A) through the opening of the Vacuum 
Diaphragm Rod Gauge T87C-77000-A until the rod (part of T87C-77000-A) bottoms 
out against the vacuum throttle valve.

Tighten the lock knob on the Vacuum Diaphragm Rod Gauge T87C-77000-A 
and remove Vacuum Diaphragm Rod Gauge T87C-77000-A from the transaxle case.

Use a depth gauge to measure the distance from the flat surface of the 
Vacuum Diaphragm Rod Gauge T87C-77000-A to the end of the rod (part of 
T87C-77000-A).

[FIGURE: D7460D.gif]

Use this measurement to select the correct size throttle control valve 
rod from the following chart.

and install the vacuum throttle valve diaphragm into the transaxle case. Use 
pliers to tighten the crimped portion of the vacuum throttle valve diaphragm. 

Connect the vacuum hose to the vacuum throttle valve diaphragm. 

Fill and check the transmission fluid level. Refer to the procedures in 
this section.

DISASSEMBLY

Transaxle 

 CAUTION: To prevent dirt from entering the transaxle, it should be disassembled 
and kept in a clean area. Remove the torque converter, taking care not to 
spill the transmission fluid. Before disassembly, clean the outer surface of 
the transaxle by using steam, cleaning fluid, etc. 

 CAUTION: During disassembly, avoid using rags that can leave fabric particles on 
components as this can block passages and cause valves to stick. Clean the 
disassembled parts, and clean the oil passages with compressed air and check 
to be sure they are not clogged. 

 NOTE: The casings allow separate repairs to be carried out on either the 
automatic transaxle or the final drive section. When a problem exists that 
only requires work on one section, separate the transaxle. Cover the section 
not requiring attention to prevent foreign material from entering the 
assembly.

Remove the eight differential ring gear bolts that secure the ring gear 
to the gearcase. Tap the ring gear around its circumference with a plastic or 
fiber mallet to loosen it and remove the ring gear from the gearcase.

 CAUTION: Do not exert excess pressure on the gearcase. 

Mount the gearcase in a vise equipped with soft jaws. 

Use a 4mm (5/32 inch) pin punch at least 90mm (3.5 inches) long, and a 
hammer to remove the differential pinion shaft lock pin (4241). Drive the 
differential pinion shaft lock pin free of the gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7557D.gif]

 NOTE: Whenever a differential bearing (4221) is removed from the gearcase, it 
must be replaced with a new bearing and race. 

Use Bearing Pulling Attachment D84L-1123-A and Step Plate Adapter 
D80L-630-3 (part of D80L-630-A) or equivalent to press the differential 
bearing (speedometer drive gear end) from the gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7558E.gif]

Remove the speedometer drive gear (17285) from the gearcase.

Use Differential Bearing Cone Remover/Replacer T77F-4220-B1 and Step 
Plate Adapter D80L-630-3 (part of D80L-630-A) or equivalent to remove the 
differential bearing (ring gear end) from the gearcase. 

Slide the differential pinion shaft (4211) out of the gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7560B.gif]

 NOTE: The differential pinion thrust washer (4230) and differential side gear 
thrust washer (4228) should be kept with their respective gears for possible 
reinstallation. 

Rotate the differential pinion gears and differential pinion thrust 
washers out of the gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7561B.gif]

Remove the differential side gears (4236) and differential side gear 
thrust washer from the gearcase. 

[FIGURE: C7562B.gif]

Refer to Cleaning and Inspection for differential inspection.

 Assembly 

Before differential assembly, clean all parts and dry with compressed 
air. Apply the specified transmission fluid to all surfaces after assembly. 

Install the speedometer drive gear to the gearcase, aligning the 
locating tang on the speedometer drive gear with the groove in the gearcase. 

Use Driver Handle T80T-4000-W, Bearing Cone Replacer T87C-77000-C or a 
press to install the differential bearing (speedometer drive gear end) to the 
gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7576C.gif]

Use Driver Handle T80T-4000-W, Bearing Cone Replacer T87C-77000-C or a 
press to install the rear differential bearing to the gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7577C.gif]

Locate and record the identification number on each differential side 
gear thrust washer. The following chart gives the thickness of the 
differential side gear thrust washers. This information may be used when 
setting the backlash of the differential side gears and the differential 
pinion gear.

 DIFFERENTIAL SIDE GEAR THRUST WASHERS

Coat the differential side gear thrust washers with the specified 
transmission fluid and install the differential side gear thrust washers to the 
differential side gears. Install the side gear assemblies to the gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7562B.gif]

Coat the differential pinion thrust washers with the specified 
transmission fluid. Install the differential side gears to the gearcase so 
that they are parallel to each other. Install the thrust washers onto the 
differential side gears.

[FIGURE: C7579B.gif]

After installing the differential pinion thrust washers on the 
differential pinion gears, turn the differential pinion gears back on the 
differential side gears and install them into the gearcase. The differential 
pinion gears and differential pinion shaft hole must be aligned on both sides 
of the gearcase. If the differential side gears and gearcase shaft hole do not 
line up, remove the differential pinion gears and install them into the 
gearcase again.

[FIGURE: C7580B.gif]

Install the differential pinion shaft into the gearcase with the flat 
on the shaft up and the differential pinion shaft lock pin hole entering the 
case last.

[FIGURE: C7581B.gif]

Use a suitable drift and hammer to install the differential pinion 
shaft lock pin through the gearcase and into the differential pinion shaft. 
Sink the differential pinion shaft lock pin until it is approximately 1.5mm 
(1/16 inch) below the surface of the gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7582B.gif]

Install the ring gear to the gearcase, with the depression on the gear 
toward the gearcase.

[FIGURE: C7584D.gif]

Align the threaded holes in the gear with the holes in the gearcase. 
Install the ring gear bolts and hand-tighten all of them. 

Tighten the ring gear bolts to 69-83 Nm (51-62 lb-ft). 
Tighten in two stages, marking the first bolt to be tightened and working in a 
crisscross pattern until all the bolts have been properly tightened. 

Check and adjust (if necessary) the side gear and pinion gear backlash 
as follows: 

Install the left and right front wheel driveshaft and joints into the 
differential.

Support the front wheel driveshaft and joints on V-blocks.

[FIGURE: C7585C.gif]

Use Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to measure 
the backlash of both differential pinion gears. The standard backlash is 
0-0.1mm (0.000-0.004 inch).

differential side gear thrust washer from the following table. Differential

Oil Pump

 Oil Pump — Exploded View 

[FIGURE: D7535C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

Position the oil pump with the pump cover facing up. 

Remove the seven pump cover bolts. 

Remove the pump cover. Do not allow the gears to fall out of the housing.

 NOTE: Do not mark the gears by pin-punching or otherwise stressing the gears. 

Before removing the inner and outer gears, mark them with an indelible 
marker or equivalent. 

Remove the pump flange and inner and outer gears.

Before assembly, inspect the oil pump as follows: 

Place Gauge Bar T80L-77003-A over the machined surface of the pump 
housing. Measure the clearance between the inner gear and the straightedge 
with a feeler gauge. Repeat this procedure and measure the clearance between 
the outer gear and the gauge bar. Standard clearance for both measurements is 
0.02-0.04mm (0.001-0.002 inch). The maximum allowable clearance is 0.08mm 
(0.003 inch). If any measurement is beyond the wear limit, replace parts as 
necessary to obtain the desired clearance. 

Measure the clearance between the edge of the outer gear teeth and the 
crescent dam. Take this measurement at the high point of the crescent, with 
the outer gear pressed against the pump housing. Standard clearance is 
0.14-0.21mm (0.006-0.008 inch). Maximum allowable clearance is 0.25mm (0.010 
inch). 

Measure the clearance between the outer gear and the pump housing. 
Standard clearance is 0.05-0.20mm (0.002-0.008 inch). Maximum allowable 
clearance is 0.25mm (0.010 inch). 

 NOTE: If, after installing new seal rings, the clearance is still beyond the 
maximum allowed, it will be necessary to replace the pump housing. 

Measure the clearance between the seal ring and the seal ring grooves 
on the pump cover. Repeat this measurement procedure until all four seal ring 
groove clearance measurements have been taken. Standard clearance is 
0.04-0.16mm (0.002-0.006 inch). Maximum allowable clearance is 0.40mm (0.016 
inch).

Check for a worn pump housing bushing as follows: 

Measure the outer diameter of the pump flange sleeve. The sleeve outer 
diameter limit is 37.900mm (1.492 inches). Replace the pump flange if the 
sleeve is worn beyond this limit.

Measure the pump cover bushing inside diameter. The bushing diameter 
limit is 38.075mm (1.499 inches). Replace the oil pump if the bushing is worn 
beyond this limit.

Refer to Cleaning and Inspection for oil pump inspection.

 Assembly 

Remove any oil pump gasket material remaining on the the surfaces of 
the pump housing and transaxle case. 

Assemble the pump gears and flange so that the alignment marks on the 
inner and outer gears are aligned and facing out. Coat the gears, pump 
housing, flange, and cover with the specified transmission fluid.

[FIGURE: D6969D.gif]

Install the pump cover to the pump housing. Install the seven pump 
cover bolts. Tighten the pump cover bolts to 11-14 Nm (95-122 
lb-in). 

[FIGURE: D6971D.gif]

After assembly, install the oil pump shaft (7B328) to the oil pump and 
ensure the gears turn easily.

Direct Clutch Snap Ring

Use snap ring pliers or a flat-blade screwdriver to remove the direct 
clutch snap ring. 

Remove the direct clutch pressure plate, clutch plates, and dished 
plate from the direct clutch drum. 

Place the T-handle of Clutch Spring Compressor T65L-77515-A through the 
direct clutch drum. Install and tighten the nut of Clutch Spring Compressor 
T65L-77515-A until the tension is relieved from the direct clutch hub snap ring.

[FIGURE: D6958B.gif]

Use snap ring pliers or a flat-blade screwdriver to remove the direct 
clutch hub snap ring. 

Remove Clutch Spring Compressor T65L-77515-A.

Remove the direct clutch piston spring retainer and the return springs. 

 WARNING: WHEN PERFORMING THE FOLLOWING PROCEDURE, USE CARE TO PROTECT YOURSELF 
FROM THE FORCE OF THE PISTON. KEEP FINGERS FROM BETWEEN THE WOOD BLOCK AND 
PISTON. EYE PROTECTION SHOULD ALSO BE USED TO PERFORM THIS OPERATION. 

Place a wood block over the direct clutch drum. Remove the piston by 
applying compressed air (not to exceed 400 kPa [60 psi]) 
into the fluid hole of the direct clutch drum, and remove the piston. 

Remove the inner and outer piston seal rings and discard.

Refer to Cleaning and Inspection for clutch inspection.

 Assembly 

Clean and blow dry all parts. 

Coat the new inner and outer piston seal rings with the petroleum jelly 
and install the seals to the direct clutch piston. 

Install the direct clutch piston into the direct clutch drum by pushing 
evenly around the circumference, being careful not to damage the seal rings.

[FIGURE: D7544D.gif]

Install the piston return springs to the mounting pegs on the direct 
clutch piston. 

Place the spring retainer over the return springs. 

Use Clutch Spring Compressor T65L-77515-A to compress the direct clutch 
to gain access to the snap ring groove.

Install the direct clutch hub snap ring and make sure it is fully 
seated in the groove. Remove Clutch Spring Compressor T65L-77515-A.

[FIGURE: D7545B.gif]

Install the direct clutch dished plate with the beveled side facing the 
direct clutch piston.

[FIGURE: D7546A.gif]

 NOTE: When installing new clutch plates, allow the plates to soak in the 
specified transaxle fluid for a minimum of two hours. 

Install the direct clutch plates, starting with an external spline 
clutch plate, then an internal spline clutch plate, and alternating until all 
direct clutch plates are installed.

Install the direct clutch pressure plate and the direct clutch snap 
ring. Ensure that the direct clutch snap ring is fully seated in the snap ring 
groove.

Check and adjust the direct clutch clearance as follows:

Measure the clearance between the snap ring and the pressure plate of 
the direct clutch by using a feeler gauge. If the clearance is not within 
1.6-1.8mm (0.063-0.071 inch) adjust it by selecting a proper pressure plate 
using the following chart.

[FIGURE: D7541C.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY OF SUBASSEMBLIES

Forward Clutch 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Clutch Spring Compressor

T65L-77515-A

 Disassembly 

Use a feeler gauge to measure the clearance between the snap ring and 
the pressure plate of the forward clutch. The clearance should be 0.8-1.0mm 
(0.031-0.039 inch). If the clearance is not within specification, adjust it 
using the appropriate pressure plate during installation.

[FIGURE: D7550C.gif]

Use snap ring pliers or a flat-blade screwdriver to remove the forward 
clutch snap ring.

Remove the pressure plate, the clutch plates, and the dished plate from 
the forward clutch drum. 

Place the T-handle of Clutch Spring Compressor T65L-77515-A through the 
forward clutch drum. Install and tighten the nut of Clutch Spring Compressor 
T65L-77515-A until the tension is relieved from the forward clutch hub snap 
ring.

[FIGURE: D6959B.gif]

Remove the forward clutch hub snap ring using snap ring pliers or a 
flat-blade screwdriver. 

Remove Clutch Spring Compressor T65L-77515-A. 

Remove the forward clutch piston spring retainer and the forward clutch 
return springs. 

 WARNING: WHEN PERFORMING THE FOLLOWING PROCEDURE, USE CARE TO PROTECT YOURSELF 
FROM THE FORCE OF THE PISTON. KEEP FINGERS FROM BETWEEN THE WOOD BLOCK AND 
PISTON. EYE PROTECTION SHOULD ALSO BE USED WHEN PERFORMING THIS PROCEDURE. 

Place a wood block over the forward clutch drum. Remove the forward 
clutch piston by applying a short burst of compressed air (not to exceed 400 
kPa [60 psi]) into the fluid hole of the pump housing with 
the direct clutch and forward clutch assemblies positioned on the oil pump 
extension.

[FIGURE: D7552A.gif]

Remove the inner and outer piston seal rings and discard. 

Refer to Cleaning and Inspection for clutch inspection.

 Assembly 

Clean and blow dry all parts. 

Coat the new inner and outer piston seal rings with the petroleum jelly 
and install the seals to the forward clutch piston. 

Install the forward clutch piston into the forward clutch drum by 
pushing evenly around the circumference. Be careful not to damage the seal 
rings.

[FIGURE: D7553A.gif]

Install the forward clutch piston return springs on the mounting pegs 
on the forward clutch piston.

Place the forward clutch piston spring retainer over the forward clutch 
return springs. 

Use Clutch Spring Compressor T65L-77515-A to compress the forward 
clutch to gain access to the forward clutch hub snap ring groove. 

Install the forward clutch hub snap ring. Ensure it is fully seated in 
the groove, then remove Clutch Spring Compressor T65L-77515-A.

[FIGURE: D7554A.gif]

Install the forward clutch dished plate with the beveled side facing 
the forward clutch piston.

[FIGURE: D7555A.gif]

 NOTE: When installing new clutch plates, allow the plates to soak in the 
specified transaxle fluid for a minimum of two hours. 

Install the clutch plates, starting with an external splined clutch 
plate, then an internal splined clutch plate, and alternating until all the 
clutch plates are installed. Install the forward clutch pressure plate and the 
forward clutch snap ring.

Check and adjust the forward clutch clearance as follows:

Install the forward clutch retaining plate, one-way clutch, and the 
forward clutch snap ring. Ensure that the forward clutch snap ring is fully 
seated in the snap ring groove.

Use a feeler gauge to measure the clearance between the snap ring and 
the pressure plate of the forward clutch. If the clearance is not within 
0.8-1.0mm (0.031-0.039 inch) adjust it by selecting the proper forward clutch 
pressure plate from the following chart.

[FIGURE: D7557A.gif]

Insert the hex of Torque Adapter T87C-77000-E into the end of the idler 
gear shaft (7F358) and place the assembly into a vise as shown.

[FIGURE: D7590C.gif]

Use a 1-1/2 inch socket to remove the idler gear shaft nut. 

[FIGURE: D7586B.gif]

 NOTE: Before removing the idler gear (7F475) from the idler gear shaft, note 
the direction of the notches in the gear teeth face for assembly. 

Remove the idler gear bearings and the idler gear from the idler gear 
shaft. 

Inspect the idler gear and idler gear bearings for pitting or scoring. 
Replace the idler gear bearing and bearing race as a set if worn or damaged. 

Hold the idler gear in a vise equipped with soft jaws. Use Impact Slide 
Hammer T50T-100-A and Internal Puller D80L-943-A or equivalent to pull one 
bearing race from the idler gear.

[FIGURE: D7587D.gif]

Press the remaining bearing race from the idler gear using Step Plate 
Adapter D80L-630-7 (part of D80L-630-A) or equivalent as shown.

[FIGURE: D7588C.gif]

Inspect the bearing races for scoring. If worn or damaged, replace the 
bearing races and idler gear bearings as matched sets.

 Assembly 

Use a hydraulic press, Driver Handle T80T-4000-W, and the appropriate 
step plate adapter from Step Plate Adapter Set D80L-630-A or equivalent to 
press the bearing races into the idler gear.

[FIGURE: D7589D.gif]

 NOTE: Install the idler gear with the notches in the teeth facing the 
direction noted during disassembly. 

Assemble idler gear bearings, adjustment shims, idler gear, and idler 
gear shaft nut on the idler gear shaft. Use Torque Adapter T87C-77000-E to 
hold the idler gear shaft. Tighten the idler gear shaft nut to 128 Nm
 (94 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: D7590C.gif]

Reposition the assembly in a vise equipped with protective jaw caps.

Use Torque Adapter T87C-77000-E and a torque wrench to measure the 
bearing preload by rotating the torque adapter tool.

[FIGURE: D7591C.gif]

The correct amount of bearing preload will indicate a drag of 0.03-0.9 Nm
 (0.26-7.8 lb-in) torque while rotating the tool. 

Higher torque readings indicate excessive bearing preload and the need 
for more adjustment shims. Too little drag indicates insufficient preload and 
need for fewer shims. Consult the chart for available shims and part numbers.

Maximum allowable number of shims is seven. 

Preload can be reduced by increasing the total thickness of the 
adjustment shim, or increased by reducing the total thickness of the 
adjustment shims.

support insulator bracket bolts to 38-51Nm (28-37 lb-ft).

 NOTE: Do not tighten the front transaxle support insulator through bolt and 
nut until the transmission support crossmember (6A023) is installed.

Install the front transaxle support insulator and the front transaxle 
support insulator through bolt and nut.

Position the transmission support crossmember and install the rear 
engine support rebound insulator bolts (6B091). Tighten the rear engine 
support rebound insulator bolts to 64-89 Nm (47-66 lb-ft). 

Tighten the front transaxle support bracket through bolt and nut to 
93-113 Nm (69-83 lb-ft).

Install the two front transaxle support insulator nuts. Tighten the 
front transaxle support insulator nuts to 43-52 Nm (32-38 
lb-ft).

Install the two rear transaxle support insulator nuts. Tighten the rear 
transaxle support insulator nuts to 28-46 Nm (21-34 lb-ft).

Remove Differential Plugs T87C-7025-C and install the front wheel 
driveshaft and joints (3B436). Refer to Section 05-04 for the installation 
procedure. 

Align the marks on the oil cooler tubes and oil cooler hoses, then 
slide the hoses over the lines. Install the hose clamps.

Attach the tie rod end (3A130) to the front wheel knuckle (3K186). 
Tighten the tie rod end nut to 35-40 Nm (26-30 lb-ft). 
Install a new tie rod end cotter pin. 

[FIGURE: G8226C.gif]

Attach the front suspension lower arm ball joint to the front wheel 
knuckle. Tighten the clamp bolt to 54-68 Nm (40-50 lb-ft). 

Install the front stabilizer bar (5482). Refer to Section 04-01 for the 
installation procedure.

Install the front fender splash shield (16103). Tighten the front 
fender splash shield bolts to 8-10 Nm (65-95 lb-in).

Install the front wheel and tire assemblies. Tighten the lug bolts 
(1107) to 88-118 Nm (65-87 lb-ft). 

Lower the vehicle. 

Remove Three-Bar Engine Support 014-00750 or equivalent.

Attach the shift cable and bracket (7E395) to the transaxle.

 CAUTION: Do not use any type of power wrench to tighten the nut. Damage to the 
transaxle may result. 

Install the manual control lever arm on the manual control lever 
(7A256) and tighten the manual control lever nut to 44-64 Nm 
(33-47 lb-ft).

Install coolant pipe retaining bracket located below the distributor.

Connect the transaxle vacuum hose. 

Connect the transaxle electrical connectors. 

Connect the ground strap to the transaxle. Tighten the ground strap 
bolt to 8-10 Nm (65-95 lb-in).

Connect the speedometer cable (17260) to the transaxle.

Connect the battery ground cable (14301).

Add the specified transmission fluid to the transaxle. Refer to the 
procedure in this section. 

 CAUTION: Ensure the gearshift lever (7210) position aligns with the manual 
control lever position exactly before starting vehicle. 

Start the engine (6007). Check for leaks and proper fluid level.

Sun Gear and Sun Shell

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Case

After component removal, clean the case with cleaning solvent, or use a 
high pressure steam cleaner to remove any internal or external grease, oil, or 
dirt.

Inspect all press fit bearing races for pitting, scoring or other types 
of damage. If any races must be replaced the mating bearing must be replaced 
as well.

Check the threads of any threaded bolt holes. All damaged threads must 
be repaired before reassembly of the transaxle.

Inspect all snap ring grooves looking for any damage to the slot into 
which the snap ring seats.

Check the case where the low one-way clutch notches into it. Look for 
broken notches or other types of damage.

Check case half mating surfaces for nicks or deformation. Look for 
cracks in the housings, and broken or cracked ears on the converter housing 
where it bolts to the engine (6007).

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Input Idler Gear and Final Drive Gears

Clean both gears with cleaning solvent and allow to dry.

Inspect gears for nicks, chips, or missing teeth. Any damage to one

caused by lack of lubrication.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Differential 

 Case 

Clean the gear case, differential pinion gears (4215), differential 
pinion shaft (4211), and differential side gears (4236) in cleaning solvent. 
Allow to dry.

Inspect the gear case for damage at the thrust areas where the gears 
ride. Look for grooves, pitting, or scoring.

Check the gear case for damage at the differential pinion shaft bore. 
Ensure that it has not become oblong. Check to see that the differential 
pinion shaft fits snugly in the bore without any lateral movement.

Check the differential pinion shaft for grooves and ensure that the 
roll pin bore has not become deformed.

 Gears 

Inspect the ring gear retaining bolt holes in the gear case. Ensure 
that no threads are damaged or stripped.

Check the gear teeth of the differential pinion gears and differential 
side gears. Look for chipped, nicked, or broken teeth. Ensure that there is no 
scoring on the teeth surfaces caused by lack of lubrication. Inspect the 
thrust washers on the rear of the gears for grooving, scoring, or pitting. 
Check the inner splines of the differential side gears where they spline to the 
front wheel driveshaft and joints (3B436) for stripping or worn spline teeth.

Inspect the speedometer drive gear (17285) for chips, nicks, or concave 
wear at the gear's center.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Ball Bearings

Clean the bearing with cleaning solvent. Allow to dry.

Inspect the roller surface for pitting, brinelling, heat scoring, or

Check the bearing cage for bends or distortion. Check the security of 
the roller in the cage and look for excessive play between the rollers and the 
cage. 

Inspect the bearing races for pitting, scoring, or heat cracks and make 
sure they are secure in their bore.

Damaged bearings and races must be replaced as a matched set.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Torque Converter 

The torque converter (7902) is welded together and cannot be 
disassembled. 

Check the torque converter for damage or cracks and replace, if 
necessary.

Inspect for damage, breakage, or rough areas on the inside bushing. 
Make sure the bushing size is within specification. If the bushing is not 
within specification, replace the torque converter. 

Remove any rust from the pilot hub and boss of the torque converter. 

Measure the inner diameter of the boss bushing. If it exceeds 53.075mm 
(2.0896 inches), replace the torque converter. 

When internal wear or damage has occurred in the transaxle, 
contaminants such as metal particles, clutch plate material, or band material 
may have been carried into the torque converter and oil cooler. These 
contaminants can be a major cause of recurring transaxle troubles and must be 
removed from the system before the transaxle is put back into service.

Inspect the one-way clutch end play by moving it with your fingers. If 
the end play is greater than 1mm (0.04 inch) or if a noise is heard or 
roughness is felt when the turbine shaft (7F351) is turned, replace the torque 
converter. 

[FIGURE: D12499A.gif]

Whenever the transaxle has been disassembled to replace worn or damaged 
parts or because the valve body sticks due to foreign material, the torque 
converter, oil and oil cooler hoses must be cleaned and flushed using the 
Rotunda Torque Converter/Oil Cooler Cleaner 014-00028 or equivalent. Under no 
circumstances should an attempt be made to clean torque converters by hand. 

The lack of a drainplug in the torque converter increases the amount of 
residual flushing solvent retained in the converter after cleaning. This 
retained solvent is not acceptable, and diluting is required. The following 
procedure is to be used after removal of the torque converter from the 
cleaning equipment. 

 Thoroughly drain the remaining solvent through 
the hub. 

Add 0.5L (0.53 US quarts) of clean transmission fluid into the 
converter. Agitate by hand. 

 Thoroughly drain the solution through the converter hub.

================================================================================
PAGE 2758
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 07-01: Transaxle, Automatic

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Transmission Oil Cooler

Conduct back-flushing with a Rotunda Torque Converter/Oil Cooler 
Cleaner 014-00028 or equivalent. Test your equipment to make sure that a 
vigorous fluid flow is present before proceeding. Replace the system filter if 
flow is weak or contaminated.

To aid in attaching the cleaner to the transmission cooler hoses, 
connect two additional rubber hoses to the transmission cooler hoses as 
described following.

Connect the cleaner tank pressure line to the transmission cooler 
return hose (hose attached to LH fitting of the transmission oil cooler).

Connect a tank return hose to the transmission cooler pressure hose 
(hose attached to the RH fitting of the transmission oil cooler). Place the 
outlet end of this hose in the solvent tank reservoir.

[FIGURE: D12725A.gif]

Turn on solvent pump and allow the solvent to circulate a minimum of 
five minutes (cycling switch on and off will help dislodge contaminants in 
cooler system).

Switch off the solvent pump and disconnect the solvent pressure hose 
from the cooler return line.

Use compressed air to blow out the transmission oil cooler and hoses 
(blow air into the cooler return hose) until all solvent is removed.

Remove the rubber hose from the remaining transmission cooler hose.

ADJUSTMENTS

Kickdown Switch

Disconnect the kickdown switch electrical connector.

Using Rotunda 73 Digital Multimeter 105-R0051 or equivalent, measure 
the resistance between the two kickdown switch terminals as follows:

With the accelerator pedal in the fully released position the 
resistance should be greater than 10,000 ohms.

Press the accelerator pedal to the wide open throttle position. The 
resistance should be less than five ohms.

If the kickdown switch (9E740) does not meet the specifications loosen 
the kickdown switch locknut.

Adjust and recheck the kickdown switch until it is within the 
specifications. If the kickdown switch can not be adjusted to be within the 
specifications, replace it.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests

 Filter, Transaxle Fluid Cooler Line 

 NOTE: The transaxle linkage/cable adjustment, automatic transmission fluid 
level, and line pressure must be within specification before performing this 
test.

Remove the fluid level indicator (7A020) from the oil filler tube 
(7A228).

Place a funnel in the oil filler tube.

Raise and support the vehicle.

Remove the fluid cooler hose (rear fitting) from the fitting on the 
transaxle case.

Connect one end of a hose to the fluid cooler hose and route the other 
end of the hose up to a point where it can be inserted into the funnel at the 
oil filler tube.

Lower the vehicle. Insert the end of the hose into the funnel.

Start the engine (6007) and run at idle with transaxle in NEUTRAL (N).

When the fluid flowing from hose is solid, the amount of fluid should 
be about 0.47L (0.5 qt) delivered in 30 seconds. If the flow is within 
specification, test is completed.

If the flow is not within specification, stop the engine. Disconnect 
the hose from the cooler return line and connect it to the converter-out line 
fitting (front fitting) on the transaxle case.

Repeat steps 7 and 8. If the flow is not within specification, flush 
the system and replace the filter. If specified flow is not yet obtained, 
replace the cooler lines.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transaxle Fluid Cooler

 Removal and Installation 

The transaxle fluid cooler is integral to the radiator (8005). In order 
to replace the transaxle fluid cooler, the radiator must be replaced. Refer to 
 Section 03-03 for the removal and installation procedures.

 Fluid Cooler Tube 

 Removal and Installation 

Raise and support the vehicle.

Position a clean, suitable container under the fluid cooler tubes.

Loosen the two fluid cooler tube clamps.

Disconnect and plug the fluid cooler tube from the transaxle.

Install the new fluid cooler tube and two new fluid cooler tube clamps 
on the transaxle.

Quickly disconnect the old fluid cooler tube from the fluid cooler and 
connect the new fluid cooler tube.

Position and tighten the two fluid cooler tube clamps.

Inspect and fill the transmission fluid. Refer to Section 07-01 for the 
procedures.

================================================================================
PAGE 2769
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 07-02: Transaxle, Automatic — Cooling

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fluid Cooler

When internal damage has occurred in the transaxle, metal particles, 
clutch plate material, or band material may have been carried into the 
transaxle fluid cooler. These contaminants must be cleaned out of the 
transaxle fluid cooler, fluid cooler tubes and fluid cooler hoses before the 
transaxle is put back into service. To clean the transaxle fluid cooler, use a 
mechanically agitated cleaner such as Rotunda Torque Converter and Oil Cooler 
Cleaner 014-00028 or equivalent. Follow all of the manufacturers' instructions 
for proper use.

================================================================================
PAGE 2770
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 07-02: Transaxle, Automatic — Cooling

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fluid Cooler Tubes

Upon inspection, if either of the fluid cooler line fittings are 
defective or damaged, the radiator (8005) must be replaced. Refer to Section 03-03 for the removal and installation procedures.

If the fluid cooler lines are cracked or damaged in any way, replace 
the fluid cooler lines.

Transaxle Construction

The five-speed manual transaxle has a split case design. One half of 
the case is the flywheel housing and the other half is the transaxle case.

The transaxle assembly is installed transversely in the engine

These support insulators also serve as rear mounts for the engine (6007).

The transverse installation of the transaxle assembly requires the left 
front wheel driveshaft and joint (3B437) and right front wheel driveshaft and 
joint (3B436) to transfer torque from the differential (4026) to the front 
wheels. The front wheel driveshaft and joints engage the differential side 
gears (4236) at the transaxle end and wheel hubs (1104) at the wheel end.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shift Linkages

 External 

Refer to Section 07-06 for information on manual transaxle external 
shift linkages.

 Internal 

 Reverse Gate Plate 

The input shift shaft (7L267) enters the flywheel housing through a 
gear shift control shaft boot (7F110) and lip-type shifter shaft seal (7288).

[FIGURE: C11296A.gif]

Item

7F477

Input Shift Shaft Selector Plate Arm

In the flywheel housing, the input shift shaft passes through and is 
pinned to the input shift shaft selector plate arm (7F477).

[FIGURE: C11297A.gif]

The input shift shaft selector plate arm extends away from the input 
shift shaft to engage with the shift fork selector lever (7F116) located in the 
reverse gate plate (7K129). The shift fork selector lever is mounted on a 
shift lever shaft (7C355) supported in the reverse gate plate to enable the 
shift fork selector lever to move back and forth, as well as rotate slightly. 

Two pins extend from the shift fork selector lever:

A shift selector pin which engages and moves the gear shifter forks.

A shift gate pin which meshes with the shift pattern in the reverse 
gate plate.

The forward and backward motion of the shift fork selector lever aligns 
the shift selector pin with one of the gearshift selector arms or the

[FIGURE: C11299B.gif]

Fifth/Reverse Gearshift Selector Arm

Rotation of the shift fork selector lever allows the shift selector pin 
to shift the transaxle into gear.

The shift gate pin extending from the opposite side of the shift fork 
selector lever aligns the slots in the reverse gate plate. This ensures proper 
alignment of the shift selector pin.

 Reverse Lock Out 

Because FIFTH and REVERSE are on a straight line in the shift pattern, 
a shift interlock is installed to prevent a direct shift from FIFTH gear into 
REVERSE.

The reverse lock out cam is mounted on the reverse gate plate where the 
shift gate pin engages the shift pattern.

[FIGURE: C11301B.gif]

The reverse lock out cam is spring-loaded to block the path of the 
shift gate pin to REVERSE gear from FIFTH gear. When the shift gate pin moves 
from the FIFTH gear position, the contour of the reverse lock out cam directs 
the shift gate pin into the NEUTRAL position. The shift gate pin can enter the 
REVERSE gear position only from the NEUTRAL position.

 Shift Control Shafts 

When the shift fork selector lever rotates, its motion is transferred 
to the synchronizers through gearshift selector arms, shift control shafts and 
gear shifter forks. The reverse idler gear and bushing (7141) requires an 
additional lever extending from the fifth/reverse gearshift selector arm to 
engage.

The transaxle contains three shift control shafts:

First/second gear shift control shaft (7241)

Third/fourth gear shift control shaft

Fifth gear (or main) shift control shaft

Only the first/second gear shifter fork and shift control shaft are 
moved directly by the shift selector pin. The two remaining shift control 
shafts require gearshift selector arms to transfer the motion of the shift 
fork selector lever to the gear shifter forks. As the transaxle is shifted 
into gear, the gear shifter fork engages a synchronizer.

 Shift Control Shafts 

[FIGURE: C11300A.gif]

Gear Shifter Fork, Third/Fourth

 Reverse Idler Gear/Reverse Gearshift Lever 

The reverse idler gear and bushing is mounted on a reverse idler gear 
shaft (7140) supported at one end in the flywheel housing and at the other in 
the transaxle case. Because the reverse idler gear and bushing slides and 
rotates on the reverse idler gear shaft the bushing is necessary to prevent 
metal-to-metal contact and wear. 

When the reverse idler gear and bushing slides on the reverse idler 
gear shaft it engages the reverse drive gear on the input shaft (7017) and the 
reverse gear (7K013) on the output and fifth gear drive shaft (7061). The 
driving gear is part of the input shaft and the reverse gear is machined on 
the outside diameter of the first/second synchronizer sleeve. 

When the reverse idler gear and bushing rotates on the reverse idler 
gear shaft it reverses the power flow to the output and fifth gear drive shaft.

To engage the reverse idler gear and bushing, the motion of the shift 
fork selector lever is transferred to the reverse gearshift lever (7K002) 
through the fifth/reverse gearshift selector arm. The reverse gearshift lever 
is mounted on a meshlock plunger (7233) that allows it to act as a fulcrum. 
When the fifth/reverse gearshift selector arm moves its end of the reverse 
gearshift lever, the opposite end slides the reverse idler gear and bushing 
along the reverse idler gear shaft into engagement with the input shaft and 
output shaft gears.

 Shift Interlocks 

Once the transaxle is shifted into a gear, movement of the remaining 
shift control shafts is prevented by the shift interlocks. The shift control 
shafts are locked in position to eliminate the simultaneous engagement of the 
transaxle in two gears. 

The shift interlock consists of ashift rod lock pin (7C316) and two 
shift rod lock pin plugs. The shift rod lock pin plugs are located on each 
side of the fifth gear shift control shaft. The shift rod lock pin is 
positioned in the fifth gear shift control shaft to contact the ends of the 
shift rod lock pin plugs.

In NEUTRAL, the shift control shaft detents align with the shift rod 
lock pin plugs and shift rod lock pin, allowing movement of any of the three 
shift control shafts. Depending upon the gear selected, the shift rod lock pin 
plugs and shift rod lock pin will shift their position to lock the remaining 
two shift control shafts in position.

 NEUTRAL 

[FIGURE: C11302B.gif]

In first/second gear or third/fourth gear, the affected shift rod lock 
pin plug moves to lock the fifth gear shift control shaft. Motion is 
transferred through the shift rod lock pin to the remaining shift rod lock pin 
plug to lock the other shift control shaft.

 FIRST 

[FIGURE: C8303C.gif]

A shift to FIFTH or REVERSE gear moves both shift rod lock pin plugs 
away from the fifth gear shift control shaft to lock both the first/second 
gear shift control shaft and third/fourth gear shift control shaft.

 Shift Detents 

When the transaxle is shifted into a gear, the positive feeling of 
engagement is provided by the shift detents. The detents are spring-loaded 
balls that ride against notches cut in the shift control shafts. Each shift 
control shaft has three notches. The center notch on all shift control shafts 
is the NEUTRAL detent. The notches on either side of the center notch 
represent a gear position. 

[FIGURE: C11303A.gif]

The first/second and fifth/reverse detents are located in the transaxle 
case. The third/fourth detent is located in the flywheel housing. The detent 
balls and springs are installed from outside of the case and threaded plugs 
are used to seal the bores.

[FIGURE: C11304A.gif]

 Geartrain 

The geartrain consists of the: 

Input shaft 

Output and fifth gear drive shaft

Reverse idler gear and bushing 

Differential (4026) 

The input shaft is splined to the clutch disc (7550) and supported in 
the transaxle case on ball bearings (7025). Input shaft end play is controlled 
with selective shims installed directly in the transaxle case bore. The 
third/fourth synchronizer is installed on the input shaft. 

The output and fifth gear drive shaft is supported in the flywheel 
housing on tapered roller bearings. The preload on the output and fifth gear 
drive shaft bearing is set using selective shims. The preload shims are 
installed under the output and fifth gear drive shaft bearing cup in the 
transaxle case. The first/second synchronizer is installed on the output and 
fifth gear drive shaft. The fifth gear synchronizer is installed on the end of 
the output and fifth gear drive shaft.

Differential

4221

Differential Bearing

The ends of the differential (4026) are supported on tapered roller 
differential bearings (4221). The cups for these differential bearings are 
seated in the transaxle case and the flywheel housing. Preload on the 
differential bearings is set using a selective differential bearing shim 
(4067) that is installed under the differential bearing cup in the transaxle 
case.

[FIGURE: C11307B.gif]

The differential includes the typical differential side gears (4236) 
and shaft-mounted differential pinion gears (4215). Direct contact between the 
four gears and the differential case is prevented by differential side gear 
thrust washers (4228) installed under the gears. The differential pinion shaft 
(4211) is held in position by a differential pinion shaft lock pin (4241) that 
extends through the end of the differential pinion shaft and the differential 
case.

The speedometer drive gear (17285) is also mounted on the differential 
case. It is located between the tapered roller differential bearing and the 
differential case. A tab on the speedometer drive gear and a matching slot in 
the differential case prevent the speedometer drive gear from spinning on the 
differential case.

[FIGURE: C11308B.gif]

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification 

Before referring to the Symptom Chart in this section, try to determine 
whether the cause of the problem is the transaxle or the clutch. The vehicle 
should be road tested, if possible, to determine or confirm the complaint. 
Under normal operating conditions, a large percentage of transaxle complaints 
are due to misadjusted, damaged, or worn components outside of the transaxle, 
such as clutch, clutch linkage, and shift linkage. Before and during the road 
test, make sure that the clutch is functioning properly, the shift linkage is 
properly adjusted and that the transaxle is filled to the proper level with 
the specified lubricant. 

If the transmission fluid level is low, the affected area should first 
be cleaned of all grease, dirt, and oil. The vehicle should be operated long 
enough to bring the transmission fluid to operating temperature. Inspect the 
areas shown in the following illustration. 

Remember to check the transmission fluid level and fill to the full 
mark before performing the diagnosis.

 Leak Inspection Points 

[FIGURE: C8173C.gif]

If the condition is narrowed to the transaxle, refer to the Symptom 
Chart for the description that best fits the condition. Use the Possible 
Source column to isolate the condition to a specific component and then use 
the Action column to determine the appropriate repair. In some cases, this 
column will refer to procedures either in this section or other sections in 
the Service Manual. After making a repair, always road test the vehicle to 
confirm the diagnosis and repair. 

Refer to Section 08-00 if the problem is narrowed to the clutch system.

IN-VEHICLE SERVICE

Transmission Fluid Check 

The speedometer cable sleeve (17B301) is used as a dipstick to check 
the transmission fluid level. To check and adjust the transmission fluid 
level, use the following procedure: 

 NOTE: Pliers may be necessary to loosen the speedometer cable retainer.

 Loosen the speedometer cable retainer on the speedometer cable sleeve 
and slide it up the speedometer cable (17260).

Disconnect the speedometer cable from the speedometer cable sleeve. 

Remove the speedometer cable sleeve bolt. 

Remove the speedometer cable sleeve and speedometer gear assembly. 

Remove all traces of transmission fluid from the speedometer gear 
(17271) and speedometer cable sleeve.

Insert the speedometer cable sleeve into its bore in the flywheel 
housing. 

Remove the speedometer cable sleeve and check the transmission fluid 
level using the indicator mark on the speedometer cable sleeve. 

[FIGURE: C8011C.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not fill the transmission above the full (F) mark. 

If the transmission fluid level is below the low (L) mark, add the 
required amount of specified transmission fluid through the speedometer cable 
sleeve bore. 

 NOTE: If there is any doubt about the condition of the speedometer gear 
O-ring, it must be replaced. 

Inspect the speedometer gear O-ring. If there is any sign of damage or 
deterioration, replace it. 

Install the speedometer cable sleeve and speedometer gear as an 
assembly. 

Install the speedometer cable sleeve bolt. Tighten the speedometer 
cable sleeve bolt to 8-11 Nm (71-97 lb-in). 

Connect the speedometer cable and hand tighten the speedometer cable 
retainer on the speedometer cable sleeve.

REMOVAL

Ring Gear, Flywheel 

Remove the flywheel (6375). Refer to the procedure in this section.

Support the flywheel on a flat and stable stand that will allow the 
flywheel ring gear (6384) to separate from the flywheel. 

 WARNING: THIS PROCEDURE SHOULD BE PERFORMED ONLY BY A PROPERLY EQUIPPED AND 
EXPERIENCED ACETYLENE TORCH OPERATOR. TO AVOID PERSONAL INJURY, TONGS MUST BE 
USED OR ASBESTOS GLOVES MUST BE WORN WHEN HANDLING THE HEATED FLYWHEEL RING 
GEAR. 

Expand the flywheel ring gear by evenly heating it with an acetylene 
torch. 

Use a brass drift and hammer to drive the flywheel ring gear off the 
flywheel. Tap the flywheel ring gear evenly to prevent binding.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY OF SUBASSEMBLIES

Synchronizer 

 NOTE: Before disassembling a synchronizer, make an alignment mark on the hub 
and sleeve. The synchronizer sleeve and hub are matched during factory 
assembly and should be reassembled in exactly the same position. The marks 
will provide the necessary alignment reference. 

 Disassembly 

Slide the synchronizer hub and synchronizer inserts out of the 
synchronizer sleeve. 

Remove the synchronizer blocking springs from the synchronizer hub.

 First/Second Synchronizer Shown, Other Synchronizers Similar 

[FIGURE: C7998C.gif]

 Assembly 

Use the marks made during disassembly for alignment reference to 
install the synchronizer hub in the synchronizer sleeve. 

If alignment marks are not present, make sure the synchronizer hub and 
synchronizer sleeve are assembled with the hub oil grooves facing the 
direction shown in the illustrations for the fifth synchronizer and the 
first/second synchronizer. Because the outside diameter of the third/fourth 
synchronizer is concentric, the relationship of the oil grooves to the sleeve 
is not important.

 Fifth Synchronizer 

[FIGURE: C7783D.gif]

 First/Second Synchronizer 

[FIGURE: C7785C.gif]

Install the synchronizer inserts. There are two synchronizer insert 
sizes. The following illustration and chart detail which size synchronizer 
insert belongs with which synchronizer.

[FIGURE: C8002B.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure each spring engages the hole in the synchronizer hub as shown 
and that they rotate away from the same holes in opposite directions. 

Install the synchronizer blocking springs.

[FIGURE: C8003B.gif]

Torque Adapter

T88C-7025-E

Remove the transaxle case-to-flywheel housing bolts and the transaxle 
case.

Perform the input shaft end play check procedure in this section. If 
necessary, remove the input shaft (7017) and install the correct end play shim.

Make sure the output and fifth shaft funnel (7L276) and output and 
fifth gear drive shaft bearing cup are installed in the flywheel housing.

Remove the original preload shim(s) from the transaxle case and install 
the output and fifth gear drive shaft bearing cup.

Install the transaxle case-to-flywheel housing bolts. Tighten the 
transaxle case-to-flywheel housing bolts to 19-26 Nm (14-19 
lb-ft).

 NOTE: Do not install more than two bearing preload shims.

amount of torque required to turn the input shaft. 

[FIGURE: C8032B.gif]

If the torque wrench reads 0.06-0.5 Nm (0.5-4.4 
lb-in), preload is within specifications. 

If preload is not within specifications, install the appropriate 
bearing preload shims.

 Input Shaft End Play Check 

Make sure the input shaft funnel is in position in the transaxle case 
bore. 

Remove the original end play shim(s) and install the input shaft 
bearing cup. 

Install the input shaft. 

Install the transaxle case. 

Install the transaxle case-to-flywheel housing bolts. Tighten the 
transaxle case-to-flywheel housing bolts to 19-26 Nm (14-19 
lb-ft).

Tap the end of the input shaft with a plastic-tipped hammer to make 
sure the input shaft, input shaft bearing cup, and input shaft funnel are 
properly seated. 

Mount a Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C, or equivalent, on 
the flywheel housing with the stylus contacting the end of the input shaft.

[FIGURE: C8031D.gif]

 NOTE: If a shim other than the original is installed, output and fifth gear 
drive shaft bearing preload and differential bearing preload must be checked. 
Adjust preloads if necessary. Refer to the procedures in this section.

 NOTE: Do not install more than two shims. 

Raise the input shaft and note the dial indicator reading. 

If the reading is 0.005-0.1mm (0.0002-0.004 inch), input shaft end play 
is within specifications. 

If end play is not within specifications, install an appropriate end 
play shim.

INSTALLATION

Flywheel Ring Gear

 WARNING: THIS PROCEDURE SHOULD BE PERFORMED ONLY BY A PROPERLY EQUIPPED AND 
EXPERIENCED ACETYLENE TORCH OPERATOR. TO AVOID PERSONAL INJURY, TONGS MUST BE 
USED OR ASBESTOS GLOVES MUST BE WORN WHEN HANDLING THE HEATED FLYWHEEL RING 
GEAR. 

 CAUTION: Do not heat the flywheel ring gear beyond 300°C (572°
F). Excessive heat may destroy the heat treatment the 
flywheel ring gear received during manufacture. Heat-indicating crayons, 
available from most tool suppliers, can be used to measure the temperature of 
the flywheel ring gear. At a certain temperature, the crayon will melt, 
providing an indicator that can prevent overheating of the flywheel ring gear. 

Expand the replacement flywheel ring gear (6384) by heating the 
flywheel ring gear on a flat metal surface. Keep the torch moving to prevent 
hot spots.

 NOTE: The bevel on the inside diameter of the flywheel ring gear must face 
the engine side of the flywheel (6375). 

Use asbestos gloves or tongs to place the flywheel ring gear on the 
flywheel.

Use a brass drift and hammer to drive the flywheel ring gear onto the 
flywheel. Tap the flywheel ring gear evenly to prevent binding.

Install the flywheel. Refer to the procedure in this section.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Case 

 NOTE: Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure of the input shaft oil seal 
(7A011) and differential seals to any solvents used to clean the transaxle 
case. 

 Inspection 

 NOTE: Casting imperfections sometimes look like cracks. 

Inspect the transaxle case and flywheel housing for cracks, worn or 
damaged bearing bores, damaged threads, or any other damage that could affect 
the operation of the transaxle. 

Inspect the transaxle case and flywheel housing mating surfaces for 
small nicks or burrs that could cause misalignment of the two halves. Remove 
all small nicks or burrs with a fine stone or file. 

Inspect the tapered roller bearings. Replace if worn or damaged. 

Check the input shaft (7017) for chipped teeth, cracks, scores, or bent 
reverse gear teeth. 

Check the reverse idler gear and bushing (7141) for chipped, broken, or 
bent teeth. Check the reverse idler gear and bushing for bushing damage. Check 
wear of the reverse idler gear shaft (7140). It is normal for the front of the 
teeth to show wear; this does not interfere with proper function. 

Check the teeth, splines, and journals of the output shaft for damage. 

Check all other gears for chipped, broken, or worn teeth. Check for 
eroded clutching teeth and damaged cone surfaces. These clutching teeth will 
normally show rounding of the points, which does not interfere with normal 
operation. 

Check the synchronizer sleeves for free movement on their hubs. Make 
sure the alignment marks are properly indexed. Check for damaged clutching 
teeth (these splines normally show wear at the points, but this does not 
interfere with synchronizer function). Check for position of insert springs. 

Inspect the synchronizer blocking rings for wear marks on the teeth and 
back face, which indicates that the ring was bottoming on the gear face due to 
wear of the blocker ring.

================================================================================
PAGE 2807
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 07-03: Transaxle, Manual

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Case Service 

 NOTE: The case threads which retain the following should not be serviced: 

Fork interlock sleeve retaining pin. 

Backup lamp switch (15520).

Detent spring screw. 

Reverse gate plate (7K129).

If a transaxle case thread is damaged, helicoil service kits may be 
purchased. To service a damaged thread, the following procedures should be 
carefully followed: 

Using the same drill size as the thread outside diameter, drill out the 
damaged threads. For example, use an 8mm drill for an 8mm X 1.5 thread. 

Select the proper special tap and tap the drilled hole. The tap is 
marked for the size of the thread being serviced. The special tap marked 8mm X 
1.5 will not cut the same thread as a standard 8mm X 1.5 tap. It does cut a 
thread large enough to accommodate the insert and after the insert is 
installed, the original thread size (8mm X 1.5) is restored. 

Select the proper coil inserting tool. These tools are marked with the 
thread size being serviced. Place the insert on the tool and adjust the sleeve 
to the length of the insert being used. Press the insert against the face of 
the tapped hole. Rotate the tool clockwise and wind the insert into the hole 
until the insert is one-half turn below the face. 

Working through the insert, bend the insert tang straight up and down 
until it breaks off at the notch. 

Improperly installed inserts can be removed with an extractor tool. 
Place the extractor tool in the insert so that the blade rests against the top 
coil, one-quarter to one-half turn away from the end of the coil. Tap the tool 
sharply with a hammer so that the blade will cut into the insert. Exert 
downward pressure on the tool and turn it counterclockwise until the insert is 
removed.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Gears 

Examine the differential pinion gears (4215) and differential side 
gears (4236) for scoring, excessive wear, nicks, and chips. Worn, scored, and 
damaged gears cannot be serviced and must be replaced. 

Check the following components, and repair or replace if necessary. 

Check the first, second, third, fourth and fifth gears for: 

Worn or damaged synchronizer blocking ring (7107), hub sleeve coupling, 
or gear teeth. 

Worn or damaged inner surface or end surface of gears.

Check the input shaft gear assembly for:

A clearance between the selective snap ring and input shaft bearing 
(fifth gear end) of 0.1mm (0.004 inch)

[FIGURE: C8004B.gif]

Check the input shaft (7017) for:

Scoring, excessive wear, nicks and chips. Replace if necessary.

Check the output and fifth gear drive shaft assembly for:

A clearance between the selective snap ring and the output and fifth 
gear drive shaft bearing of 0.1mm (0.004 inch).

[FIGURE: C8006B.gif]

Check the output and fifth gear drive shaft for:

Worn or damaged gear contact surfaces, splines or gear teeth.

Clogged oil passage.

Check the synchronizer blocking ring for:

Engagement with the gear. The synchronizer blocking ring must engage 
smoothly with the gear.

Worn or damaged teeth or tapered surface.

Check the synchronizer for:

Worn or damaged splines, synchronizer insert groove, or end surface.

Check for smooth movement of the synchronizer hub within the 
synchronizer sleeve when it is installed.

[FIGURE: C11375A.gif]

Check the synchronizer sleeve for:

Worn or damaged hub splines or shifter fork groove

Excessive clearance between the sleeve and shifter fork.

Check the synchronizer inserts and springs for:

Worn inserts.

Bent spring. 

Check the reverse idler gear for:

Worn or damaged bushing, gear teeth, or release lever coupling groove.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Differential Case 

Ensure the differential bearing journals are smooth. Carefully examine 
the differential case bearing shoulders, which may have been damaged when the 
bearings were removed. The differential bearings (4221) will fail if they do 
not seat firmly against the shoulders. Check the fit (free rotation) of the 
differential side gears (4236) in their cavities.

================================================================================

Section 07-03: Transaxle, Manual

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Bearing Cups 

Check bearing cups for scores, galling, or spalling. If the bearing 
cups are not damaged, do not remove them from the transaxle case or the 
flywheel housing. If the bearing cups must be replaced, remove and install 
them with the appropriate tools.

================================================================================

Section 07-03: Transaxle, Manual

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Bearing Cone and Roller Assemblies 

Bearing rollers must turn without roughness in their cups. Examine the 
roller ends for step wear. If inspection reveals either a damaged cup or a 
damaged cone and roller assembly, both parts must be replaced.
