DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shift Control Linkage

The Aspire automatic transaxle external controls consist of:

Shift cable and bracket (7E395)

Ignition/shifter interlock cable (3F719)

Shift lock actuator (3Z719)

Gearshift lever (7210)

Gearshift lever trunnion (7B108)

Transmission control selector dial bezel (7D443)

The basic external components required to shift the automatic transaxle 
are two levers connected by an encased cable. At the transaxle, the shift 
cable and bracket is attached to the gearshift lever trunnion by a gearshift 
cable mounting bracket (7E381) and a cotter pin. One locknut secures the shift 
cable and bracket to the driver-operated gearshift lever. Two transmission 
shift cable and bracket bolts hold the shift cable and bracket to the vehicle 
floorpan. A routing bracket secures the shift cable and bracket and directs it 
out of the engine compartment toward the gearshift lever.

Protection is provided where the shift cable and bracket extends from 
the casing to the levers to prevent the entry of contaminants. At the 
transaxle, a flexible rubber boot encloses the shift cable and bracket and the 
end of the cable casing. The bulkhead opening through which the shift cable 
and bracket enters the passenger compartment is sealed by a rubber grommet 
installed on the shift cable and bracket.

The gearshift lever is supported on bushings and a pivot bolt that 
extends through the housing and bushings. A lockwasher and nut hold the pivot 
bolt in position. As the gearshift lever pivots on the bolt, a spring and 
roller assembly stops at each gear position.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shift Interlock System

The shift interlock system consists of the following: 

Park range switch (not serviceable) 

Shift lock actuator (3Z719)

Ignition/shifter interlock cable (3F719)

Manual emergency override 

 Ignition/Shifter Interlock Cable 

[FIGURE: D9384E.gif]

Free movement into and out of specific gearshift lever (7210) positions 
is prevented by the shift interlock system. The gearshift lever cannot be 
moved from D to 2, 2 to 1, N to R, or P to R unless the shift release button 
on the gearshift lever knob is depressed. When the shift release button is 
depressed, a transmission control selector rod (7E148) extending through the 
gearshift lever pushes downward on the interlock pin. 

The downward movement of the interlock pin allows it to clear the gates 
in the interlock plate. A spring installed below the interlock pin returns the 
pin, transmission control selector rod, and button to the interlock position 
when the button is released. 

The gearshift lever cannot be moved from the PARK (P) position unless 
the ignition switch (11572) is turned to the START or ON position and the 
brake pedal (2455) is depressed.

================================================================================
PAGE 2817
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 07-05: Transaxle, Automatic — External Controls

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Manual Emergency Override Function, Shift Interlock

In the event that the shift lock actuator (3Z719) does not operate, the 
manual shift override must be activated to manually move the lock lever on the 
gearshift lever (7210).

The override function can be easily activated. Manually moving the lock 
lever on the gearshift lever will allow free movement of the gearshift lever.

[FIGURE: D12653A.gif]

To manually override the shift interlock system, refer to the following 
steps:

Verify that the gearshift lever is locked in the PARK (P) position.

Lift the override access cover.

[FIGURE: D12491B.gif]

Insert a long-tipped screwdriver into the transmission control selector 
dial bezel opening and push downward carefully to release the lock lever.

 NOTE: Mechanic's wire is meant to be used as a guide that will allow you to

 CAUTION: Be careful not to kink the ignition/shifter interlock cable. 

 NOTE: Mechanic's wire is meant to be used as a guide that will allow you to

Disconnect the two shift lock actuator electrical connectors.

 CAUTION: Do not loosen locknut "B." It is factory preset for proper shift 
interlock operation. 

Loosen the locknut "A" and remove the ignition/shifter interlock cable 
(3F719).

[FIGURE: D12441A.gif]

Remove the four gearshift lever locknuts from the gearshift lever.

[FIGURE: D12448B.gif]

 Installation 

Position the gearshift lever on the four studs on the vehicle floorpan 
and install the four gearshift lever locknuts. Tighten the four gearshift 
lever locknuts to 6-8 Nm (53-70 lb-in).

Position the ignition/shifter interlock cable in the shift interlock 
cable bracket and tighten locknut "A" to 10-15 Nm (89-132 
lb-in).

Position the shift lock actuator on the shift lock actuator bracket and 
install the two shift lock actuator screws.

Connect the two shift lock actuator electrical connectors.

Install the shift cable and bracket and the two shift cable and bracket 
bolts. Tighten the two shift cable and bracket bolts to 8-11 Nm
 (71-97 lb-in).

Install the shift cable and bracket on the gearshift lever stud and 
secure with the shift cable and bracket locknut.

Position the transmission control selector dial bezel on the gearshift 
lever. Align the holes in the slider and thetransmission control selector dial 
bezel and install an alignment pin to hold the slider in this position.

[FIGURE: D12449B.gif]

Route the transmission control selector indicator lamp wiring through 
the routing clips on the transmission control selector dial bezel. Insert the 
transmission control selector indicator lamp the lamp housing, then lock it 
into position by turning it counterclockwise.

Install the four transmission control selector dial bezel screws.

Remove the alignment pin.

Install the gearshift lever knob and the two gearshift lever knob screws.

Place the shift console panel over the gearshift lever.

Reach behind the shift console panel and connect all of the electrical 
connectors.

Install the two shift console panel screws and the two shift console 
panel fasteners. 

Position the parking brake console and install the parking brake 
console screw.

Install the console panel storage bin into the rear of the parking 
brake console.

Connect the battery ground cable.

Move the gearshift lever to PARK (P).

Install the heater core. Refer to Section 12-02 for the procedure.

Install the instrument panel. Refer to Section 01-12 for the 
installation procedure.

Place the gearshift lever in the PARK (P) position.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Transaxle, Manual — External Controls

A tubular transmission gearshift rod and clevis (7B140) connects the 
input shift shaft (7L267) at the five-speed transaxle with the floor-mounted 
gearshift lever (7210) in the passenger compartment. 

The transmission gearshift rod and clevis and gearshift lever are 
stabilized against the forward and rearward action of shifting by a gearshift 
lever stabilizer bar and support (7L257) attached to the front floor pan 
(11135) and to the transaxle. 

From the gearshift lever knob (7213), the gearshift lever extends 
downward through the gearshift lever boot (7277) which is attached to the 
shift console panel.

The gearshift lever and support housing contain the:

 Transmission gearshift lever support shaft spring (7227). 

 Gearshift control linkage lower boot (7E138). 

Bushing.

Bushing boot.

Lower gearshift lever boot (7C301). 

Gearshift lever seal (7D358). 

The gearshift lever support is attached to the front floor pan by four 
gearshift control attaching nuts (7E093).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Rod and Clevis, Gearshift

 Removal 

Raise and support the vehicle.

Remove the transmission selector shift rod adjustment sleeve (7353) and 
nut.

[FIGURE: C8040C.gif]

If necessary, remove the gearshift lever socket bushings (7335) from the 
input shift shaft (7L267).

Remove the transmission gearshift lever clamp (7K104) and nut.

[FIGURE: C8041C.gif]

Remove the gearshift selector arm bushings (7A133) from the gearshift 
lever (7210).

Remove the transmission gearshift rod and clevis (7B140).

 Installation 

Coat the inside of the gearshift selector arm bushings with a light 
film of Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C, XG-1-K, or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B and install the gearshift selector arm bushings in 
the gearshift lever.

Position the transmission gearshift rod and clevis on the gearshift 
lever. Install the transmission gearshift lever clamp. Tighten the 
transmission gearshift lever clamp nut to 16-23 Nm (12-17 
lb-ft).

Coat the inside of the gearshift lever socket bushings with a light 
film of Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C, XG-1-K, or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B and install the gearshift lever socket bushings in 
the input shift shaft.

Position the transmission gearshift rod and clevis on the input shift 
shaft. Install the transmission selector shift rod adjustment sleeve. Tighten 
the transmission selector shift rod adjustment sleeve nut to 31-46 Nm
 (23-34 lb-ft).

Lower the vehicle.

Section 07-14A: Park/Neutral Position (PNP) Switch

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Park/Neutral Position (PNP) Switch — Automatic Transaxle

The park/neutral position switch (PNP switch) (7A247):

Is safety device used in the starter interrupt system.

Allows the engine to start only in the PARK (P) or NEUTRAL (N) position.

Does not permit engine cranking in any forward or reverse gears.

Signals gear position to the powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) 
for engine idle control.

Activates the backup lamps in the REVERSE (R) position.

Is not adjustable.

Is mounted on the transaxle case.

[FIGURE: D12370A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 2845
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 07-14A: Park/Neutral Position (PNP) Switch

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Park/Neutral Position (PNP) Switch — Manual Transaxle

The park/neutral position switch (PNP switch) (7A247):

Is powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) input.

Controls idle speed when transaxle is shifted to NEUTRAL (N) position.

Is not adjustable.

Is located on the flywheel housing near the input shift shaft (7L267).

Activates the backup lamps in the REVERSE (R) position.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification — Automatic Transaxle

 NOTE: The park/neutral position switch (PNP switch) (7A247) is not used for 
the starting interrupt system on vehicles with the manual transaxle (M/T). The 
PNP switch is used by the powertrain control module (PCM) for engine control. 
Refer to the Powertrain Control Emissions Diagnosis Manual(Can be 
purchased as a separate item.) for diagnosis and testing of the PNP 
switch.

Verify the customer concern by operating either of the two systems 
causing the concern:

Starter interrupt system

Backup lamps

Visually inspect the following components of the system of concern.

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Gearshift lever binding or damaged

Gear shift lever linkage binding or damaged

Burned out light bulb

Loose or corroded connections

Damaged park/neutral position switch

Damaged starter motor

Section 07-14B: Clutch Pedal Position (CPP) Switch

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Pedal Position (CPP) Switch

The clutch pedal position switch (CPP) (11A152) is located at the top 
of the clutch pedal (7519). This CPP switch signals the powertrain control 
module (PCM) (12A650) when the clutch pedal is depressed. The PCM uses this 
information to determine if the engine (6007) is under load or not under load 
(coasting). The CPP switch is closed when the clutch pedal is depressed and 
open when the clutch pedal is at rest.

[FIGURE: D12475D.gif]

Section 07-14C: Starter Clutch Pedal Position (SCPP) Switch

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Starter Clutch Pedal Position (SCPP) Switch

The Starter Clutch Pedal Position (SCPP) switch is a safety switch that 
will not allow the engine (6007) to start or "crank" unless the clutch pedal 
is fully depressed. The SCPP switch is located on the bulkhead near the clutch 
pedal (7519). Fully depressing the clutch pedal closes the SCPP switch 
contacts, completing the starting circuit and allowing the engine to start or 
"crank."

[FIGURE: D12475D.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Starter Clutch Pedal Position (SCPP) Switch

If the vehicle does not start with the clutch pedal (7519) depressed, 
adjustment of the Starter Clutch Pedal Position (SCPP) switch may be 
necessary. 

To adjust the SCPP switch, turn the SCPP switch nuts slightly. Ensure 
the SCPP switch is properly adjusted by depressing the clutch pedal and 
attempting to start the vehicle. If the SCPP switch is properly adjusted, the 
SCPP switch will close, completing the circuit to the starter motor (11002) 
and allowing the vehicle to start.

Section 08-00: Clutch System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Before referring to the Symptom Chart in this section, try to determine 
whether the cause of the condition is the transaxle or the clutch. The vehicle 
should be road tested, if possible, to determine or confirm the condition. 
Under normal operating conditions, a large percentage of transaxle complaints 
are due to misadjusted or faulty components outside of the transaxle, such as 
the clutch, clutch linkage, and shift linkage. Before and during the road 
test, make sure that the clutch is functioning properly, the shift linkage is 
properly adjusted and that the transaxle is filled to the proper level with 
lubricant. 

If the concern is narrowed to either the clutch, clutch release cable 
(7K553), or linkage, refer to the Symptom
Chart for the description that best fits the condition. After making a repair, always road test the vehicle to 
confirm the diagnosis and repair. 

Refer to the diagnostics in Section 07-03 if the concern is caused by 
the transaxle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Dowels, Flywheel Housing to Block 

 Removal 

 NOTE: The following procedure can be used for flywheel housing to block 
dowels (6397) located either in the cylinder blocks (6010) or the flywheel 
housing.

Remove the transaxle. Refer to Section 07-03 for the removal procedure.

Flywheel housing to block dowels can be removed by using a drift pin 
where the dowel is installed in a drilled hole, and locking pliers where the 
flywheel housing to block dowel is installed in a blind hole. They should be 
pulled or driven from their seat, taking care not to damage surface area 
around the flywheel housing to block dowel during removal. 

 Installation 

Flywheel housing to block dowels can be installed by driving them into 
place using a brass or plastic hammer. Care should be exercised to drive the 
flywheel housing to block dowels squarely into place until fully seated and 
not to damage surrounding surface areas. 

Install the transaxle. Refer to Section 07-03 for the installation 
procedure.

 Pilot Bearing 

 Removal 

Remove the flywheel (6375). Refer to Section 08-01 for the removal 
procedure.

Use a suitable driver to remove the pilot bearing (7600) from the 
flywheel.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Make sure the driver contacts the bearing outer race. Any contact to 
the inner race will damage the pilot bearing. 

Install the pilot bearing using a suitable driver. 

[FIGURE: C8165A.gif]

Install the flywheel. Refer to Section 08-01 for the installation 
procedure.

Section 08-00: Clutch System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Pressure Plate 

Inspect the surface of the clutch pressure plate (7563) for burn marks, 
scores, ridges, and warpage. Clutch pressure plate resurfacing is not 
recommended, but minor burn marks or scores can be removed with crocus cloth. 
If the clutch pressure plate is badly heat checked, warped, or deeply scored, 
replace clutch pressure plate. 

 CAUTION: Do not use cleaners with a petroleum base, and do not immerse the 
clutch pressure plate in the solvent. 

Clean the clutch pressure plate and flywheel (6375) surfaces with a 
suitable solvent, such as denatured alcohol, to be sure surfaces are free from 
any oil film.

================================================================================
PAGE 2873
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 08-00: Clutch System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Disc 

Inspect the clutch disc linings for oil or grease. Eliminate the source 
of any oil or grease before replacing the clutch disc (7550). 

 CAUTION: Do not use cleaners with a petroleum base, and do NOT immerse the 
clutch disc in ANY solvents. 

Any excessive amount of lubricant on the pilot bearing (7600) or clutch 
release hub and bearing (7548) will contaminate the clutch disc linings. Too 
much lubricant in the transaxle or a plugged transaxle vent will force the 
transmission fluid out the input shaft (7017) and onto the clutch disc 
linings. Also, crankshaft rear oil seal leaks or oil leaks from the 
flywheel-to-crankshaft bolts (6379) can contaminate the clutch disc. 

Inspect the clutch disc for worn or loose linings. Check the clutch 
disc for distortion and loose rivets at the hub. Check for broken springs. 
Replace the clutch disc if any of these conditions are present. Springs loose 
enough to rattle will not cause noise when the vehicle is operating. Be 
especially careful when installing a new clutch disc to avoid dropping it or 
contaminating it with oil or grease.

Check the lining surface for hardening or the presence of oil.

 NOTE: Use emery cloth to remove minor imperfections in the clutch disc 
lining surface.

Check for worn clutch disc lining. Measure the depth to the rivet heads 
with a slide caliper. The minimum allowable depth is 0.3mm (0.012 inch).

[FIGURE: C11286A.gif]

Check for loose clutch disc lining rivets.

Check the runout of the clutch disc using Rotunda Radial Run-Out Gauge 
007-0056A or equivalent. The maximum allowable vertical runout is 1.0mm (0.039 
inch) and the maximum allowable lateral runout is 0.700mm (0.0276 inch).

[FIGURE: C11283B.gif]

Check for wear or rust on the splines and remove with an emery cloth.

[FIGURE: C7484F.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Pilot Bearing 

 Ball Type 

Check the fit and rotation of the pilot bearing (7600) in the bore of 
the flywheel (6375). Replace the pilot bearing if it is worn or damaged.

Inspect the pilot bearing for roughness, evidence of overheating, or 
loss of lubricant. Replace if any of these conditions are found.

 NOTE: Avoid using too much lubricant because it may be thrown onto the clutch 
disc (7550) when the clutch disc revolves. Install the pilot bearing with the 
shielded side of the pilot bearing toward the clutch disc.

Coat the pilot bearing bore in the flywheel with a small quantity of 
lithium base grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C, XG-1-K, or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B.

================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 08-00: Clutch System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Release Hub and Bearing 

 CAUTION: The clutch release hub and bearing (7548) is pre-lubricated and should 
not be cleaned with solvent. 

Wipe all oil and dirt off the clutch release hub and bearing. 

Hold the clutch release hub and bearing inner race and rotate the 
clutch release hub and bearing outer race while applying pressure. If rotation 
is rough or noisy, replace the clutch release hub and bearing. 

Inspect the clutch release hub and bearing for burrs which may cause 
the assembly to drag on the case bushing retainer. If burrs are found, inspect 
the case bushing retainer for evidence of scoring. Polish out burrs and 
scoring with crocus cloth. 

Apply a thin film of Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C, XG-1-K, or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to the case bushing 
retainer, both sides of the clutch release fork (7N515) where it contacts the 
clutch release hub and bearing and retaining springs, and to the clutch 
release hub and bearing surface that contacts the clutch pressure plate 
fingers. 

 CAUTION: Care must always be exercised when applying lubricants to the clutch 
release hub and bearing, and the clutch release fork, as excessive lubricant 
would contaminate the clutch disc (7550). 

 CAUTION: Misalignment between the engine (6007) and transaxle can cause case 
bushingclutch release hub and bearing wear and damage. 

Carefully fill the grease groove inside the clutch release hub and 
bearing with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C, XG-1-K, or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. Clean all excess grease from the bore of the 
clutch release hub and bearing, excess grease will be forced into the spline 
by the transaxle input shaft bearing retainer and will contaminate the clutch 
disc.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch System

The input shaft (7017) is linked to the engine (6007) through a 
mechanical clutch consisting of a Belleville spring-type clutch pressure plate 
and a 180mm (7 inch) clutch disc. After it has passed through the splines, the 
input shaft is supported in the flywheel (6375) on a small, fully sealed pilot 
bearing (7600). 

The holding force exerted by the clutch pressure plate (7563) against 
the clutch disc (7550) is released by a pedal-operated clutch release cable 
(7K553) linked to a clutch release lever (7515), clutch release fork (7N515), 
and clutch release hub and bearing (7548). 

[FIGURE: C7456C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

Flywheel Housing

6375

Flywheel

The clutch pedal (7519) is suspended with the brake pedal (2455) from a 
support bracket welded to the body. Both pedals hang from the support bracket 
on a common pivot bolt secured in position by a nut and washer.

From the top of the clutch pedal, the clutch release cable extends to a 
clutch release lever at the transaxle. The clutch system operates as follows: 

When the clutch pedal is pressed, the clutch release cable rotates the 
clutch release lever that enters the flywheel housing and connects to the 
clutch release fork. 

As the clutch release lever rotates, the clutch release fork slides the 
clutch release hub and bearing along the transaxle bearing support until it 
contacts and releases the clutch pressure plate. 

When the clutch pedal is released, springs attached to the support 
bracket and clutch release lever return the clutch release components to the 
engaged position. 

Clutch pedal free play is adjusted where the clutch release cable 
passes through the clutch release lever. A nut on the threaded end of the 
clutch release cable is used to reposition the clutch release cable connecting 
link that engages the clutch release lever. Repositioning the clutch release 
cable connecting link adjusts clutch pedal free play by lengthening or 
shortening the clutch release cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Clutch Preassembly Procedures

These procedures should be performed after component removal, and 
before installation. Refer to clutch disc (7550) and clutch pressure plate 
(7563) removal and installation procedures in this section.

Clean the flywheel housing interior with a suitable solvent.

Clean the input shaft (7017) with a wire brush and suitable solvent. 
Check condition of the input shaft. Use a stone to dull the sharp edges of the 
splines. If splines are worn excessively or notched, the clutch disc will not 
slide on the input shaft. Replace the input shaft as required.

Clean the flywheel face with denatured alcohol or a suitable solvent.

Clean the clutch release lever (7515) with a wire brush. Smooth the 
clutch release lever finger locating faces with carborundum stone and then 
clean with a suitable solvent. Apply a light coating of Premium Long-Life 
Grease XG-1-C or -K, or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to 
the clutch release lever finger ends and locating faces. If clutch release 
lever is worn or damaged, replace it.

Apply Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K, or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B to the clutch release shaft bushings (7N620) until 
clean grease appears from the two clutch release shaft bushings. Remove the 
excess grease.

If reinstalling the old clutch disc, clean the clutch pressure plate 
with denatured alcohol or a suitable solvent.

 Removal 

Remove the transaxle. Refer to Section 07-03 for the removal procedure. 

If the clutch pressure plate (7563) will be reused, paint or scribe 
alignment marks on the clutch pressure plate and flywheel (6375) for assembly 
reference.

 CAUTION: Loosen the clutch pressure plate bolts one turn at a time to release 
the clutch pressure plate spring tension evenly. Failure to release the 
tension evenly could cause distortion of the clutch pressure plate. 

 CAUTION: Do not allow oil or grease to contaminate the clutch disc facing. Even 
a trace of oil or grease may cause clutch disc (7550) grabbing or slipping. 
Handle the clutch disc by its edges and do not touch the facing. 

Use Clutch Aligner T77F-7137-A to keep clutch plate from dropping when 
the clutch pressure plate belts are removed.

Use Flywheel Holding Tool T74P-6375-A to prevent turning of the 
flywheel while loosening the six clutch pressure plate bolts. Remove the six 
clutch pressure plate bolts, the clutch pressure plate.

[FIGURE: C8162E.gif]

Remove the clutch disc and the Clutch Aligner T77F-7137-A.

[FIGURE: C8156B.gif]

 Installation 

If a new clutch disc is being installed, sand the friction surfaces on 
the clutch pressure plate. Check the flywheel and clutch pressure plate for 
wear or damage. Refer to section 08-00 for cleaning and inspection.

 NOTE: Before installing the clutch disc, make sure the correct side is facing 
the flywheel. Installation direction is correct when the damper springs face 
away from the flywheel. A new clutch disc will be stamped FLYWHEEL to indicate 
the correct installation direction. 

 NOTE: Refer to Clutch Preassembly Procedures in this section, prior to 
installing the clutch disc and clutch pressure plate.

Position the clutch disc on the flywheel and hold it in position with 
Clutch Aligner T77F-7137-A.

[FIGURE: C8156B.gif]

 NOTE: Use the marks made during removal for alignment reference. 

Position the clutch pressure plate on the flywheel and loosely install 
the six clutch pressure plate bolts. 

 NOTE: Tighten the clutch pressure plate bolts evenly and alternately to 
prevent distortion of the clutch pressure plate. 

Tighten the six clutch pressure plate bolts to 18-26 Nm
 (13-20 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C11407A.gif]

[FIGURE: C8162E.gif]

Remove the Clutch Aligner T77F-7137-A and the Flywheel Holding Tool 
T74P-6375-A.

 NOTE: Before installing the transaxle, clean the clutch disc splines on the 
input shaft (7017) and coat them with a light film of Premium Long-Life Grease 
XG-1-C or -K, or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Install the transaxle. Refer to Section 07-03 for the installation 
procedure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Ring Gear, Flywheel 

 WARNING: THIS PROCEDURE SHOULD BE PERFORMED ONLY BY A PROPERLY EQUIPPED AND 
EXPERIENCED ACETYLENE TORCH OPERATOR. TO AVOID PERSONAL INJURY, TONGS MUST BE 
USED OR ASBESTOS GLOVES MUST BE WORN WHEN HANDLING THE HEATED FLYWHEEL RING 
GEAR. 

 Removal 

Remove the flywheel (6375). Refer to the procedure in this section.

Support the flywheel on a flat and stable stand that will allow the 
flywheel ring gear (6384) to separate from the flywheel. 

Expand the flywheel ring gear by evenly heating it with an acetylene 
torch. 

Use a brass drift and hammer to drive the flywheel ring gear off the 
flywheel. Tap the flywheel ring gear evenly to prevent binding.

[FIGURE: C8168B.gif]

 Installation 

 WARNING: THIS PROCEDURE SHOULD BE PERFORMED ONLY BY A PROPERLY EQUIPPED AND 
EXPERIENCED ACETYLENE TORCH OPERATOR. TO AVOID PERSONAL INJURY, TONGS MUST BE 
USED OR ASBESTOS GLOVES MUST BE WORN WHEN HANDLING THE HEATED FLYWHEEL RING 
GEAR. 

 CAUTION: Do not heat the flywheel ring gear beyond 300°C (572°
F). Excessive heat may destroy the heat treatment the 
flywheel ring gear received during manufacture. Heat-indicating crayons, 
available from most tool suppliers, can be used to measure the temperature of 
the flywheel ring gear. At a certain temperature, the crayon will melt, 
providing an indicator that can prevent overheating of the flywheel ring gear. 

Expand the replacement flywheel ring gear by heating the flywheel ring 
gear on a flat metal surface. Keep the torch moving to prevent hot spots.

 NOTE: The bevel on the inside diameter of the flywheel ring gear must face 
the engine side of the flywheel. 

Use asbestos gloves or tongs to place the flywheel ring gear on the 
flywheel.

Use a brass drift and hammer to drive the flywheel ring gear onto the 
flywheel. Tap the flywheel ring gear evenly to prevent binding.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Pedal

The clutch pedal (7519) is suspended with the brake pedal (2455) from a 
support bracket welded to the body. Both pedals hang from the support bracket 
on a common pivot bolt secured in position by a nut and washer.

From the top of the clutch pedal, the clutch release cable (7K553) 
extends to a clutch release lever (7515) at the transaxle. The clutch system 
operates as follows: 

When the clutch pedal is pressed, the clutch release cable rotates the 
clutch release lever that enters the flywheel housing and connects to the 
clutch release fork (7N515).

As the clutch release lever rotates, the clutch release fork slides the 
clutch release hub and bearing (7548) along the transaxle bearing support 
until it contacts and releases the clutch pressure plate (7563). 

When the clutch pedal is released, springs attached to the support 
bracket and clutch release lever return the clutch release components to the 
normal position. 

Clutch pedal free play is adjusted where the clutch release cable 
passes through the clutch release lever. The clutch release cable adjuster nut 
on the threaded end of the clutch release cable is used to reposition the 
clutch release cable connecting link that engages the clutch release lever. 
Repositioning the clutch release cable connecting link adjusts clutch pedal 
free play by lengthening or shortening the clutch release cable.

ADJUSTMENTS

Clutch Pedal

 Pedal Height 

Disconnect the clutch release cable (7K553) at the clutch release lever 
(7515) to eliminate the possibility that the clutch release cable is affecting 
clutch pedal height. 

Move the floor carpet and insulation out of the way. 

Measure the distance from the upper center of the clutch pedal (7519) 
to the bulkhead. 

If the clutch pedal height measures 205mm (8.075 inches), it is within 
specification. 

If clutch pedal height is not within 205mm (8.075 inches), continue 
with adjustments. 

Inspect the clutch pedal mounting for damaged, worn, or missing parts 
and service as necessary. If no concerns are found, continue with the 
adjustments.

 NOTE: The Clutch Pedal Position Switch (CPP) (11A152) serves as the clutch 
pedal stop. 

To adjust clutch pedal height, loosen the CPP switch locknut and thread 
the CPP switch in or out until the clutch pedal is at the specified height. 
Tighten the CPP switch locknut to 14-18 Nm (10-13 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C8169D.gif]

Connect the clutch release cable to the clutch release lever and adjust 
clutch pedal free play. Refer to the procedure in this section. 

Measure clutch pedal height. If connecting the clutch release cable 
changed clutch pedal height, check the clutch release cable for binding or 
damage and service as necessary. 

 Free Play 

Carefully move the clutch pedal back and forth while measuring the 
amount of travel. 

If clutch pedal free play is 9-15mm (0.35-0.59 inch), it is within 
specification.

If clutch pedal free play is not 9-15mm (0.35-0.59 inch), continue with 
adjustments. 

[FIGURE: C8170F.gif]

While pulling back on the clutch release lever, measure the clearance 
between the clutch release lever and the clutch release cable connecting link. 
Thread the adjuster in or out until the clearance between the clutch release 
cable connecting link and the clutch release lever is 1.5-2.5mm (0.06-0.10 
inch).

[FIGURE: C8013D.gif]

Check free play at the clutch pedal. If it is not within specification, 
inspect the clutch release components for a problem.

After adjustment, ensure that when disengaged, the clutch disengagement 
height is 74mm (2.92 inches) minimum.

 Three Way Catalytic Converter (TWC) 

The three way catalytic converter (TWC) (5E212), mounted in the engine 
exhaust stream, plays a major role in the emissions control system. The engine 
exhaust consists mainly of nitrogen (N 2 ); however, it also 
contains carbon monoxide (CO), carbon dioxide (CO 2 ), water vapor (H 2 
O), oxygen (O 2 ), nitrogen oxides (NO x 
), and hydrogen (H 2 ) as well as various, unburned hydrocarbons 
(HC). Three of these exhaust components, CO, NO x , and HC are 
major air pollutants, so their emission into the atmosphere must be controlled.

The TWC works as a gas reactor to convert and reduce the pollutant 
levels to within legally prescribed limits.

The catalyst metals are thin coated onto and supported by a 
honeycomb-shaped, high-temperature ceramic, mounted inside the three way 
catalytic converter shell. The result is a highly effective converter design 
having minimum exhaust gas flow restriction and good durability.

 Precautions 

 WARNING: EXHAUST GASES CONTAIN CARBON MONOXIDE WHICH CAN BE HARMFUL TO HEALTH 
AND ARE POTENTIALLY LETHAL. EXHAUST SYSTEM LEAKS SHOULD BE REPAIRED 
IMMEDIATELY. NEVER OPERATE THE ENGINE IN ENCLOSED AREAS. 

 CAUTION: Leaded gas must not be used in a vehicle fitted with athree way 
catalytic converter, the lead will poison the catalyst. 

The following precautions must be observed when operating a vehicle 
equipped with a three way catalytic converter.

If a vehicle is continually misfueled, the lead in the fuel will be 
deposited in the three way catalytic converter and completely blanket the 
catalyst. Lead combines chemically with platinum to poison the catalyst. 
Continuous use of leaded fuels can totally destroy the catalyst, and render 
the three way catalytic converter useless. This addition of lead to the three 
way catalytic converter can also solidify the catalyst, causing excessive back 
pressure in the exhaust system, possibly causing engine damage.

Extremely high temperatures of 1100°C (2012°
F) or above, due to misfiring or over-rich fuel/air mixtures 
will cause the ceramic base to sinter or burn, destroying the three way 
catalytic converter.

The three way catalytic converter has been designed to provide a long 
service life. No maintenance is necessary for the three way catalytic 
converter; however, the following conditions must be avoided:

Driving or running the engine (6007) continuously with a misfiring 
spark plug (12405). Refer to the diagnosis section of the appropriate group 
when idling is unstable or when the engine lacks power.

Parking or stopping the vehicle over combustible material. If the 
vehicle is parked or stopped over combustible material such as dry grass, the 
material may be ignited by the high temperature of the three way catalytic 
converter and/or muffler (5230).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Exhaust Shields

 Service and/or Replacement 

Exhaust shields, consisting of formed metal sheets, attach to the 
exhaust and muffler pipes with clamps and starter shank fasteners. Exhaust 
shields are not subject to service other than removal of debris that may 
collect in the shield area. They are serviced with the muffler inlet pipe 
(5A212) or the exhaust inlet pipe (5246). The muffler shield is attached with 
bolts to the underbody above the muffler (5230). It may be serviced and/or 
replaced individually.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Verify the customer concern or complaint.

Visually inspect the components of the exhaust system.

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Exhaust pipe pinched, crushed

Damaged, loose vacuum hoses

Incorrect idle speed

Dirty air cleaner element

Damaged three way catalytic converter

Misrouted, damaged wiring

Corroded, loose connectors

 Exhaust Leakage or Noise 

At idle or during normal driving conditions, a buzz or rattle may be 
detected which can be traced to the exhaust system. This may be due to a loose 
or damaged heat shield on the exhaust pipes or on the muffler (5230). Loose or 
damaged heat shields should be repaired or replaced as soon as possible to 
maintain vehicle safety.

Damaged or deteriorated exhaust gaskets or pipes, or a damaged or 
deteriorated muffler can also be the cause of a noisy exhaust system. These 
components should be repaired or replaced when they are found to be defective 
to maintain vehicle safety.

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Exhaust System

Inspect the exhaust inlet pipe (5246), muffler inlet pipe and resonator 
(5A289),three way catalytic converter (TWC) (5E212) and muffler (5230) for 
cracked joints, broken welds, and corrosion damage that would result in a 
leaking exhaust system. Inspect the clamps, brackets, and insulators for 
cracks and stripped or badly corroded bolt threads.

================================================================================
PAGE 2923
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 09-00: Exhaust System

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Exhaust System Alignment

A misaligned exhaust system is usually indicated by vibration, 
grounding, rattling, or binding of system components. Often the associated 
noise is hard to distinguish from other chassis noises. Look for broken or 
loose clamps and brackets. Replace or tighten as necessary. It is important 
that exhaust clearances and alignment be maintained.

Perform the following procedure to align the system.

Loosen the attaching hardware, clamps, and the pipe support brackets.

Align the exhaust system, beginning at the front of the vehicle, to 
establish maximum clearance.

 NOTE: Tighten the exhaust inlet pipe nuts evenly and alternately.

Tighten all attachments.

 NOTE: Muffler (5230), three way catalytic converter (TWC) (5E212), exhaust 
inlet pipes (5246), muffler inlet pipe and resonator (5A289), brackets, 
clamps, and insulators should be replaced if they are worn or become badly 
corroded. Do not attempt to service these parts.

Start the engine (6007) and inspect the exhaust system for leaks.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Injected Engines 

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE, CARRY LIGHTED TOBACCO OR AN OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND MAY BE IGNITED, RESULTING IN POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY. 

 CAUTION: The fuel tubes leading from the fuel tank (9002) to the engine (6007) 
are under pressure during vehicle operation. When fuel injected engines are 
turned off, the fuel in the fuel tubes remains pressurized for long periods of 
time to provide quick start-ups. Special procedures for servicing these 
pressurized fuel systems are outlined in this section. 

The Aspire is equipped with a 1.3L sequential electronic fuel injection 
(SEFI) engine. The engine is fuel injected through the fuel injection supply 
manifold (9D280) to the intake port at each cylinder. The fuel system used 
with a fuel injected engine has an electric fuel pump to provide high-pressure 
fuel to the fuel injector nozzle tip.

================================================================================
PAGE 2935
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Lines and Electric Fuel Pump

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank and Fuel Tank Filler Pipe

The fuel tank (9002) is mounted on the rear underside of the vehicle. A 
fuel pump (9350) draws fuel from the fuel tank and delivers it under pressure 
through the fuel supply line and fuel filter (9155) to the fuel injectors 
(9F593). Excess fuel is routed back to the fuel tank via a fuel return line. A 
fuel evaporation pipe (9038) is routed from the fuel tank to the evaporative 
emissions canister (EVAP canister) (9D653). All lines underneath the vehicle 
run parallel along the LH side of the vehicle. A fuel pressure regulator 
(9C968), mounted at the return side of the fuel injection supply manifold 
(9D280), regulates fuel pressure. 

 Fuel System Components 

[FIGURE: V7857G.gif]

Fuel Pump and Fuel Level Sensor Assembly

All vehicles are equipped with a restricted fuel tank filler pipe 
(9034) that allows only an unleaded fuel nozzle to be inserted. The fuel tank 
holds approximately 38L (10.06 gal) of fuel. 

The restrictor consists of a narrow opening in the fuel tank filler 
pipe, covered by a spring steel trap door. The smaller unleaded fuel nozzle 
will fit through the narrow opening and push the trap door aside, allowing 
normal filling. Leaded fuel nozzles will not fit through the narrow opening. 
The closing of the trap door causes a fuel backup and automatic nozzle 
shutoff. 

The restricted fuel tank filler pipe is manufactured as an assembly and 
must be serviced by removal and replacement with a new fuel tank filler pipe. 
The fuel tank filler pipe is not to be modified in any way.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Tank Filler Cap 

 WARNING: THE FUEL TANK FILLER CAP MAY BE PRESSURIZED. TO REMOVE, ROTATE CAP OVER 
1/2 TURN COUNTERCLOCKWISE. IF FUEL TANK FILLER CAP IS VENTING FUEL OR A 
HISSING SOUND IS HEARD, WAIT UNTIL THE CONDITION STOPS BEFORE REMOVING THE 
FUEL TANK FILLER CAP. IF THESE PRECAUTIONS ARE NOT FOLLOWED, FUEL MAY SPRAY 
AND CAUSE PERSONAL INJURY. 

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE OR CARRY LIT TOBACCO OR AN OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND MAY BE IGNITED, RESULTING IN PERSONAL INJURY. 

The fuel tank filler cap (9030) is of a threaded screw-on design with a 
pre-vent feature that allows the fuel tank (9002) to vent for the first 
three-quarter turn before unthreading. All fuel tank filler caps are attached 
to the vehicle with a tether using the fuel tank filler pipe-to-housing screw 
at the three to four o'clock position. The fuel tank filler cap assembly 
provides pressure and vacuum relief functions, and should be replaced with the 
proper pressure/vacuum relief fuel tank filler cap to prevent possible system 
malfunction. 

An overfill flapper valve is located at the end of the fuel tank filler 
pipe and helps prevent fuel overflow.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Evaporative Emission Separator

Two-door models incorporate a vapor separator which is installed behind 
the LH quarter trim panel (31012), between the fuel tank (9002) and 
evaporative emissions canister (EVAP canister) (9D653) The vapor separator 
prevents liquid fuel from entering the EVAP canister while the liquid fuel is 
directed back to the fuel tank.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Evaporative Emission Valve

Two-door models also incorporate a fuel vapor valve, located behind the 
evaporative emission separator. In the case of a vehicle rollover, the 
Evaporative Emission Valve (9B593) closes, preventing any fuel from draining 
out of the fuel tank (9002) or the fuel lines.

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Lines

Fuel is drawn from the fuel tank (9002) by a fuel tank-mounted fuel 
pump. Fuel is then delivered under pressure through the fuel supply line and 
fuel filter (9155) to the fuel injection supply manifold (9D280), and then to 
the fuel injectors (9F593). Excess fuel is returned to the fuel tank through 
the fuel return line. A fuel evaporation pipe (9038) is routed from the fuel 
tank to the evaporative emissions canister (EVAP canister) (9D653). All fuel 
lines run parallel to each other underneath the LH side of the vehicle. Fuel 
pressure is controlled by a fuel pressure regulator (9C968) mounted at the 
return side of the fuel injection supply manifold.

================================================================================
PAGE 2941
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Lines and Electric Fuel Pump

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Pump, Electric 

 NOTE: On 2-door models, the fuel pump assembly housing is round-shaped and 
secured to the fuel tank (9002) with four screws. On 4-door models, the fuel 
pump assembly housing is oval-shaped and secured to the fuel tank with eight 
screws.

The fuel pump (9350) works in conjunction with the following components: 

Fuel pressure regulator (9C968)

Fuel pump relay (9345)

Inertia fuel shutoff switch (IFS switch) (9341)

 4-Door Shown, 2-Door Similar 

[FIGURE: V7879D.gif]

The fuel pump is mounted to the fuel pump assembly housing inside the 
fuel tank. The fuel pump includes a check valve located at the fuel pump 
outlet. The function of this valve is to maintain pressure in the system after 
the vehicle is shut down. The pressure retention helps prevent hot starting 
problems. A pressure relief valve is provided to regulate the maximum fuel 
pump outlet pressure. 

The fuel tank sender filter (9A011) protects the fuel pump at its 
inlet. This fuel tank sender filter strains dirt and contaminants which could 
plug or damage the internal fuel pump components.

[FIGURE: V9117A.gif]

The fuel pump relay controls fuel pump operation. The fuel pump relay 
is mounted under the LH side of the instrument panel (04320) between the 
instrument panel and the floor. The fuel pump operates only when the engine 
(6007) is cranking or running. It does not operate when the engine is not 
running, even with the ignition switch (11572) turned ON. During cranking, 
power from the ignition switch causes the fuel pump relay to close the feed 
circuit to the fuel pump.

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Pressure Regulator 

The fuel pressure regulator (9C968) is mounted on the return line end 
of the fuel injection supply manifold (9D280). The fuel pressure regulator is 
controlled by manifold vacuum and maintains fuel pressure at 210-260 kPa 
(30-38 psi). When intake manifold vacuum is low (fuel demand high), spring 
pressure inside the fuel pressure regulator causes the valve to close 
partially, which increases fuel pressure in the fuel injection supply 
manifold. When intake manifold vacuum is high (fuel demand low), vacuum acting 
on the diaphragm compresses the spring, opening the valve further. Return fuel 
flow increases, resulting in lower fuel pressure in the fuel injection supply 
manifold.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Inertia Fuel Shutoff (IFS) Switch 

 CAUTION: Inspect the fuel system for leaks before resetting the inertia fuel 
shutoff switch (IFS switch) (9341). 

An IFS switch is connected in series with the fuel pump circuit and 
will stop fuel pump operation in the event of a major collision or vehicle 
rollover. The reset button must be pushed to reset the IFS switch once it has 
been triggered.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Filling

 CAUTION: Fill the fuel tank (9002) with unleaded fuel only. Failure to do so may 
cause vehicle damage. 

The fuel tank capacity is 38L (10.06 gal). The fuel level is constantly 
measured by the fuel level sensor within the fuel tank. This amount is 
displayed on the fuel gauge (9280) (located on the instrument panel (04320)) 
whenever the key is in the ignition switch (11572) and in the ACC (I) or ON 
(II) position. The fuel gauge is divided into five increments ranging from E 
(empty) to F (full).

================================================================================
PAGE 2948
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Lines and Electric Fuel Pump

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tank — 2-Door 

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE OR CARRY LIT TOBACCO OR AN OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND MAY BE IGNITED, RESULTING IN PERSONAL INJURY. 

 Removal 

Relieve fuel system pressure. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Drain the fuel tank (9002). Refer to the procedure in this section.

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301).

Remove the rear seat cushion and cover (60030). Refer to Section 01-10 
for the removal procedure. 

Remove the LH quarter trim panel (31012). Refer to Section 01-05 for 
the removal procedure. 

Use a suitable tool to remove the three luggage compartment floor cover 
hold-down pins.

[FIGURE: R5323C.gif]

Fold the luggage compartment floor cover (45455) forward until the fuel 
pump assembly access plate is uncovered. 

Remove the fuel pump assembly access plate screws. 

Lift the fuel pump assembly access plate and disconnect the fuel pump 
assembly electrical connector. 

Disconnect the fuel supply line from the fuel level sensor. 

Disconnect the fuel return line from the top of the fuel tank. 

Remove the six inner rear floor filler cover bolts and the two inner 
rear floor filler cover nuts.

[FIGURE: V6196C.gif]

Remove the inner rear floor filler cover (10360).

Loosen the hose clamps and disconnect the fuel tank to filler pipe hose 
(9047) and the three evaporative emission hoses (9G297) from the fuel tank. 

[FIGURE: GV0226A.gif]

Disconnect the overflow hose from the fitting on the fuel tank. 

Raise and support the vehicle. 

Squeeze the hose clamp and disconnect the vapor hose from the fuel 
evaporation pipe (9038).

[FIGURE: V6186C.gif]

 NOTE: The fuel tank bolts are coated with a special thread-lock material. 
Therefore, the fuel tank bolts must be replaced with new bolts whenever removed.

Remove the four fuel tank bolts and discard. 

Move the fuel tank toward the left and remove it from under the vehicle.

 Installation 

Slide the fuel tank into position from the LH side of the vehicle. 

Install the four new fuel tank bolts. Tighten the four fuel tank bolts 
to 26-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

Connect the vapor hose to the fuel evaporation pipe. 

Lower the vehicle. 

Connect the three evaporative emission hoses to the fittings on the 
fuel tank. 

Connect the overflow hose to the fitting on the fuel tank. 

Connect the fuel tank to filler pipe hose to the fitting on the fuel 
tank. 

Connect the fuel return line to the fitting on the top of the fuel tank. 

Connect the fuel supply line to the fitting on the fuel level sensor. 

Connect the fuel pump assembly electrical connector.

Add fuel to the fuel tank. 

Perform a visual inspection for leaks and repair as necessary. 

Connect the battery ground cable. 

Start the engine (6007). Visually inspect for leaks at all locations, 
and repair leaks as necessary. 

Position the inner rear floor filler cover and install the six inner 
rear floor filler cover bolts and the two inner rear floor filler cover nuts. 

Tighten the six inner rear floor filler cover bolts and the two inner 
rear floor filler cover nuts to 10-23 Nm (8-16 lb-ft).

Position the fuel pump assembly access plate. 

Install the fuel pump assembly access plate screws. 

Position the luggage compartment floor cover and install the three 
luggage compartment floor cover hold-down pins. 

Install the LH quarter trim panel. Refer to Section 01-05 for the 
installation procedure. 

Install the rear seat cushion and cover. Refer to Section 01-10 for the 
installation procedure.

PAGE 2949
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 10-01: Fuel Tank, Filters, Lines and Electric Fuel Pump

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Tank — 4-Door

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE OR CARRY LIT TOBACCO OR AN OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN 
WORKING ON OR NEAR ANY FUEL-RELATED COMPONENT. HIGHLY FLAMMABLE MIXTURES ARE 
ALWAYS PRESENT AND MAY BE IGNITED, RESULTING IN PERSONAL INJURY. 

 Removal 

Relieve the fuel system pressure. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Drain the fuel tank (9002). Refer to the procedure in this section.

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301).

Remove the rear seat cushion and cover (60030). Refer to Section 01-10 
for the removal procedure.

Remove the LH quarter trim panel (31012). Refer to Section 01-05 for 
the removal procedure.

Use a suitable tool to remove the three luggage compartment floor cover 
hold-down pins.

[FIGURE: R5323C.gif]

Fold the luggage compartment floor cover (45455) forward until the fuel 
pump assembly access plate is uncovered.

Remove the four fuel pump assembly access plate screws.

Lift the fuel pump assembly access plate and disconnect the fuel pump 
assembly electrical connector.

Disconnect the fuel supply line from the fuel pump assembly housing.

Disconnect the fuel return line from the top of the fuel tank.

Raise and support the vehicle.

Position a jack under the fuel tank.

Loosen the two screw-type clamps and remove the fuel tank to filler 
pipe hose (9047) and the overflow hose.

[FIGURE: V9029B.gif]

Remove the two fuel tank support strap bolts and the fuel tank support 
straps (9092). Unhinge the opposite fuel tank support strap ends and remove 
the fuel tank support straps from the vehicle.

[FIGURE: V9030B.gif]

Push the brake hose clip (2814) through the bracket on the fuel tank 
and position the front parking brake cable and conduit (2853) out of the way.

Ensure that the fuel tank to filler pipe hose and the front parking 
brake cable and conduit are positioned out of the way to allow clearance for 
removal of the fuel tank.

Carefully lower the fuel tank onto the jack.

 Installation 

Position the fuel tank on the jack.

Position the front parking brake cable and conduit and install the 
brake hose clip on the bracket.

Install each fuel tank support strap end into the slot above the fuel 
tank. Secure the opposite end of each fuel tank support strap with the fuel 
tank support strap bolts.

Tighten the fuel tank support strap bolts to 44-60 Nm 
(33-44 lb-ft).

Install the fuel tank to filler pipe hose and the overflow hose on the 
fuel tank. Tighten the screw clamps.

Lower the vehicle.

Connect the fuel return line to the top of the fuel tank.

Connect the fuel supply line to the fuel pump assembly housing.

Place the fuel pump assembly access plate in the fuel tank opening and 
connect the fuel pump assembly electrical connector.

Add fuel to the fuel tank.

Perform a visual inspection for leaks and repair as necessary.

Connect the battery ground cable.

Start the engine (6007). Visually inspect for leaks at all locations, 
and repair leaks as necessary.

Install the four fuel pump assembly access plate screws.

Fold the luggage compartment floor cover back over the fuel pump 
assembly access plate.

Install the three luggage compartment floor cover hold-down pins.

Install the LH quarter trim panel. Refer to Section 01-05 for the 
installation procedure.

Install the rear seat cushion and cover. Refer to Section 01-10 for the 
installation procedure.

(33-44 lb-ft).

 Removal

Open the fuel filler door. 

Remove the fuel tank filler cap (9030).

[FIGURE: V6189D.gif]

[FIGURE: R5323C.gif]

[FIGURE: V6196C.gif]

[FIGURE: V6187C.gif]

screws.

Close the fuel filler door.

Install the screw and the ground strap wire.

Connect the overflow tube to the overflow hose and tighten the hose 
clamp.

Secure the three evaporative emission hoses to the overflow tube with 
the routing strap.

Install the fuel tank to filler pipe hose to the fuel tank filler pipe 
and tighten the hose clamp.

Install the inner rear floor filler cover.

Install the six inner rear floor filler cover bolts and two inner rear 
floor filler cover nuts.

Tighten the six inner rear floor filler cover bolts and the two inner 
rear floor filler cover nuts to 10-23 Nm (8-16 lb-ft).

Unfold the luggage compartment floor cover over the rear floor and 
insert the three luggage compartment floor cover hold-down pins.

Install the LH quarter trim panel. Refer to Section 01-05 for the 
installation procedure.

Install the rear seat cushion and cover. Refer to the procedure in 
 Section 01-10 for the installation procedure.

Connect the battery ground cable.

 Fuel Tank to Fuel Filler Pipe Hose 

 WARNING: DO NOT SMOKE OR CARRY LIT TOBACCO OR AN OPEN FLAME OF ANY TYPE WHEN

the fuel tank filler pipe.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Fuel Return System

 Removal and Installation 

The fuel return system is used to maintain fuel flow at the fuel 
charging assembly.

The fuel lines leading from the fuel tank (9002) to the engine (6007) 
are under pressure during vehicle operation. Fuel not used by the fuel 
injectors (9F593) during operation is routed back to the fuel tank through a 
fuel return line.

The fuel return system is serviced in the same manner as the fuel 
lines. Refer to the procedure in this section.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Fuel Tanks 

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY TUBES ON VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH FUEL INJECTED ENGINES WILL 
REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THE 
PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM. REFER TO FUEL 
SYSTEM PRESSURE RELIEF IN THIS SECTION. 

 CAUTION: Remove the fuel pump (9350) and the fuel level sensor prior to cleaning 
the fuel tank (9002). 

 CAUTION: Care should be exercised not to deform the plastic reservoir inside the 
fuel tank with excessively hot steam or direct contact with plastic surface. 

The fuel tank does not require special service procedures and may be 
steam-cleaned and/or serviced using standard procedures. 

After cleaning, allow the fuel tank to thoroughly air dry. The fuel 
vapor valve should be replaced. Install the fuel tank.

Fuel System Pressure Relief

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY TUBES WILL REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME

[FIGURE: A20566B.gif]

position. The fuel pressure is now relieved.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Fuel System — Pressurized 

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY LINES ON VEHICLES EQUIPPED WITH FUEL INJECTED ENGINES WILL 
REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME AFTER ENGINE SHUTDOWN. THE 
PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING THE FUEL SYSTEM. REFER TO FUEL 
SYSTEM PRESSURE RELIEF IN THIS SECTION. 

Sequential electronic fuel injection (SEFI) systems are equipped with a 
fuel pump (9350) that provides fuel to the engine (6007) at higher pressure 
than conventional fuel systems. A fuel return system is also provided. All 
fuel hose/tube connections are made with hose clamps, and all hoses are 
serviced as assemblies. The metal tubes attached to the vehicle underbody may 
be serviced. The metal underbody tubes must be cut and formed out of rolls of 
fuel system service tubing available at the dealerships. 

A damaged section of tubing can be cut out of the existing line and 
replaced with a comparable service tubing section, spliced into the line by 
means of threaded fasteners and connectors. 

All replacement hoses must be serviced as assemblies. Bulk fuel hose 
must not be used to service hoses in high pressure fuel systems. 

 Fuel Lines, Steel 

 WARNING: FUEL SUPPLY LINES WILL REMAIN PRESSURIZED FOR LONG PERIODS OF TIME 
AFTER ENGINES SHUTDOWN. THIS PRESSURE MUST BE RELIEVED BEFORE SERVICING OF THE 
FUEL SYSTEM IS BEGUN. 

 CAUTION: The use of copper tubing is not recommended due to fuel contamination. 

 Removal 

Relieve fuel system pressure. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Drain the fuel from the fuel tank (9002). Refer to the procedure in 
this section.

Disconnect the line(s) at the fuel tank and at the engine. Remove the 
lines from the holding clips along the underbody. Remove all damaged hoses and 
tube sections. 

 Installation 

Cut a new section of tubing approximately the same length as the 
section to be replaced, allowing for the threaded connectors/fasteners. 

Bend the tube section to conform to the contour of the original tube. 

Square the ends of the cut tubing with a file. Remove burrs. Blow out 
any particles with compressed air. 

Position the lines in the underbody clips. Do not tighten at this time. 

[FIGURE: V9043A.gif]

 NOTE: After disassembly of the flareless fitting joint, such as at the fuel 
hose to fuel line connection, the flareless fitting can be reassembled. To 
reassemble, reconnect the threaded fitting and seat the ferrule to be 
finger-tight. When the ferrule is seated, draw the nut up approximately 
one-sixth to one-third of a turn with a wrench to complete the tightening 
operation. 

Assemble the fitting by sliding the nut over the tubing with the 
threaded (open) end out. 

 CAUTION: Make sure that the ferrule is assembled correctly before installing it 
on the tube. 

Slide the ferrule onto the tubing with the cutting edge out; the large 
head end should be inside of the nut. 

Lubricate the ferrule and the threads on the fasteners with oil. 

Bottom the tube in the fitting, and tighten the nut until the ferrule 
just grips the tube. When the tube can no longer be turned by hand, the 
ferrule has started to grip the tube. 

After the ferrule grips the tube, tighten the nut one full turn. 

Tighten the fuel line to the underbody clips to secure the fuel lines. 

Fill the fuel tank and check for leaks.

Section 10-02: Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Accelerator Pedal and Linkage

The position of the throttle plate is regulated by the accelerator 
cable (9A758). A ferrule attached to the accelerator cable end engages the 
throttle control lever (9A776) at the throttle body (9E926). From the throttle 
control lever, the accelerator cable enters a casing that routes through the 
engine compartment to the bulkhead. At the accelerator pedal and shaft (9725), 
a plastic insert with lock tabs is used to secure the accelerator cable. 

The accelerator pedal and shaft is mounted on an accelerator shaft 
retainer (9D747) that is secured to the front floor pan (11135) with two 
bolts. A pivot pin extending through the accelerator shaft retainer provides 
the pedal pivot point. When the accelerator pedal and shaft is pressed, its 
rotation on the pivot pin pulls the accelerator cable and opens the throttle 
plate. When released, an accelerator shaft spring (9760) returns the 
accelerator pedal and shaft and throttle plate to the idle position.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

Care should be exercised when performing service on or around the 
accelerator pedal linkage and controls. Inspect the accelerator pedal rod and 
attaching linkage for damage or distortion which would bind or limit 
accelerator pedal travel. Inspect the accelerator cable (9A758) for kinks or 
fraying which may cause binding. Also, inspect the engine idle speed 
adjustment to ensure correct idle speed specification after any accelerator 
linkage adjustment or repair.

ADJUSTMENTS

Accelerator Cable

 Free Play 

Adjust the idle speed to specification. Refer to Section 03-04 for the 
removal procedure.

Measure the free play at the accelerator pedal and shaft (9725).

Free play should be 1-3mm (0.04-0.12 inch). If necessary, loosen the 
locknut and adjust at the accelerator cable bracket (9728), located near the 
throttle body (9E926).

Tighten the locknut after proper free play is achieved.

Adjust the wide open throttle position. Refer to the Wide Open Throttle 
Position Adjustment Procedure in this section.

 Deflection 

Slide the boot down to expose the accelerator cable (9A758). 

Measure the accelerator cable deflection. The deflection should be 
1-3mm (0.04-0.12 inch). 

If necessary, loosen the locknuts and adjust the accelerator cable 
tension. Tighten the locknuts after the proper deflection is achieved. 

Slide the boot up over the accelerator cable. 

Adjust the wide open throttle position. Refer to the Wide Open Throttle 
Position Adjustment Procedure in this section.

 Wide Open Throttle Position 

Adjust the accelerator cable deflection. Refer to the Accelerator Cable 
Deflection Adjustment Procedure in this section. 

Depress the accelerator pedal and shaft to the floor. 

Confirm that the throttle plate is in the wide open position in the 
throttle body. 

If necessary, loosen the kickdown switch locknut and adjust the 
kickdown switch (9E740) on the accelerator shaft retainer (9D747). 

Tighten the kickdown switch locknut after the adjustment is completed.

Section 11-00: Steering System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

The steering system has a rack and pinion design. The manual steering 
system consists of the following components:

Steering column

Steering gear (3504)

Front wheel spindle tie rods (3280)

Tie rod ends (3A130)

The power steering system, in addition to the items listed above, has a 
power steering pump (3A674), power steering pump reservoir (3E764) and 
interconnecting hydraulic tubes and hoses.

 Steering Gear Model 

The power steering gear has power steering hose connections, a power 
steering left turn pressure hose (3A714) and a power steering right turn 
pressure hose (3A717). The manual steering gear lacks all of these items.

 Power Steering Pump 

The power steering pump draws fluid from the power steering pump 
reservoir through the power steering reservoir pump hose (3691), compresses 
the fluid, and then pumps it to the power steering gear through the power 
steering pressure hose (3A719).

1997 Aspire

Section 11-00: Steering System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification

This section includes Symptom Charts and Service Procedures. The 
Symptom Charts quickly identify the possible causes of specific steering 
complaints, while the Service Procedures detail where and how to pinpoint 
steering system conditions.

Steering system complaints usually relate to excessive steering effort 
or handling problems. Excessive steering effort can be caused by: 

Underinflated tires 

Worn or damaged suspension components 

Excessive friction in the steering linkage, caused by: 

Improper lubrication 

Damaged seals allowing moisture and contaminants to enter 

Improper adjustment of steering system components 

Handling problems include the following: 

Pulls to one side or wanders 

Failure to return to the straight ahead position when the steering 
wheel (3600) is released 

Loose feeling in steering 

All of these can be attributed to problems in the: 

Steering column

Steering gear (3504) 

Power steering pump (3A674) 

Suspension components 

Wheels (1007) and tires 

Refer to Section 04-00 for diagnosis of handling problems caused by 
suspension system components.

For steering column concerns, perform the following inspection:

Verify the customer concern by road testing the vehicle to duplicate 
the concern.

Visually inspect the following components of the steering column.

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Binding steering column shrouds

Steering system concern

Loose fittings

None

If fault is not visually evident, determine the symptom and proceed to 
the Symptom Chart.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Preliminary Procedures

 Air Bleeding 

Refer to Purging Power Steering System of Air in this section.

 Fluid Level 

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the steering system, do not keep the steering 
wheel in a fully turned position for more than 10 seconds. 

Start the engine (6007) and let it run until it reaches normal 
operating temperature.

While the engine idles, turn the steering wheel (3600) fully right and 
left several times.

Turn the engine off with the wheels (1007) in the straight ahead 
position. Check the fluid level in the power steering pump reservoir (3E764). 
The fluid level should be between the LOW and HIGH marks on the dipstick.

If the fluid level is low, add an approved power steering fluid until 
the fluid level is between the LOW and HIGH marks on the dipstick.

 Pump Belt 

Refer to Section 03-05 for the service procedures.

Section 11-00: Steering System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Turning Effort Check

 Power Steering 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spring Scale

T74P-3504-Y

Insert a thermometer into the power steering pump reservoir (3E764).

 CAUTION: Do not hold the steering wheel (3600) against a stop for more than 10 
seconds at a time. 

Start the engine (6007), then turn the steering wheel left and right 
several times until the fluid temperature reaches 50-60°C 
(122-140°F). 

With the vehicle on a hard, level surface, turn the steering wheel 
until the wheels are in the straight ahead position. 

 NOTE: For accurate readings, always pull the scale in the direction the point 
of the scale attachment is moving (at right angle to radius) through the full 
circle. 

Attach Spring Scale T74P-3504-Y to the steering wheel rim and measure 
the steering effort through one full turn of the steering wheel. The steering 
wheel effort should be 39 N (8.8 lbs) or less.

[FIGURE: G8210A.gif]

If the effort is greater than the specification, check for low fluid 
level, air in the system, and fluid leakage. Check the power steering pump 
(3A674) pressure, steering gear pressure and tire pressure. 

Remove the thermometer. 

 Manual Steering 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Spring Scale

T74P-3504-Y

Raise the wheels clear off the floor and position jack stands under the 
front suspension lower arm (3078), as close to the wheels as possible without 
interfering with steering travel. 

Turn the steering wheel stop-to-stop at least five times to free up any 
stickiness resulting from front suspension components being out of their 
normal riding positions, and then place the wheels in the straight ahead 
position. 

 NOTE: For accurate readings, always pull the scale in the direction the point 
of scale attachment is moving (at right angle to radius) through the full 
circle. 

Attach Spring Scale T74P-3504-Y to the steering wheel rim and measure 
the steering effort through one full turn of the steering wheel.

Steering effort should be approximately 5-20 N (1.0-4.5 lbs) through a 
full revolution in either direction from the straight ahead position. 

If effort is excessive, check for binding or damage in the front 
suspension and the steering linkage components. Check for excessive steering 
gear (3504) preload as outlined in Section 11-01 .

Section 11-00: Steering System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

External Leakage

Check for an overfilled power steering pump reservoir (3E764). Siphon 
off the excess fluid if necessary.

Check for power steering pump overflow or aeration.

Wipe the suspected area dry and check for the exact source of the leak. 
Oil may be running down from another area (other than the power steering 
system) and causing an oil drip.

 CAUTION: Do not hold the steering wheel against a stop for more than 10 seconds 
at a time. 

Some leaks are high-pressure leaks and may require holding the steering 
wheel (3600) for no more than ten seconds against the stop to permit oil to 
seep out. Cycle the steering wheel from stop to stop ten times to check for 
leaks. The rubber boots may have to be moved back from the steering gear 
housing to see the leak.

 System Back-Pressure 

 CAUTION: Make sure that the power steering system analyzer valve is open to

 CAUTION: Do not hold the steering wheel (3600) against a stop for more than 10

Bleed the system using the following procedure: 

Check the fluid level in the power steering pump reservoir, and add

to read the operating pressure. Do not leave the valve closed for more than 10 
seconds.

the Rotunda Power Steering Analyzer 014-00207 or equivalent and increasing the 
engine speed to 1000-1500 rpm. The pressure specification is 7358-7848 kPa 
(1067-1138 psi). 

If the pressure is within specification, continue with the remaining 
test procedures. 

If the pressure is low, repair or replace the power steering pump. If 
the pressure is too high, check for a crimped pipe and repair/replace as 
necessary, or replace the power steering pump. Refer to Section 11-02 for the 
procedure.

 NOTE: The vehicle must be connected to the Rotunda Power Steering Analyzer 
014-00207 and Adapter Fittings 014-00460 or equivalents and the power steering 
system must be bled before performing this procedure.

With the valve of the Rotunda Power Steering Analyzer 014-00207 or 
equivalent open, increase the engine speed to 1000-1500 rpm.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Steering Wheel Free Play

With the ignition OFF and the wheels in the straight ahead position, 
turn the steering wheel (3600) left and right until wheel resistance is felt. 
Free play should not exceed 30mm (1.2 inches) at the wheel rim. Excessive free 
play indicates wear in the steering column intermediate shaft coupling 
(3A525), worn front wheel spindle tie rod (3280), or improper steering gear 
(3504) preload. To check the steering column intermediate shaft coupling, grip 
or feel the lower joint at the floorboard and repeat the free play check. Any 
free play between the steering wheel and the lower joint at the floorboard, 
which is clamped to the steering column, is in the steering column assembly.

[FIGURE: G8211B.gif]

Check the front wheel spindle tie rod by raising both wheels off the 
floor. Check each wheel for wobble. First, check the wheels vertically to 
verify that outer and inner front wheel bearings are correctly adjusted; then, 
check the wheels horizontally while an assistant grips the steering column 
intermediate shaft coupling from inside the vehicle. If horizontal wobble is 
present, check the tie rod end (3A130) for free play or loose attachment to the 
front wheel knuckle (3K186). If no free play is detected at the tie rod end, 
any horizontal steering wheel wobble must be the result of worn front wheel 
spindle tie rod, ball joints, or excessive gear free play between steering 
gear and steering column. In either case the steering gear must be removed and 
adjusted, repaired, or replaced to correct the condition. Refer to Section 11-02 for the procedures.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Steering Column Bearing

When checking steering wheel free play, also check for radial play or 
wobble between the steering wheel (3600) and steering column. Any free play 
detected reflects wear in the steering column bearings, and can add to 
apparent free play. Refer to Section 11-04 for the steering column replacement 
procedure.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Steering Linkage 

The presence of water or foreign matter inside the front suspension 
steering ball stud dust seals (3332) and the steering column tube boot (3C611) 
can seriously impair operation and durability of the steering gear (3504) and 
front wheel spindle tie rod (3280). The front suspension steering ball stud 
dust seals and the steering column tube boot must be installed carefully to 
avoid twisting, distortion, and rubbing against other components. When 
installing the front suspension steering ball stud dust seals, always use new 
steering ball stud dust seal clamps. When investigating steering concerns, 
inspect the front suspension steering ball stud dust seals and the steering 
column tube boot for cracks, cuts, abrasion, and make sure the steering ball 
stud dust seal clamps are tight.

Section 11-00: Steering System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Steering Gear Mount 

[FIGURE: G6114C.gif]

The steering gear (3504) is mounted on the engine compartment bulkhead 
with steering gear insulators (3C716) and steering gear brackets. The steering 
gear insulators permit limited lateral movement of the steering gear housing 
(3548) when the vehicle is steered. Check for movement with the front wheels 
normally loaded (on the ground). If the housing moves more than 1.5mm (1/16 
inch), the steering gear insulators may have deteriorated or the steering gear 
brackets may be loose. Steering gear bracket bolts should be tightened to 
37-52 Nm (27-38 lb-ft). If the housing movement is still 
excessive after tightening the steering gear bracket, replace the steering 
gear insulators.
