SERVICE PROCEDURES

Steering Gear Bushing/Preload

[FIGURE: G6115B.gif]

Sideways play of the steering gear sector shaft in the steering gear 
housing (3548) or excessive steering rack-to-power steering gear input shaft 
(worm gear) backlash can cause a variety of steering concerns. To check 
steering gear sector shaft play, try to move the inboard ends of the front 
wheel spindle tie rod (3280) up and down, and back and forth, as illustrated. 
Any free play detected at the right end of the steering gear (3504) is 
indicative of a worn steering gear sector shaft bearing, which must be 
replaced. Free play at the left end indicates wear or insufficient preload at 
the support yoke, which may be adjustable. In either case, the steering gear 
must be removed for repair. Refer to Section 11-02 for the procedure.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Purging Power Steering System of Air

Check, and if necessary, fill the power steering pump reservoir (3E764) 
with Premium Power Steering Fluid E6AZ-19582-AA or equivalent meeting Ford

Turn the ignition key to the ON position.

times with the engine (6007) not running.

Recheck the fluid level. If it has dropped, add fluid.

 CAUTION: Do not hold the steering wheel against a stop for more than 10 seconds 
at a time.

Verify that the fluid is not foamy and that the fluid level has not 
dropped.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Fill Procedure

 Initial Fill 

Place the front wheels in the straight ahead position. Do not turn the 
steering wheel (3600) during initial fill.

Fill the power steering pump reservoir (3E764) to the FULL mark with 
fresh fluid.

Disconnect the distributor electrical connectors.

Crank the engine for 5-10 seconds. Do not allow the power steering pump 
reservoir to empty while cranking.

Recheck and refill the power steering pump reservoir after cranking. 
Repeat the procedure until the fluid level in the power steering pump 
reservoir remains constant.

Connect the distributor electrical connectors.

 Final Fill 

Start the engine (6007) and allow it to run for several minutes.

Rotate the steering wheel fully left and right from stop to stop.

Turn off the engine and check the fluid level in the power steering 
pump reservoir. Add fluid if necessary.

Purge the system of air if there is noise and aeration. Refer to the 
procedure in this section.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Steering Pump, Power

When replacing or removing the power steering pump (3A674), one of the 
two following procedures must be followed. If no jack or hoist is available to 
raise the front wheels, use Procedure No. 1. If front wheels can be safely 
raised off the ground, use Procedure No. 2.

 Procedure No. 1 

The replacement power steering pump must be primed with the specified 
power steering fluid prior to installation in the vehicle.

Remove the fitting from the pressure port and pour power steering fluid 
into the pressure port with the port facing upward to maximize the amount of 
fluid added to the power steering pump.

Turn the pump driveshaft slowly and continue to add fluid.

Install the power steering pump in the vehicle in a manner that does 
not allow the fluid to escape from the power steering pump.

Attach the power steering lines to the power steering pump and power 
steering pump reservoir (3E764).

Fill the power steering pump reservoir to the proper level.

Start the engine (6007) and allow it to run for several minutes.

 CAUTION: Do not hold the steering wheel (3600) against a stop for more than 10 
seconds at a time. 

Rotate the steering wheel fully left and right, from stop to stop 
several times.

Turn off the engine and check the fluid level in the power steering 
pump reservoir. Add fluid if necessary.

 Procedure No. 2 

Install the unprimed replacement power steering pump in the vehicle.

Attach the power steering lines to the power steering pump and the 
power steering pump reservoir.

Fill the power steering pump reservoir to the proper level.

Purge the power steering system of air. Refer to the procedure in this 
section.

Section 11-00: Steering System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Pump, Power

 Flushing 

When contamination is noted while overhauling the steering gear (3504), 
it will be necessary to flush the power steering pump (3A674). 

Leave all hoses connected, except the power steering pressure hose 
(3A719) at the steering gear. 

Place the power steering pressure hose in a suitable container. 

Fill the power steering pump reservoir (3E764) with Premium Power 
Steering Fluid E6AZ-19582-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESW-M2C33-F. 

Disconnect the distributor electrical connectors to prevent the engine 
(6007) from starting. 

While approximately 2 liters (2 quarts) of the power steering fluid are 
being poured into the power steering pump reservoir, engage the starter motor 
(11002). 

As soon as all the fluid has been poured in, turn off the ignition. 

Attach the power steering pressure hose at the steering gear. Tighten 
the power steering pressure hose-to-steering gear fitting to 16-23 Nm
 (12-17 lb-ft).

Check the reservoir fluid level. 

Crank the engine with the starter motor and continue adding fluid until 
the level remains constant. Connect the distributor electrical connectors. 

Start the engine and cycle the steering wheel (3600) from stop to stop 
to expel any air from the system.

 Cleaning 

Wash all parts except seals in a chlorinated solvent and dry with 
compressed air. 

 Inspection 

To determine when to replace power steering pump components, follow 
these guidelines. Some components must be replaced regardless of condition. 

Reuse the power steering return hose fitting if the corners are not 
rounded and the threads are intact. 

Replace all of the O-rings. 

Reuse the rotor and cam assembly if wear is limited to removal of the 
phosphate coating on the cam contour. Do not disassemble the unit. Push the 
rotor part way through the cam insert, being careful not to dislodge the 
vanes. Check the cam inside diameter for scoring or burring. Check the rotor 
faces and outside diameter for scoring and chipping. Do not repair or refinish 
the cam or rotor assembly. If wear or burring is evident, replace the cam and 
rotor assembly with new components. 

Install a new rotor and cam assembly if the vanes are worn. 

Reuse the housing if all the threaded holes are not damaged beyond 
repair. Repair the threaded holes by drilling out the damaged threads and 
installing helicoil inserts. 

Reuse the control valve if the valve bore is free of nicks and scoring 
and the valve screen is clean. The valve must fall freely in the valve bore. 
Replace the housing and/or valve if the valve sticks in the bore.

PAGE 2999
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 11-00: Steering System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Gear 

 Cleaning 

Disassembly and assembly of the steering gear (3504) and sub-assemblies 
must be made on a clean workbench. As in repairing any hydraulically operated 
unit, cleanliness is important. 

 CAUTION: Do not clean, wash, or soak seals in the cleaning solvent. 

Keep the bench, tools, and parts clean at all times. 

Thoroughly clean the exterior of the unit with a suitable solvent and, 
when necessary, drain as much of the hydraulic fluid (or gear grease) as 
possible. 

Handle all of the parts very carefully to avoid nicks, burrs, scratches 
and dirt, which could make the parts unfit for use. 

 Inspection 

Check the input shaft (worm gear) and bearings for damage. Replace them 
if necessary. 

Inspect the input shaft (worm gear) housing for scoring or burrs. 

Inspect the tube seats (if equipped) in the pressure and return ports 
in the steering gear housing (3548). If nicks, etc., are present, replace the 
tube seats. 

Check all fluid passages for obstruction or leakage. 

Inspect the steering gear housing for cracks and stripped threads, and 
inspect mating surfaces for burrs. Inspect the piston bore of the steering 
gear housing for scoring. Check the roller bearing for damage. If necessary, 
replace the steering gear housing. 

Check the input shaft (worm gear) bearings after input shaft (worm 
gear) installation to be sure that they rotate without binding or roughness. 

Check the input shaft (worm gear) and steering gear sector shaft teeth 
for nicks and burrs. 

 Flushing 

Flushing the steering gear is required when installing a repaired power 
steering pump (3A674). 

Install the new pump and connect only the power steering pressure hose 
(3A719) to the power steering pump. 

Place the power steering return hose (3A713) from the steering gear in 
a suitable container and plug the reservoir return tube. 

Fill the power steering pump reservoir (3E764) with Premium Power 
Steering Fluid E6AZ-19582-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESW-M2C33-F. 

Disconnect the distributor electrical connectors to prevent the engine 
(6007) from starting and raise the front wheels off the ground. 

 CAUTION: Do not crank the engine for more than 10 seconds because the battery 
(10655) will be drained and the starter motor (11002) damaged. 

While approximately 2L (2 quarts) of power steering fluid are being 
poured into the power steering pump reservoir, crank the engine. At the same 
time, cycle the steering wheel (3600) from stop to stop. Do not hold the 
steering wheel against a stop for more than three to five seconds at a time. 

As soon as all of the fluid has been poured in, turn the ignition key 
off, and connect the distributor electrical connector. 

Remove the plug from the reservoir return tube, and attach the power 
steering return hose to the power steering pump reservoir. 

Check the reservoir fluid level, and, if necessary, add fluid to the 
proper level. 

Lower the vehicle. 

 CAUTION: Do not hold the steering wheel against a stop for more than 10 seconds 
at a time. 

Start the engine and cycle the steering wheel from stop to stop to 
expel any trapped air from the system.

LUBRICATION

Lubrication Schedule, Manual Steering Gear

The steering gear (3504) is factory-filled with steering gear 
lubricant. Seasonal change of this lubricant should not be performed and the 
housing should not be drained. No lubricant is required for the life of the 
steering gear unless leakage is noted or service is performed.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Gear

The manual rack-and-pinion steering gear is sealed against the entry of 
water or foreign matter by two bellows and by a steering column tube boot 
(3C611) surrounding the steering column intermediate shaft coupling (3A525). 
The steering gear is lubricated at assembly and must be removed and 
disassembled if relubrication becomes necessary. 

The steering gear sector shaft (3575) is positioned and guided into the 
housing by the steering gear housing sector shaft bushing (3576) at the right 
end and a support yoke holding it in engagement with the steering gear input 
worm gear and rack (3524) at the left end. The support yoke is spring-loaded 
against the steering gear sector shaft. A yoke plug and yoke locking nut 
(3F606) keep the steering gear sector shaft fully engaged with the steering 
gear input worm gear and rack under load. 

Rubber insulators at each end of the steering gear housing (3548) 
cushion the steering gear mounting points and minimize vibration. Looseness of 
the mounts or deterioration of the insulators can cause noise and vibration 
problems. These should be checked when investigating for such concerns.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Gear 

 Removal 

Mark the lower steering column shaft (3B676) and steering column 
intermediate shaft coupling (3A525) to ensure correct assembly. 

Remove the steering column and lower steering column shaft. Refer to 
 Section 11-04 for the removal procedure. 

Remove the floor set plate bolts and the floor set plate.

Cut and discard the plastic tie strap securing the steering column tube 
boot (3C611) to the steering gear housing (3548). 

Raise and support the vehicle. 

Remove both front wheel and tire assemblies. 

Remove the tie rod ends (3A130). Refer to the procedure in this section.

Remove the three way catalytic converter (TWC) (5E212). Refer to 
 Section 09-00 for the removal procedure.

Remove the plastic front splash shield (16A324) from the right front 
fender (16006).

 NOTE: While moving the steering gear assembly in and out of the inner fender 
openings, guide the steering gear assembly carefully to avoid cutting or 
nicking the bellows.

Remove the steering gear bolts and lower the steering gear assembly 
until it is free of the steering column tube boot. 

Slide the steering gear assembly to the right, through the inner fender 
opening until the left front wheel spindle tie rod (3280) is clear of the left 
inner fender. 

Lower the left end until the steering gear assembly can be withdrawn 
from the left side. 

[FIGURE: GG0247A.gif]

Remove the steering column gear intermediate shaft coupling bolt and the 
steering column intermediate shaft coupling from the steering gear input worm 
gear and rack (3524).

 Installation 

Install the steering column intermediate shaft coupling and steering 
column gear intermediate shaft coupling bolt on the steering gear input worm 
gear and rack. Tighten the steering column gear input shaft coupling bolt to 
18-26 Nm (13-20 lb-ft).

Insert the right front wheel spindle tie rod through the right inner 
fender opening, far enough to insert the left end of the steering gear 
assembly into the left front fender opening. Shift the steering gear assembly 
to the left, being careful not to snag the bellows.

Align the steering column intermediate shaft coupling with the steering 
column tube boot and raise the steering gear assembly into engagement with the 
bulkhead.

Install the steering gear bolts, first at the left steering gear 
mounting bracket (3E552) and then at the right. Tighten the steering gear 
bolts to 37-52 Nm (27-38 lb-ft). 

Install the tie rod ends. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Install the right front splash shield on the right front fender. 

Install the three way catalytic converter. Refer to Section 09-00 for 
the installation procedure. 

Install the wheel and tire assemblies. Tighten the lug bolts (1107) to 
88-118 Nm (65-87 lb-ft).

Lower the vehicle.

Secure the steering column tube boot to the steering gear housing with 
a new plastic tie strap. 

Install the floor set plate and floor set plate bolts.

Align the index marks on the lower steering column shaft and the 
steering column intermediate shaft coupling.

Install the steering column and lower steering column shaft. Refer to 
 Section 11-04 for the installation procedure.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

 Removal 

Raise and support the vehicle.

Remove the wheel and tire assembly. 

Remove and discard the tie rod end cotter pin.

[FIGURE: G8225E.gif]

Remove the tie rod end nut.

[FIGURE: G8226D.gif]

Use Tie Rod End Separator T85M-3395-A to separate the tie rod end 
(3A130) from the front wheel knuckle (3K185). 

[FIGURE: G8227B.gif]

Place alignment marks on the tie rod end, the tie rod end jam nut, and 
the front wheel spindle tie rod (3280).

[FIGURE: G6084E.gif]

Loosen the tie rod end jam nut and unscrew the tie rod end and the tie 
rod end jam nut.

 Installation 

Thread the tie rod end jam nut and the tie rod end onto the front wheel 
spindle tie rod and align the index marks. 

If installing a new tie rod end, match the position of the old one as 
closely as possible. Tighten the tie rod end jam nut to 34-50 Nm
 (25-36 lb-ft). The tie rod end jam nut may not seat in the 
same alignment with a new tie rod end.

 NOTE: If the tie rod end is correctly aligned, the taper will seat without 
twisting the front wheel spindle tie rod or the tie rod end boot. 

Install the tie rod end into the front wheel knuckle.

Install the tie rod end nut. Tighten the tie rod end nut to 42-57 Nm
 (31-42 lb-ft). 

Install a new tie rod end cotter pin. If necessary, tighten the tie rod 
end nut until the castellations line up with the pin bore. 

Install the wheel and tire assembly. Tighten the lug bolts (1107) to 
88-118 Nm (65-87 lb-ft).

Lower the vehicle.

Check the toe. Refer to the procedure in Section 04-00 .

 Disassembly 

Remove the steering gear. Refer to the procedure in this section. 

Remove the steering gear mounting brackets (3E552) and rubber steering 
gear insulators (3C716) from the steering gear.

Mark and remove the tie rod ends (3A130) and the bellows. Refer to the 
procedure in this section. 

 CAUTION: Use a vise equipped with soft jaw caps to avoid damaging the steering 
gear sector shaft (3575). 

Extend the steering gear sector shaft from either end of the steering 
gear housing (3548) to permit gripping it in the vise. Remove the front wheel 
spindle tie rods (3280).

[FIGURE: G6077E.gif]

Remove the yoke locking nut (3F606) from the yoke plug. 

Remove the yoke plug, spring and support yoke. 

 NOTE: Be careful not to score the steering gear input worm gear and rack 
(3524). 

Use a screwdriver or suitable tool to pry the oil seal out of the 
steering gear housing. 

[FIGURE: G6078E.gif]

Remove the spacer.

Use snap ring pliers to remove the snap ring. 

[FIGURE: G6079B.gif]

Pull the steering gear input worm gear and rack out from the top of the 
steering gear housing. If necessary, use Valve Body Puller T78P-3504-B and 
Valve Body Puller Bridge T86P-3504-D.

 CAUTION: If the steering gear sector shaft is removed or installed through the 
steering gear housing sector shaft bushing (3576) at the right end of the 
steering gear housing, the steering gear sector shaft teeth may damage the 
steering gear housing sector shaft bushing. 

Remove the steering gear sector shaft by pulling it out from the left 
end of the steering gear housing.

[FIGURE: G6080E.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not remove the steering gear housing sector shaft bushing unless it 
is necessary. 

 CAUTION: Do not damage the steering gear housing while removing the steering 
gear housing sector shaft bushing. 

To remove the steering gear housing sector shaft bushing from the right 
end of the steering gear housing, press the steering gear housing sector shaft 
bushing lock tabs in at the three lock slots in the steering gear housing. 
Pull the steering gear housing sector shaft bushing out with Collet D80L-100-L 
(part of D80L-100-A) or equivalent and Impact Slide Hammer T50T-100-A.

[FIGURE: G6097C.gif]

Before assembling the steering gear, inspect the components. Refer to 
the procedures in this section.

 Assembly 

Clean all of the parts. 

Lubricate the steering gear sector shaft teeth, steering gear input 
worm gear and rack teeth, upper and lower steering gear input worm gear and 
rack bearings, and steering gear housing with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life 
Grease XG-1-C, -K, or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B, as 
shown.

[FIGURE: G6101D.gif]

 NOTE: Be careful not to plug the steering gear sector shaft vent holes with 
grease. 

Lubricate the oil seal lips, the support yoke, and the steering gear 
sector shaft. 

Lubricate the steering gear housing sector shaft bushing with 
lithium-based grease and install it in the right end of the steering gear 
housing, engaging the lock tabs with the lock slots.

[FIGURE: G6102D.gif]

Install the steering gear sector shaft from the left end of the 
steering gear housing, with the steering gear sector shaft teeth facing the 
steering gear input worm gear and rack bore. Position the steering gear sector 
shaft with the left end extending 62mm (2.4 inches) from the end of the 
steering gear housing.

[FIGURE: G6103D.gif]

 NOTE: The helical cut of the steering gear input worm gear and rack teeth 
will cause counterclockwise rotation of the steering gear input worm gear and 
rack as it engages with the steering gear sector shaft. 

Install the steering gear input worm gear and rack so that when the 
bearing is seated, the clamp bolt notch faces 45 degrees ± 
10 degrees forward (clockwise) from the left, as seen from the top (steering 
gear input worm gear and rack shaft end) of the steering gear housing, with the 
steering gear sector shaft centered. 

Install the snap ring with the beveled side up (toward the oil seal). 
Install the spacer tab-side down, locating the tab in the snap ring gap.

[FIGURE: G6104B.gif]

Bearing

Wrap the steering gear input worm gear and rack serrations with plastic 
electrical tape to protect the oil seal lips, and apply a thin coat of grease 
to the tape. Install the oil seal over the steering gear input worm gear and 
rack, seating it in the housing with Pinion Seal Replacer/Torque Adapter 
T87C-3504-C. Remove the protective tape.

[FIGURE: G6090B.gif]

Install the front wheel spindle tie rods. Grip the steering gear sector 
shaft in a vise equipped with protective jaw caps. Tighten the front wheel 
spindle tie rods to 11-13 Nm (97-115 lb-in).

Install the bellows and tie rod ends. Refer to the procedure in this 
section. 

Center the steering gear sector shaft so that the front wheel spindle 
tie rods are equally extended.

Grease the support yoke and install it in the steering gear housing.

Install the spring. 

Apply sealant to the yoke plug threads. Install the yoke plug. Tighten 
the yoke plug to 9-11 Nm (78-95 lb-in). 

Slowly cycle the steering gear sector shaft back and forth five times 
through 90 percent of its full stroke. Then center the steering gear sector 
shaft so that the front wheel spindle tie rods are equally extended. 

Loosen the yoke plug. Tighten the yoke plug to 2.5-3.4 Nm
 (22-30 lb-in).

[FIGURE: G6109B.gif]

Use Spring Scale T74P-3504-Y to measure the force needed to turn the 
steering gear input worm gear and rack 180 degrees (one half of a complete 
circle) from the steering gear sector shaft center position.

[FIGURE: G7032B.gif]

Adjust the steering gear input worm gear and rack to the position where 
the most turning force was needed.

Tighten the yoke plug to 5.4 Nm (48 lb-in), and then 
back it off 5-35 degrees.

[FIGURE: G6109B.gif]

 NOTE: Tighten the yoke locking nut to the specified torque without moving the 
yoke plug.

Install the yoke locking nut. Tighten the yoke locking nut to 39-49 Nm
 (29-36 lb-ft).

ADJUSTMENTS

Inspection 

Inspect the steering gear sector shaft teeth and steering gear input 
worm gear and rack teeth for unusual wear or damage. If any defects are found, 
replace both steering gear sector shaft (3575) and steering gear input worm 
gear and rack (3524). Check the steering gear housing (3548) for cracks, 
dents, or abnormal wear.

[FIGURE: G6100E.gif]

Rotate the steering gear sector shaft in V-blocks, while checking for 
runout at the center with Dial Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or 
equivalent. If runout exceeds 0.3 mm (0.0118 in), the steering gear sector 
shaft should be replaced.

[FIGURE: G6098G.gif]

Check the steering gear input worm gear and rack bearings for looseness 
or rough operation. If the steering gear input worm gear and rack upper 
bearing is defective, replace the bearing and steering gear input worm gear 
and rack as an assembly. 

Check the fit of the steering gear housing sector shaft bushing (3576) 
on the steering gear sector shaft. If loose or abnormally worn, replace the 
steering gear housing sector shaft bushing. 

Verify that the front wheel spindle tie rods (3280) flex freely through 
their normal operating angles, but are not loose at any angle. Check front 
wheel spindle tie rods for straightness, and tie rod ends (3A130) for free 
flexing without looseness.

[FIGURE: G6099C.gif]

Check the bellows for cuts, nicks, or abrasion. If damaged, replace.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering System, Power

The power steering system consists of:

Rack and pinion steering gear

Power steering pump (3A674)

Power steering pump reservoir (3E764)

Interconnecting power steering hoses

================================================================================
PAGE 3016
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Pump

The power steering pump (3A674) is mounted on the front of the engine 
(6007). The power steering pump has a vane-type design and is driven by the 
crankshaft (6303) through a drive belt (8620).

Power steering fluid is drawn into the power steering pump from the 
power steering pump reservoir (3E764) when the engine is running. Fluid is 
pressurized by the rotation of the rotor and vanes, then sent to the steering 
gear (3504). Fluid pressure is monitored and regulated by a power steering 
pressure switch (PSP switch) (3N824) and a power steering pump valve located 
in the power steering pump.

================================================================================
PAGE 3017
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Gear

The power steering gear input shaft and control (3D517) is a one-piece 
unit. It is the only valve assembly serviced within the steering gear housing 
(3548). A flexible retaining wire encircles the steering gear sector shaft 
bushing. This wire can be removed and installed through a slot in the steering 
gear housing. Lockpins secure the front wheel spindle tie rods (3280) to the 
steering gear sector shaft (3575) and replace the tab washers on many of the 
steering systems.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hydraulic Operation

The power steering pump (3A674), which is driven by the crankshaft 
(6303) through a drive belt (8620) and pulleys, develops the hydraulic 
pressure necessary to operate the system. When the steering wheel (3600) is 
turned, the steering gear (3504) converts this hydraulic pressure and flow 
into mechanical motion that will move the front wheels in the direction of the 
turn. 

Fluid is drawn into the vane type power steering pump from the power 
steering pump reservoir (3E764) when the engine (6007) is running.

================================================================================
PAGE 3019
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Pressure Relief Valve Operation

The fluid is pressurized by the rotation of the rotor and vanes and 
forced into the steering gear (3504). Power steering pump output pressure is 
regulated by a power steering pump pressure relief valve located in the power 
steering pump housing.

================================================================================
PAGE 3020
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Steering Pressure (PSP) Switch

The power steering pressure switch (PSP switch) (3N824) is normally 
closed. As power steering load increase, the PSP switch opens and increases 
the idle speed. For a functional check of the PSP switch operation, refer to 
the procedure in this section.

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Pump, Power

 Removal 

Disconnect thebattery ground cable (14301). 

Remove the air cleaner intake tube (9C675) and the engine air cleaner 
(ACL) (9600). Refer to Section 03-12 for the procedure.

Disconnect the power steering pressure (PSP) switch electrical 
connector from the PSP switch.

Disconnect and plug the power steering reservoir pump hose (3691).

Remove the power steering pressure hose nut and the power steering 
pressure hose retainer bracket bolt and then disconnect the power steering 
pressure hose (3A719) from the power steering pump (3A674) and the power 
steering pump support (3C511). Plug the power steering pressure hose.

[FIGURE: G8214C.gif]

Loosen the power steering pump adjustment locknut and the power 
steering pump adjustment bolt.

[FIGURE: G8216B.gif]

Remove the two power steering pump-to-power steering pump support bolts.

Remove the drive belt (8620).

Remove the tensioner bolt.

[FIGURE: G8217A.gif]

Section 11-02: Steering System, Power

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Power Steering Pressure (PSP) Switch 

 Leak Check 

The power steering pressure switch (PSP switch) (3N824) uses an O-ring 
seal. If a leak occurs, check that the PSP switch is properly tightened to 
25-29 Nm (18-22 lb-ft). If the leak continues, replace the 
O-ring and then the PSP switch.

 Functional Check 

Check operation of the PSP switch if either or both of the following 
conditions are noted:

Engine (6007) stalls during parking maneuvers.

Engine idles at high speed.

Disconnect the PSP switch electrical connector from the PSP switch.

Connect a continuity tester, Rotunda 73 Digital Multimeter 105-R0051 or 
equivalent, between the PSP switch terminal and ground.

Start the engine and let it idle.

The PSP switch should normally be open (infinite ohms) with the 
steering wheel straight ahead.

Turn the steering wheel (3600) toward either stop while watching the 
continuity tester. The PSP switch should close near the stops (zero ohms).

If the PSP switch fails either test, replace the PSP switch. Refer to 
the procedure in this section.

If the PSP switch is OK, check engine idle speed. Refer to Section 03-04 for the procedure.

Install the spring. 

Apply sealant to the yoke plug threads and yoke locking nut.

Install the yoke plug.

[FIGURE: G7523A.gif]

lb-in). Scribe the steering gear housing (3548) at the 0 degree mark of the 
Yoke Plug Torque Gauge T90C-3504-CH. Loosen the yoke plug until the 67°

rotating torque.

49-59 Nm (36-43 lb-ft).

Valve Housing Adjustment 

 NOTE: Perform this adjustment if the power steering gear actuator housing 
(3E564), steering gear housing (3548), or power steering gear input shaft and 
control (3D517) have been replaced. 

Measure the power steering gear actuator housing, power steering gear 
input shaft and control lower bearing and spacer, and steering gear housing as 
shown in the following illustration.

[FIGURE: G7048C.gif]

Item

Steering Gear Sector Shaft Housing Oil Seal

Power Steering Gear Actuator Housing

Use the following formula to determine the proper shim thickness:

T = A + C - B

where T is the shim thickness.

Having calculated the proper shim thickness, use the following formula 
to determine the number of shims to use.

0.05mm (0.0020 inch) shims are available.

N = T / 0.05mm (0.0020 inch)

where N is the number of shims to use. Always round up or down to the 
closest full number.

For example:

If T was determined to be 0.17mm:

N = 0.17mm / 0.05mm = 3.4 shims.

3.4 shims rounded to the nearest whole number = 3 shims.

Three shims would be used.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Column

The steering assembly consists of the following components: 

Steering wheel (3600). 

Steering column. 

Upper steering column support bracket. 

Lower steering column support bracket. 

Lower steering column shaft (3B676). 

Steering column intermediate shaft coupling (3A525). 

Steering gear (3504). 

The steering column shroud (3530) houses the multi-function switch 
(13K359) and the ignition switch (11572).

The upper steering column support bracket is secured to the instrument 
panel crossmember by two bolts. 

The steering column connects the steering wheel and the lower steering 
column shaft. 

The lower steering column shaft is connected to the steering gear by the 
steering column intermediate shaft coupling. 

The lower steering column support bracket is attached to the pedal 
support bracket with two nuts.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Column with Air Bag

The steering column supports the driver side air bag module (043B13). 
The driver side air bag module is designed to minimize driver injury in an 
accident when used with a safety belt. An air bag sliding contact (14A664) at 
the base of the steering wheel (3600) transfers electrical signals to the 
driver side air bag module mounted in the center of the steering wheel.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Column Lock

The steering column lock helps to prevent vehicle theft. To lock the 
steering column, turn the ignition switch (11572) to the LOCK position. The 
ignition switch must be in the LOCK position to remove the key.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Wheel with Air Bag

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Steering Wheel Puller

T67L-3600-A

 Removal 

Center the front wheels to the straight ahead position.

 WARNING: THE ELECTRICAL CIRCUIT NECESSARY FOR DRIVER SIDE AIR BAG MODULE 
DEPLOYMENT IS POWERED DIRECTLY BY THE BATTERY. TO AVOID ACCIDENTAL DEPLOYMENT 
AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY, THE BATTERY GROUND CABLE MUST BE DISCONNECTED 
PRIOR TO SERVICING OR REPLACING ANY DRIVER SIDE AIR BAG MODULE SYSTEM 
COMPONENTS. 

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301) and wait 1 minute for the 
backup power supply to be depleted.

Remove the four driver side air bag module bolts and lift the driver 
side air bag module (043B13) off of the steering wheel (3600).

[FIGURE: G8262B.gif]

Disconnect the two driver side air bag module electrical connectors.

Make an alignment mark on the steering wheel and the steering column 
shaft for proper installation.

Remove the steering wheel nut.

[FIGURE: G8263A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to remove the steering wheel by hitting the steering 
column shaft with a hammer. The steering column shaft will collapse causing 
the steering wheel to bind. 

Use Steering Wheel Puller T67L-3600-A to remove the steering wheel. 
Route the wiring harness through the steering wheel as the steering wheel is 
lifted off of the steering column shaft.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: If the air bag sliding contact (14A664) has been accidentally rotated, 
the air bag sliding contact alignment must be adjusted. Refer to the procedure 
in this section. 

To install, reverse the removal procedure, aligning the index marks on 
the steering wheel and steering column shaft.

Tighten the steering wheel nut to 39-49 Nm (29-36 
lb-ft).

Tighten the driver side air bag module bolts to 4-6 Nm 
(36-53 lb-in).

Sliding Contact, Air Bag

 Removal

Steering Column 

 Fixed 

 Removal

 (13-20 lb-ft).

 (12-17 lb-ft).

Section 11-04: Steering Column

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Column 

Check the length of the steering column shaft to be sure it has not 
been partially collapsed by a previous impact. It should measure 598.1mm (23.6 
inches). 

[FIGURE: G8387A.gif]

Check for side play of the steering column shaft in the steering column 
bearings. Any detectable side play can adversely affect steering control. If 
the side play is in excess of 0.75mm (0.03 inch), serious bearing wear is 
indicated, and the steering column should be replaced.

Section 11-05: Steering Column Switches

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Multi-Function Switch

The multi-function switch (13K359) is mounted on the steering column 
and controls the following components: 

Headlamps (13008)

Parking lamps (13200), tail lamps and marker lamps

Flash-to-pass switch

High/low-beam lamps

Turn signal lamps

Hazard/flasher lamps

Windshield washer/wiper 

Rear window washer/wiper 

[FIGURE: J5321B.gif]

The windshield wipers are controlled by the wiper control lever, which 
is integral with the multi-function switch. The wiper control lever is located 
on the right side of the multi-function switch. To operate the windshield 
wipers, the ignition switch (11572) must be in the ACC or ON position. The 
windshield wipers have three fixed positions: OFF, LO and HI.

Some vehicles are equipped with optional intermittent windshield 
wipers. If the INT position is chosen, the windshield wipers will cycle at 
10-second intervals.

The windshield washer pump (17664) is controlled by the wiper control 
lever, an integral part of the multi-function switch. To operate the 
windshield washer pump, the ignition switch must be in either the ACC or ON 
position. To turn on the windshield washer pump, pull the wiper control lever 
toward the steering column. Release the lever to turn the windshield washer 
pump off. The windshield wipers will operate for a few wipes and return to 
their previous setting (OFF, HI, LO, or INT). Windshield washer pump operation 
is available in all positions of windshield wiper operation.

The high-beams and the flash-to-pass feature are controlled by the turn 
signal lever, which is integral with the multi-function switch. To activate 
the high-beams, move the turn signal lever away from the driver to the stop 
position. Releasing the turn signal lever in this position will maintain 
high-beam operation. To return to low-beams, move the turn signal lever back 
to its normal position.

To operate the flash-to-pass feature, pull the turn signal lever gently 
toward the driver. When the turn signal lever is released, the headlamps will 
return to the low-beams. When driving without the headlamps on, the 
flash-to-pass feature will automatically turn on the high-beams until the turn 
signal lever is released.

The rear window wiper is controlled by the dial on the end of the wiper 
control lever, an integral part of the multi-function switch. To operate the 
rear window wiper, the ignition switch must be in the ACC or ON position. The 
rear window wiper switch has only two positions: OFF and ON. To operate the 
rear window wiper, rotate the dial away from the driver. Rotate the dial 
toward the driver to stop the rear window wiper.

The rear window washer is controlled by the dial on the end of the 
wiper control lever, which is integral with the multi-function switch. To 
operate the rear window washer, the ignition switch may be in either the ACC 
or ON position. To operate the rear window washer with the rear window wiper 
in the ON position, rotate the dial away from the driver. To operate the rear 
window washer with the rear window wiper in the OFF position, rotate the dial 
toward the driver. The rear window wiper will automatically run for a few 
wipes and then shut off.

The turn signals are controlled by the turn signal lever which is an 
integral part of the multi-function switch. The turn signal lever is mounted 
on the left side of the multi-function switch. To operate the turn signals, the 
ignition switch must be in the ON position. To indicate a full turn, move the 
turn signal lever to the end-of-travel position for the desired turn. The turn 
signal lever will remain in this position until the turn is complete. The 
steering wheel cancel cam automatically releases the turn signal lever.

The turn signal system also has a lane change feature. To operate the 
lane change feature, hold the turn signal lever in the first position when 
changing lanes. When the lane change is complete, release the turn signal 
lever and it will return to its original position.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition Switch

The ignition switch (11572) is located in the lock cylinder housing 
which is clamped to the steering column. The ignition switch is concealed 
beneath the steering column shrouds (3530) and is secured to the lock cylinder 
housing with a single screw. 

[FIGURE: J5614A.gif]

The ignition switch is a rotary type switch operated directly by the 
ignition key lock cylinder. A plastic lug on the end of the lock cylinder 
engages a matching slot on the switch contact plate. When the ignition key is 
turned to the ACC, ON, or START position, rotation of the contact plate will 
connect various circuits to battery voltage. In the ACC position, accessories 
such as the radio chassis (18806) and cigar lighter knob and element (15052) 
are energized. In the ON position, the circuits required to operate the 
vehicle are energized. In the START position, the starter solenoid (11390) 
receives voltage, closing the contacts to energize the starter circuit which 
allows the starter motor (11002) to crank the engine (6007).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hazard Flasher Switch

 NOTE: The turn signal system is deactivated when the hazard flasher system is 
on. Turn signal and windshield wiper switch motion does not affect the hazard 
flasher system.

The hazard flasher switch is an integral part of the multi-function 
switch (13K359). The hazard flasher system operates independently from the 
ignition switch (11572). All turn signal lamps will flash in unison when the 
hazard flasher switch is pressed and released. The hazard flasher switch is 
located on the top portion of the steering column shroud (3530). It is 
identified by the "double triangle" symbol. In the on position, the hazard 
flasher switch will move out and away from the steering column. The hazard 
flasher system is turned off by pushing the hazard flasher switch, then 
releasing it. The hazard flasher switch remains in or toward the steering 
column while it is in the off position.

Flasher, Indicator

The indicator flasher (13350) is located to the left and below the

hazard flasher switch to complete their circuits and flash intermittently. 
When the turn signal switch is closed, the contacts connect either the left or 
the right turn signal and hazard circuits to the indicator flasher. When the 
hazard flasher switch is closed, the contacts connect all four lamps to the 
indicator flasher.

BASIC PRINCIPLES

Heat Transfer 

If two substances of different temperature are placed near each other, 
the heat in the warmer substance will always travel to the colder substance 
until both are of equal temperature. 

In order to determine the amount of heat that transfers from one 
substance to another, science has established a definitive standard of 
measurement called the British Thermal Unit, or BTU. One BTU is the amount of 
heat required to raise the temperature of one pound of water 0.55°
C (1°F). 

For example, to raise the temperature of one pound of water from 0°
C (32°F) to 100°C (212°
F), one BTU of heat must be added for each 0.55°
C (1°F) rise in temperature, or a total of 
180 BTUs of heat. Conversely, in order to lower the temperature of one pound 
of water from 100°C (212°F) to 0°
C (32°F), 180 BTUs of heat must be removed 
from the water.

================================================================================
PAGE 3086
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 12-00: Climate Control System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

BASIC PRINCIPLES

Latent Heat of Vaporization 

When a liquid boils (changes to a gas), it absorbs heat without raising 
the temperature of the resulting gas. When the gas condenses (changes back to 
a liquid), it gives off heat without lowering the temperature of the resulting 
liquid. 

For example, place one pound of water at 0°C (32°
F) in a container over a flame. With each BTU of heat that 
the water absorbs from the flame, its temperature rises 0.55°
C (1°F). Thus, after it has absorbed 180 BTUs of heat, the 
water reaches a temperature of 100°C (212°
F). Even though the flame continues to give its heat to the water, the 
temperature of the water remains at 100°C (212°
F). The water, however, starts to boil or change from the 
liquid to the gaseous state and it continues to boil until it is passed off 
into the atmosphere as vapor. 

If this vapor was collected in a container and checked with a 
thermometer, it also would show a temperature of 100°C (212°
F). In other words, there was a rise of only 100°
C (180°F) from 0°-100°
C (32°-212°F) in the water 
and vapor temperature, even though the flame applied many more than 180 BTUs 
of heat. In this case, the heat is absorbed by the liquid in the process of 
boiling and disappears in the vapor. If the vapor was brought into contact 
with cool air, the hidden heat would reappear and flow into the cooler air as 
the vapor condensed back to water. Scientists refer to this natural law as the 
latent (hidden) heat of vaporization. 

Water has a latent heat of vaporization of 970 BTUs and a boiling point 
of 100°C (212°F). This means that one pound 
of water at 100°C (212°F) will absorb 970 
BTUs of heat in changing to vapor at 100°C (212°
F). Conversely, the vapor will give off 970 BTUs of heat in 
condensing back to water. The tremendous heat transfer that occurs when a 
liquid boils or a vapor condenses is an important factor for all conventional 
refrigeration systems.

For a liquid to be a good refrigerant, it must also have a low boiling 
point. That is, the temperature at which it boils must be lower than the 
substance to be cooled. 

In order to make practical use of the heat transfer that takes place 
when a liquid boils, we must choose a liquid with a low boiling point. 
Refrigerant 134a is used in automotive air conditioning systems because it 
boils at -29.85°C (-21.7°F) in an open 
container. Here is a liquid that boils or vaporizes well below passenger 
compartment temperatures and, in vaporizing, will absorb tremendous amounts of 
heat without getting any warmer.

================================================================================
PAGE 3087
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 12-00: Climate Control System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

BASIC PRINCIPLES

Effect of Pressure on Boiling or Condensation 

The saturation temperature is the temperature when boiling or 
condensation of a liquid or vapor occurs. The saturation temperature of a 
liquid or vapor increases or decreases according to the pressure exerted on 
it. 

In an expansion valve refrigerant system, liquid refrigerant R-134a is 
stored in the A/C condenser core (19712) under high pressure. When the liquid 
R-134a is released into the A/C evaporator core (19860) by the A/C evaporator 
expansion valve (19849), the resulting decrease in pressure and partial 
boiling lowers the temperature of the R-134a to its new boiling point. As the 
R-134a flows through the A/C evaporator core, air passes over the outside 
surface of the evaporator coils. As it boils, the R-134a absorbs heat from the 
air and thus cools the passenger compartment. The heat from the passenger 
compartment is absorbed by the boiling refrigerant and held as latent heat in 
the vapor. The refrigeration cycle is now under way. The following steps 
complete the cycle: 

Dispose of the heat in the vapor. 

Convert the vapor back to liquid for reuse. 

Return the liquid to the starting point in the refrigeration cycle. 

The A/C compressor (19703) and the A/C condenser core perform these 
functions. The A/C compressor pumps the refrigerant vapor (containing the 
latent heat) out of the A/C evaporator core, then forces it under high 
pressure into the A/C condenser core, which is located in the outside 
airstream at the front of the vehicle. The increased pressure in the A/C 
condenser core raises the R-134a condensation or saturation temperature to a 
point higher than that of the outside air. As the heat transfers from the hot 
vapor to the cooler air, the R-134a condenses back to a liquid. 

The high pressure liquid then passes through the suction 
accumulator/drier (19C836) to the A/C evaporator expansion valve. The A/C 
evaporator expansion valve meters the refrigerant into the A/C evaporator 
core, and the refrigeration cycle begins again.

It may be difficult to understand how heat can be transferred from a 
comparatively cooler passenger compartment to the hot outside air. The answer 
lies in the difference between the refrigerant pressure that exists in the A/C 
evaporator core and the pressure that exists in the A/C condenser core. In the 
A/C evaporator core, the A/C compressor suction reduces the pressure and the 
boiling point below the temperature of the passenger compartment. Heat 
therefore transfers from the passenger compartment to the boiling refrigerant. 
In the A/C condenser core, the A/C compressor raises the condensation point 
above the temperature of the outside air. Thus, the heat transfers from the 
condensing refrigerant to the outside air. The A/C evaporator expansion valve 
and the A/C compressor simply create pressure conditions that permit the laws 
of nature to function.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Climate Control System Service

Prompted by environmental concerns, Ford Motor Company is now producing 
vehicles equipped with non-chlorofluorocarbon (non-CFC) air conditioning 
systems. The new refrigerant used is R-134a, a hydrofluorocarbon that has no 
chlorine molecule, which destroys the atmosphere's ozone layer. R-134a will 
eventually replace R-12 as the refrigerant for all Ford climate control 
systems. R-134a systems function in the same manner as R-12 systems except for 
minimal operating pressure differences and component variations.

Aspire vehicles use the new R-134a A/C system. This system uses 
different components, refrigerant, and refrigerant oil than the traditional 
Ford R-12 A/C systems used in previous years.

It is important to understand that R-134a and R-12 air conditioning 
systems are not entirely the same. They have components that are slightly 
different from one another and in some cases service requirements are also 
different. However, the most important thing to understand is that R-134a 
refrigerant, refrigerant oil, and components can only be used on R-134a 
systems while R-12 refrigerant, refrigerant oil, and components can be used 
only on R-12 systems. While these two types of A/C systems operate and 
function in a nearly identical manner, the refrigerant, refrigerant oil, and 
components used in these systems are not compatible.

Also, R-134a systems require the use of dedicated special service tools 
and equipment. R-134a special service tools and equipment that come in contact 
with the R-134a refrigerant or refrigerant oil can only be used on R-134a A/C 
systems. R-12 special service tools and equipment cannot be used on R-134a A/C 
systems and vice versa.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Precautions

 WARNING: AVOID BREATHING A/C REFRIGERANT AND LUBRICANT VAPOR OR MIST. IF 
ACCIDENTAL SYSTEM DISCHARGE OCCURS, VENTILATE THE WORK AREA BEFORE RESUMING 
SERVICE. 

 WARNING: WEAR IMPERVIOUS GLOVES AND SAFETY GOGGLES AT ALL TIMES WHEN HANDLING 
LIQUID REFRIGERANT. SHOULD ANY LIQUID REFRIGERANT GET INTO THE EYES OR ON THE 
SKIN, IMMEDIATELY FLUSH EYES AND SKIN WITH PLENTY OF WATER FOR AT LEAST 15 
MINUTES. REMOVE CONTAMINATED CLOTHING AND SHOES. CALL A PHYSICIAN. 

 WARNING: REFRIGERANT HFC-134A IS ALWAYS UNDER PRESSURE. BECAUSE THE SYSTEM IS 
TIGHTLY SEALED, HEAT APPLIED TO ANY PART COULD CAUSE THIS PRESSURE TO BUILD UP 
EXCESSIVELY. TO AVOID A DANGEROUS EXPLOSION, KEEP AWAY FROM OPEN FLAMES, 
GLOWING METAL SURFACES, BLOW TORCH, STEAM CLEANING AND WELDING. HFC-134A CAN 
BE DECOMPOSED AT HIGH TEMPERATURES. 

 WARNING: ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GOGGLES WHEN SERVICING ANY PART OF THE REFRIGERANT 
SYSTEM. 

 WARNING: EXTREME CARE MUST BE TAKEN TO PREVENT ANY LIQUID REFRIGERANT FROM 
COMING IN CONTACT WITH THE SKIN, AND ESPECIALLY THE EYES. 

 CAUTION: Using R-12 components, refrigerant or refrigerant oil on an R-134a 
system will cause damage to the A/C system. Do not replace components, 
refrigerant, or refrigerant oil from an R-134a system with components, 
refrigerant, or refrigerant oil for an R-12 system or vice versa. R-12 and 
R-134a components are not interchangeable. Mixing components from these two 
types of systems will cause component failure and damage to the A/C system. 

 CAUTION: The refrigerant used in this refrigerant system is HFC-134a 
(Tetrafluoroethane) which is a hydrofluorocarbon refrigerant. HFC-134a, is 
also known as R-134a is non-corrosive, non-explosive, non-flammable and has 
slight ethereal type odor. HFC-134a is heavier than air. Although it is 
classified as a safe refrigerant, certain precautions must be observed to 
protect the parts involved and the person working on the unit. 

 CAUTION: Use only R-134a refrigerant. Due to environmental concerns, when the 
air conditioning system is drained, the refrigerant must be collected using 
refrigerant recovery/recycling equipment meeting SAE standards J1990 and 
J2210. HFC-134a must never be removed without the appropriate equipment or 
release into the atmosphere. Use of a recovery machine dedicated for R-134a is 
necessary to reduce the possibility of oil and refrigerant incompatibility 
concerns. Refer to the instructions provided by the equipment manufacturer 
when removing refrigerant from or installing refrigerant into the air 
conditioning system. 

 CAUTION: Liquid R-134a, at normal atmospheric pressures and temperatures, 
evaporates so quickly that it has a tendency to freeze anything it contacts. 
Extreme care must be taken to prevent any liquid refrigerant from coming in 
contact with the skin and especially the eyes. 

 CAUTION: Ensure that refrigerant containers are never heated to over 52°
C (125°F). Refrigerant containers should be 
stored and installed in accordance with all state and local ordinances. 

 CAUTION: When admitting R-134a into the refrigerant system, always keep the tank 
in an upright position. If the tank is on its side or upside down, liquid 
R-134a will enter the system and may damage the A/C compressor. 

 CAUTION: Refrigerant R-134a should not be mixed with air for leak testing or 
used with air for any other purpose above atmospheric pressure. R-134a is 
combustible when mixed with high concentrations of air and high pressures.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Service Precautions 

 Never open or loosen a connection before discharging the 
system with a recycling machine such as the Rotunda R-134a A/C Service Center 
176-00001 or the Rotunda R-134a Mobile Recycling Center 023-00150 or equivalent. 

 When loosening a connection, allow any residual pressure 
to leak off before opening the fitting. 

 A system which has been opened for replacement of a 
component, or which has discharged through leakage, must be evacuated before 
charging. 

 Immediately after disconnecting a component from the 
system, seal open fittings with a cap or plug. 

 Before disconnecting a component from the system, clean 
the outside of the fittings thoroughly. 

 Do not remove sealing caps from a replacement component 
until it is ready to be installed. 

 Refrigerant oil will absorb moisture from the atmosphere 
if left uncapped. Do not open an oil container until ready to use, and install 
the cap immediately after using. Store oil only in a clean, moisture-free 
container. 

 Before connecting an open fitting, always install a new 
O-ring seal. Coat the fitting and O-ring seal with refrigerant oil before 
making the connection. 

 When installing a refrigerant line, avoid sharp bends. 
Position the line away from the exhaust or any sharp edges which may chafe the 
line. 

 Do not open a refrigerant system or uncap a replacement 
component unless it is close to room temperature. This will prevent 
condensation from forming inside a component which is cooler than the 
surrounding air. Whenever a major component such as an A/C evaporator core 
(19860), A/C condenser core (19712), A/C compressor (19703), or refrigerant 
line is replaced, it is mandatory that the suction accumulator/drier (19C836) 
also be replaced. 

 Keep service tools and work area clean. Contamination of 
a refrigerant system through careless work habits must be avoided. 

 Whenever components in the engine compartment or instrument panel 
areas are being serviced, the battery ground cable (14301) must be 
disconnected to eliminate the possibility of electrical shorts, burnt wiring, 
and dangerous fires. Extreme care must be exercised when performing electrical 
tests where the battery (10655) must be connected to operate the system.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Refrigerant System Operation

The air conditioning system consists of: 

A/C compressor (19703)

A/C condenser core (19712)

A/C condenser cooling fan (19A805)

suction accumulator/drier (19C836)

A/C evaporator core (19860)

A/C condenser fan switch

A/C pressure cut-off switch

A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat (19618)

A/C evaporator expansion valve (19849)

Evaporator to compressor suction line (19867)

A/C compressor to condenser discharge line (19972)

Climate control assembly

The Aspire uses an expansion valve type of refrigerant control system. 
The refrigerant cycle is controlled by an A/C evaporator expansion valve 
mounted inside the A/C evaporator case. The A/C evaporator expansion valve 
senses A/C evaporator core temperature and opens or closes slightly to control 
the amount of refrigerant circulating through the A/C evaporator core and A/C 
compressor.

 Refrigerant Flow 

The A/C compressor pulls in low-pressure vapor and pumps out 
high-pressure vapor to the A/C condenser core. The high-pressure vapor 
entering the A/C condenser core is cooled by outside air passing over the A/C 
condenser core cooling fins. This heat loss causes the high-pressure vapor to 
become high-pressure liquid. The high-pressure liquid passes through the 
suction accumulator/drier before entering the A/C evaporator expansion valve. 
The A/C evaporator expansion valve controls the amount of refrigerant entering 
the A/C evaporator core where hot, humid air passes over the A/C evaporator 
core coils. The A/C evaporator core coils remove the heat and humidity from 
the air being circulated in the passenger compartment. When the low-pressure 
liquid absorbs the heat in the A/C evaporator core, it again becomes a 
low-pressure gas. The low-pressure gas then returns to the A/C compressor.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Compressor and A/C Clutch Assemblies

The A/C compressor (19703) is a rotary vane design and is belt driven 
by the engine crankshaft (6303). An A/C compressor clutch drives the A/C 
compressor shaft. When voltage is applied to the A/C compressor clutch field 
coil, the A/C clutch hub is drawn by magnetic force toward the A/C compressor 
clutch pulley, which rotates freely on the A/C compressor. The magnetic force 
locks the A/C clutch hub to the A/C compressor clutch pulley to turn the A/C 
compressor shaft. When voltage is removed from the A/C compressor clutch field 
coil, the A/C clutch hub moves away from the A/C compressor clutch pulley and 
the A/C compressor shaft ceases to rotate.

[FIGURE: L9250B.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Refrigerant System Protection

 A/C Compressor Pressure Relief Valve 

 The A/C compressor (19703) features a pressure relief valve which will 
discharge high pressure refrigerant to the atmosphere when the pressure 
exceeds its relief setting of 3626-4413 kPa (526-640 psi). The A/C compressor 
pressure relief valve will reseal itself when the pressure drops below its 
reset setting of 3206 kPa (465 psi).

 A/C Pressure Cut-Off Switch 

The A/C pressure cut-off switch is a safety device that shuts the A/C 
compressor clutch off if the pressure on the discharge side of the A/C 
compressor (19703) (at the suction accumulator/drier (19C836)) drops below 
201-241 kPa (29-35 psi) or is above 2940-3332 kPa (426-483 psi). The A/C 
pressure cut-off switch is wired in series with the A/C switch and the A/C 
evaporator temperature control thermostat (19618).

[FIGURE: L9247C.gif]

 Thermal Protection Switch 

A thermo protection switch is mounted in the A/C compressor to protect 
the A/C compressor from overheating. The thermal protection switch will open 
the A/C compressor clutch field coil circuit if the A/C compressor gets too hot.

[FIGURE: L9222D.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Condenser Core

The A/C condenser core (19712) is an aluminum fin and tube design heat 
exchanger located in front of the vehicle radiator (8005). The A/C condenser 
core cools compressed refrigerant gas by allowing air to pass over fins and 
tubes to extract heat and condenses the gas refrigerant to liquid as it cools.

[FIGURE: GL0887A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Evaporator Core

The A/C evaporator core (19860) is located in the evaporator housing 
under the RH side of the instrument panel (04320). It is a multi-pass 
plate/fin type design mounted in a vertical position. Vapor feed refrigerant 
enters the A/C evaporator core from the A/C evaporator expansion valve (19849) 
and cools the evaporator fins. Forced air from the blower motor (18527) 
passing through the A/C evaporator core is cooled and dehumidified, then 
conducted to the passenger compartment. Excess moisture from the 
dehumidification process is drained through an A/C evaporator drain hose 
(19858) to the outside of the vehicle.

[FIGURE: L9240A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Evaporator Expansion Valve 

The A/C evaporator expansion valve (19849) is located on the A/C 
evaporator inlet. The A/C evaporator expansion valve senses the temperature 
and pressure of the refrigerant at the A/C evaporator outlet and meters the 
refrigerant into the A/C evaporator core (19860). Liquid refrigerant must not 
be allowed to pass into the A/C compressor (19703) or serious damage can 
result. The A/C evaporator expansion valve is a control device that controls 
the amount of high-pressure refrigerant that enters the A/C evaporator core. 
The proper amount of refrigerant allows maximum cooling and provides for 
complete evaporation of all the liquid refrigerant in the A/C evaporator core.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Evaporator Temperature Control Thermostat

The A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat (19618) is a safety 
device which shuts the A/C compressor clutch off to prevent the A/C evaporator 
core (19860) from freezing. When the temperature of the A/C evaporator core 
drops to 0° ± 1°C (32°
 ± 1.8°F) the A/C 
evaporator temperature control thermostat turns the A/C compressor clutch off. 
When the A/C evaporator core temperature increases to 3°-5°
C (37.4°-41.0°F) the A/C 
evaporator temperature control thermostat turns the A/C compressor clutch on. 
An A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat sensing bulb inside of the 
A/C evaporator core signals the A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat 
when to open or close. The A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat is 
wired in series with the A/C clutch control relay (19D572) and signals the 
powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) to turn the A/C compressor clutch on 
and off. 

The A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat is located at the top 
of the A/C evaporator upper case (19C974) directly beneath the glove 
compartment (06010).

[FIGURE: L9241B.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Condenser Fan Switch

 NOTE: The A/C condenser cooling fan (19A805) does not operate whenever the 
A/C compressor (19703) is engaged. The operation of the A/C condenser cooling 
fan is controlled by the A/C condenser fan switch.

The A/C condenser fan switch is located on the outlet manifold of the 
A/C condenser core (19712). When manifold pressure exceeds 1,519 kPa (220 
psi), the A/C condenser fan switch closes and the A/C condenser cooling fan 
starts to operate. When manifold pressure drops below 1,225 kPa (178 psi), the 
A/C condenser fan switch opens and the A/C condenser cooling fan turns off.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suction Accumulator/Drier

 NOTE: Replacement of the suction accumulator/drier is not required
when repairing the air conditioning system except when there is
physical evidence of system contamination from a failed A/C
compressor or damage to the suction accumulator/drier.

The suction accumulator/drier (19C836) collects moisture in the 
refrigerant that was generated during condensation. It prevents the moisture 
from recirculating through the system. 

Refrigerant enters the suction accumulator/drier from the jumper line 
through the inlet tube. The heavier, oil-laden refrigerant falls to the bottom 
of the outlet tube near the bottom of the suction accumulator/drier. A bleed 
hole, covered with a filter screen, allows a small amount of the heavier 
liquid refrigerant and oil mixture to re-enter the liquid line at a controlled 
rate. When the heavier liquid refrigerant and oil mixture enters the liquid 
line, it has an opportunity to vaporize and circulate through the A/C 
evaporator core (19860) and A/C compressor (19703) without causing damage to 
the A/C compressor due to refrigerant slugging. 

A desiccant bag is mounted inside the suction accumulator/drier to 
absorb any moisture which may be in the refrigerant system. A sight glass is 
located on the top of the suction accumulator/drier for checking refrigerant 
condition. The suction accumulator/drier is located to the left of the 
radiator (8005) and is mounted to the vehicle body.

 Suction Accumulator/Drier Location

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Special Service Equipment

 CAUTION: Do not use R-12 service tools and equipment when servicing a R-134a 
system. Doing so may cause damage to the R-134a A/C system. 

The refrigerant system has a high-pressure (discharge) and a 
low-pressure (suction) gauge port valve. These are Schrader valves. They 
provide access to both sides (high-pressure and low-pressure) of the system 
for service hoses and a manifold gauge set so system pressures can be read. 

R-134a systems require the use of special servicing equipment designed 
specifically for R-134a systems. R-12 servicing equipment cannot be used when 
servicing R-134a A/C systems. The Rotunda R-134a service equipment includes:

Rotunda R-134a A/C Service Center 176-00001 or equivalent

Rotunda R-134a Mobile Recycling Center 023-00150

Rotunda R-134a Automatic Calibration Halogen Leak Detector 023-R1003 or 
equivalent

Rotunda R-134a Manifold Gauge Set 176-R0032A or equivalent

Rotunda R-134a Vacuum Pump (1.5 CFM) 176-R0126 or equivalent

Rotunda R-134a Vacuum Pump (3.0 CFM) 176-R0034 or equivalent

Rotunda R-134a Low Side Quick Disconnect 176-R0036 or equivalent

Rotunda R-134a High Side Quick Disconnect 176-R0037 or equivalent.

Rotunda A/C Flusher 014-00991 or equivalent

No Air Circulation or Improper Air Circulation (Blower Motor Operates)

Component Tests — Climate Control System

 Heater Blower Motor Switch 

Locate and disconnect the heater blower motor switch C227.

blower motor switch as indicated:

If the resistances are correct, return to the Pinpoint Tests. 
Otherwise, replace the heater blower motor switch (18578).

 Heater Core 

Look for evidence of coolant leakage at the hose-to-heater core 
attachments.

Check the system for loose heater water hose clamps. 

If a leak is found and the heater water hose clamps are tight, check 
the heater core tubes for distortion or evidence of being bent out of shape. 
Severe distortion of the heater core tubes could cause leakage at the heater 
water hose connection. 

 Plugged Heater Core 

Ensure the engine coolant is at the proper level, then start the engine 
(6007) and feel the outlet heater water hose (18472) to see if it is hot. If 
it is not warm, flow through the heater core (18476) is restricted.

 Pressure Test — In Vehicle Test 

Heater core leaks can be indicated by wet carpeting and coolant odor in 
the passenger compartment.

An inadequate seal between the heater core tubes can allow coolant to 
follow the tube to the heater core and appear as a leak. If a heater core leak 
is suspected, use the following procedures.

Drain the coolant from the cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 for 
the procedure.

Disconnect the heater water hoses from the heater core tubes.

Install a short piece of heater water hose approximately 10 cm (4 
inches) in length on each heater core tube.

Prepare the heater core as follows:

Fill the heater core and heater water hoses with water.

Install Plug BT-7422-B in one heater water hose end and Adapter 
BT-7422-A from Rotunda Radiator/Heater Core Pressure Tester 014-R1069 or 
equivalent in the other heater water hose end. 

 Rotunda Radiator/Heater Core Pressure Tester Kit 014-R1069 

[FIGURE: L9236A.gif]

Secure the hoses, plug, and adapter with hose clamps.

Pressure test the heater core as follows:

Attach the Rotunda Radiator/Heater Core Pressure Tester Kit 014-R1069 
or equivalent to Adapter BT-7422-A on the heater hose.

Close the bleed valve at the base of the gauge.

Pump 206 kPa (30 psi) of air pressure into the heater core.

Observe the pressure gauge for a minimum of three minutes. The pressure 
should not drop.

If the pressure does not drop, the heater core does not leak.

If the pressure drops, check the hose connections to the core tubes for 
leaks. If the hoses do not leak, remove the heater core from the vehicle and 
perform the bench pressure test. 

 Pressure Test — Bench Test 

Drain all coolant from the heater core.

Attach the heater water hoses with the plug and adapter to the heater 
core tubes as indicated in the in-vehicle pressure test.

Attach the Rotunda Radiator/Heater Core Pressure Tester Kit 014-R1069 
or equivalent to the adapter.

[FIGURE: L8697C.gif]

Pump 206 kPa (30 psi) of air pressure into the heater core.

Submerge the heater core in water.

If a leak is observed, service or replace the heater core. 

 Blower Motor 

Locate and disconnect the blower motor (18527) C231.

Apply 12 volts to terminal C231-1 and ground to terminal C231-2 on the 
blower motor .

If the blower motor does not operate, replace the blower motor. 
Otherwise, return to the Pinpoint Test.

 A/C Blower Motor Resistor 

Key OFF.

Measure the resistance between the wire terminals of the A/C blower 
motor resistor (19A706) according to the chart below.
