REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Refrigerant Oil Addition

 During A/C Compressor Replacement 

When replacing the A/C compressor (19703), measured quantities of 
Motorcraft Refrigerant Oil YN-12b or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
WSH-MIC231-B should be added to the A/C compressor. It is important that only 
the specified type and quantity of this refrigerant oil be used. A surplus of 
oil will reduce the cooling capacity of the system. Too little oil will result 
in poor lubrication of the A/C compressor.

When the A/C compressor operates, oil gradually leaves the A/C 
compressor and circulates through the system with the refrigerant. Eventually 
a balanced condition is reached in which a certain amount of oil is retained 
in the A/C compressor and a certain amount is continually circulated. If the 
A/C compressor is removed after the system has been operated, some oil will go 
with it. To maintain the original oil charge, it is necessary to compensate 
for the amount of oil lost with the old A/C compressor by adding an equal 
amount to the new A/C compressor. Clean refrigerant oil should be added to the 
replacement components as follows:

A new service replacement A/C compressor contains 175ml (5.91 fluid 
ounces) of Motorcraft Refrigerant Oil YN-12b or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSH-MIC231-B. Prior to installing the replacement A/C 
compressor, drain the oil into a clean, calibrated container. Then drain the 
oil from the old A/C compressor into another clean, calibrated container. Add 
the same amount of clean refrigerant oil as removed from the old A/C 
compressor to the new A/C compressor, plus 20ml (0.6762 fluid ounce). 

 During Component Replacement 

When replacing components of the air conditioning refrigerant system, 
measured quantities of Motorcraft Refrigerant Oil YN-12b or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSH-MIC231-B should be added to the replacement components. 
It is important that only the specified type and quantity of refrigerant oil 
be used. A surplus of oil will reduce the cooling capacity of the system. Too 
little oil will result in poor lubrication of the A/C compressor.

When the A/C compressor operates, oil gradually leaves the A/C 
compressor and circulates through the system with the refrigerant. Eventually 
a balanced condition is reached in which a certain amount of oil is retained 
in the A/C compressor and a certain amount is continually circulated. If a 
refrigerant system component is removed after the system has been operated, 
some oil will go with it. To maintain the original oil charge, it is necessary 
to compensate for the amount of oil lost with the old component by adding an 
equal amount to the new component. Clean refrigerant oil should be added to 
the replacement components as follows:

A/C evaporator core (19860) — Add 50ml (1.7 fluid ounces)

A/C condenser core (19712) — Add 30ml (1 fluid ounce)

Suction accumulator/drier (19C836) — Drain the oil from 
the old suction accumulator/drier. Add the same amount plus 10ml (0.34 fluid 
ounce) of clean refrigerant oil to the new suction accumulator/drier.

Pour clean refrigerant oil directly into the replacement component. 

If any other components or a refrigerant line are replaced, no 
additional refrigerant oil is necessary.

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301). 

Discharge the refrigerant system. Refer to Section 12-00 for the 
procedure.

Disconnect the evaporator to compressor suction line (19867) from the 
A/C evaporator core outlet fitting. Discard the O-ring.

Disconnect the liquid line from the A/C evaporator core inlet fitting. 
Discard the O-ring. 

Remove the two glove compartment screws and the glove compartment 
(06010).

Disconnect the two A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat 
electrical connectors.

 Instrument Panel Removed for Clarity 

[FIGURE: L9254B.gif]

Loosen the two A/C evaporator case clamp screws, opening the clamp on 
each side of the A/C evaporator housing assembly.

 NOTE: The A/C evaporator upper case nut secures both the A/C evaporator upper 
case (19C974) and the RH heater case. The A/C evaporator lower case nut 
secures both the A/C evaporator lower case and the LH heater blower motor case 
nut.

Remove the A/C evaporator upper case nut.

Remove the A/C evaporator lower case nut.

Disconnect the A/C evaporator drain hose (19858) from the evaporator 
drain hose fitting on the A/C evaporator lower case.

[FIGURE: L9253A.gif]

Remove the A/C evaporator housing assembly.

 Installation 

Position the A/C evaporator housing assembly in the vehicle and connect 
the A/C evaporator drain hose to the A/C evaporator drain hose fitting on the 
A/C evaporator housing assembly.

Install the A/C evaporator lower case nut.

Install the A/C evaporator upper case nut.

Tighten the A/C evaporator clamp screw on each side of the A/C 
evaporator housing assembly.

Connect the two A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat 
electrical connectors.

Position the glove compartment and install the two glove compartment 
screws.

 CAUTION: Do not apply refrigerant oil to the A/C evaporator case inlet or outlet 
fittings or damage to the A/C system may occur. 

 NOTE: Apply clean refrigerant oil to the O-rings prior to installation.

From the engine compartment, install a new O-ring on the liquid line 
and connect the liquid line to the A/C evaporator core inlet fitting. Tighten 
the liquid line at the A/C evaporator core inlet fitting to 10 - 19 Nm
 (87-174 lb-in).

From the engine compartment, install a new O-ring on the evaporator to 
compressor suction line and connect the evaporator to compressor suction line 
to the evaporator core outlet fitting. Tighten the evaporator to compressor 
suction line fitting to 20 - 29 Nm (15-21 lb-ft).

Connect the battery ground cable.

Evacuate and recharge the A/C system. Refer to Section 12-00 for the 
procedure.

Section 12-03B: Compressor and Clutch

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

A/C Compressor

A vane-type Panasonic A/C compressor is belt-driven by the A/C 
compressor clutch pulley. A magnetic clutch drives the A/C compressor shaft. 
When voltage is applied to the A/C compressor clutch field coil, the clutch 
hub is drawn by magnetic force toward the A/C compressor clutch pulley, which 
rotates freely on the A/C compressor (19703). The magnetic force locks the 
clutch hub to the A/C compressor clutch pulley to turn the A/C compressor 
shaft. When voltage is removed from the A/C compressor clutch field coil, the 
clutch hub moves away from the A/C compressor clutch pulley and the A/C 
compressor shaft ceases to rotate. Features of the Panasonic A/C compressor 
include: 

Minimal friction loss 

Compact size 

Quiet operation 

Few parts 

Compressor operation is controlled by the A/C clutch control relay 
(19D572) and the A/C pressure cut-off switch.

A thermo protection switch is integrated into the A/C compressor to 
protect the A/C compressor from overheating. The thermo protection switch will 
open the circuit to the A/C compressor clutch field coil if the A/C compressor 
gets too hot.

The thermo protection switch cannot be serviced separately and must be 
replaced with the A/C compressor as an assembly.

[FIGURE: L9222B.gif]

The A/C pressure cut-off switch is a safety device that shuts the A/C 
clutch (2884) off if the pressure on the discharge side of the A/C compressor 
(between the A/C evaporator core (19860) and the suction accumulator/drier 
(19C836)) drops below 201-241 kPa (29-35 psi) or is above 2940-3332 kPa 
(426-483 psi). The A/C pressure cut-off switch is wired in series with the A/C 
switch and the A/C evaporator temperature control thermostat (19618). 

[FIGURE: L9247C.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

A/C Clutch Air Gap

Set the A/C compressor (19703) on a level surface.

Check the resistance between the A/C clutch field coil electrical 
connector and a ground with Rotunda 73 Digital Multimeter 105-R0051 or 
equivalent. The resistance should be approximately 3 to 4 ohms at 20°
C (68°F). If the resistance is not as 
specified, replace the A/C clutch field coil.

Set the measuring probe of Dial Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or 
equivalent, on the clutch hub surface.

Apply 12 volts to the A/C clutch field coil electrical connector.

The clutch hub to A/C compressor clutch pulley clearance is equal to 
the difference between the dial indicator readings when applying and removing 
12 volts. Clearance should be between 0.4-0.6mm (0.016-0.024 inch). Add or 
remove shims as necessary. Refer to the A/C compressor clutch shim selection 
chart in this section.

Instrument Cluster and Panel Lighting

Instrument cluster and panel illumination includes:

Instrument cluster gauges

Transmission control selector indicator bulb (automatic transaxle

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Cluster 

The main components of the instrument cluster are: 

Instrument cluster back plate (10848)

Instrument cluster printed circuit (10K843)

Instruments 

Gauges 

Warning/indicator lamps 

The instruments consist of a speedometer (17255) and an odometer. The 
gauges include a fuel gauge and an engine coolant temperature gauge (10883). 
Indicator/warning lamps include turn signal and warning indicators. 

The instrument cluster mask (10890) is composed of three boards. 
Connections at the back of the cluster include the speedometer cable (17260) 
and two multiple-pin electrical connectors.

 Standard Instrument Cluster 

[FIGURE: K20357C.gif]

 Instrument Cluster Display Prove Out 

The instrument cluster performs a display prove out to verify that all 
warning/indicator bulbs and monitored systems are functioning properly. When 
the ignition switch (11572) is in the ON position with the engine (6007) off, 
the following indicators will illuminate:

CHECK ENGINE (malfunction indicator lamp [MIL])

Charging system indicator

Low oil pressure indicator

Anti-lock brake warning indicator

Safety belt warning indicator (60 second prove out)

Air bag warning indicator (six second prove out)

 Printed Circuit 

The instrument cluster printed circuit supplies current to the 
instrument cluster warning indicators, gauges and illumination bulbs. It is 
made of copper foil which is bonded to a polyester base film (usually referred 
to as Mylar®). The instrument cluster printed circuit is 
mounted on the back of the instrument cluster back plate.

PAGE 3228
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster — Conventional

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Level Indication System

 Fuel Gauge 

The fuel gauge (9280) is a cross coil-type gauge coupled to a variable 
resistance fuel level sensor (9275) located in the fuel tank (9002). Movement 
of the gauge needle depends on the amount of current flowing through the cross 
coil. 

When the resistance in the fuel level sensor is low, a high amount of 
current is sent to the cross coil within the fuel gauge. The high amount of 
current will create a strong magnetic field causing the fuel gauge to read full.

When the resistance in the fuel level sensor is high, a low amount of 
current is sent to the cross coil within the fuel gauge. The low amount of 
current will create a weak magnetic field causing the fuel gauge to read empty.

 Fuel Level Sensor 

The amount of current flowing through the fuel gauge coil depends on 
the resistance of the fuel level sensor. The resistance of the fuel level 
sensor will vary with the amount of fuel in the fuel tank. A float and arm, 
attached to a rheostat in the fuel level sensor, rides on the surface of the 
fuel. As the level rises or falls, the float and arm will change the position 
of the rheostat contact. Each position of the rheostat contact changes the 
resistance value of the rheostat and the amount of current flowing in the 
circuit. The higher the float, the less resistance in the circuit.

================================================================================
PAGE 3229
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster — Conventional

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Temperature Indication System

 Engine Coolant Temperature Gauge 

Engine coolant temperature is displayed on the engine coolant 
temperature gauge (10883) located on the right side of the instrument cluster. 
The engine coolant temperature gauge is a cross coil-type that changes 
readings according to the amount of current flow passing through the cross 
coil. 

As the coolant temperature rises, the water temperature indicator 
sender unit resistance decreases. A high amount of current is sent to the 
cross coil within the engine coolant temperature gauge. The high amount of 
current will create a strong magnetic field causing the engine coolant 
temperature gauge to read hot (H).

As the coolant temperature decreases, the water temperature indicator 
sender unit resistance raises. A low amount of current is sent to the cross 
coil within the engine coolant temperature gauge. The low amount of current 
will create a weak magnetic field causing the engine coolant temperature gauge 
to read cold (C).

 Water Temperature Indicator Sender Unit 

Variations in current flow to the engine coolant temperature gauge 
occur at the water temperature indicator sender unit (10884). When coolant 
temperature is low, the resistance value of the water temperature indicator 
sender unit is high and very little current flows through the circuit. As the 
coolant temperature increases, the resistance level drops, allowing more 
current flow. The water temperature indicator sender unit is located on the 
front of the engine (6007) near the water thermostat (8575).

================================================================================
PAGE 3230
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster — Conventional

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Pressure Indication System

 Low Oil Pressure Warning 

A red low (engine) oil pressure lamp will illuminate when engine oil 
pressure is below a prescribed level. When the oil pressure sensor contacts 
close, the low oil pressure indicator illuminates. 

The lamp will turn on when the ignition switch (11572) is first turned 
to the ON position. The engine oil pressure lamp should go out within a few 
seconds after the engine (6007) starts, indicating that engine oil pressure is 
adequate. 

 Oil Pressure Sensor 

The oil pressure sensor (9278) is calibrated to close when engine oil 
pressure falls below 30 kPa (4.3 psi). It is located on the rear of the engine 
near the oil filter (6731), just below the intake manifold (9424).

================================================================================
PAGE 3231
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster — Conventional

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charge Indication System

 Charging System Warning 

A red charging system indicator lamp is located in the instrument 
cluster. This lamp is represented by a battery symbol which glows when there 
is no generator output current or if the generator output is too high. 

When the ignition switch (11572) contacts are closed (ignition switch 
in the ON position), battery current illuminates the charging system indicator 
lamp. 

When the generator (GEN) (10346) builds up enough voltage to energize 
an electrical circuit in the voltage regulator (VR) (10316), the charging 
system indicator lamp goes out.

PAGE 3232
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster — Conventional

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Speedometer

The speedometer (17255) is a standard, mechanically driven, magnetic 
type. The speedometer drive begins at the transaxle, where the speedometer 
gear (17271) meshes with the speedometer drive gear (17285) mounted on the 
differential (4026). The speedometer gear and shaft are contained in a sleeve 
that is bolted to the transaxle. The other cable end is connected to the 
speedometer head on the instrument cluster by a clip.

================================================================================
PAGE 3233
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster — Conventional

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Odometer

The odometer registers total distance traveled. It is driven 
mechanically by the speedometer cable (17260). Operation of the odometer is 
identical to speedometer operation.

 Odometer Replacement 

The mileage on a replacement odometer cannot be reset. If a replacement 
odometer is installed, a sticker recording the vehicle's mileage at the date 
of replacement must be attached to the driver's door jamb.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Trip Odometer

The trip odometer is driven mechanically by the speedometer cable 
(17260). It registers continuously up to 999.9 miles, unless it is reset. If 
it is not reset before the 999.9 mile limit, the dial will turnover back to 0 
and begin counting again. To reset the trip odometer, press the trip odometer 
reset button.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators

The following illustration shows the locations of all indicator/warning 
lamps on the standard cluster. Warning indicator positions on the optional 
cluster are identical.

 Brake System 

The red brake warning indicator illuminates under two conditions. It 
illuminates when the parking brake control (2780) is applied or when a low 
fluid condition exists in the brake master cylinder reservoir (2K478). The 
parking brake signal switch and bracket (15A851) is located on the parking 
brake control under the parking brake console. When the parking brake control 
lever is pulled upward, the switch closes and provides a ground path for the 
indicator circuit.

The brake master cylinder fluid level sensor (2B372) is located in the 
master cylinder reservoir. When the brake fluid drops to a predetermined 
level, the contact on the float completes the ground for the indicator circuit.

 Anti-Lock Brakes 

The amber anti-lock brake warning indicator illuminates for numerous 
reasons. The indicator warns the driver that the anti-lock brake system has 
been turned off due to a symptom that exists in the system. The normal braking 
system remains operational, but the wheels could lock up during a panic stop 
while the indicator is illuminated.

 Check Engine (MIL) 

The CHECK ENGINE (malfunction indicator lamp [MIL]) 
informs the driver that a malfunction exists within the electronic engine 
control system. The powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) completes the 
ground path for the indicator circuit.

 Charging System 

The charging system indicator illuminates whenever the generator output 
is insufficient to maintain the battery state of charge. Under normal 
operation, the indicator should go out after the engine (6007) is started and 
the charging system begins to operate. If the indicator illuminates while the 
engine is running or after the ignition key is removed, a malfunction is 
indicated.

 Low Oil Pressure 

The oil pressure indicator illuminates when the oil pressure falls 
below 30 kPa (4.3 psi). Under normal operation, the indicator remains 
illuminated for a few seconds after the engine is started. The indicator goes 
out when the oil pressure rises above 30 kPa (4.3 psi). The oil pressure 
indicator is connected between the oil pressure sensor (9278) and the battery 
feed from the interior fuse junction panel.

 Air Bag 

When the passive restraint system is operating properly, the air bag 
warning indicator illuminates for approximately six seconds when the ignition 
switch (11572) is turned to the ON position. If the indicator does not 
illuminate, flashes, or remains lit continuously, a malfunction is present in 
the supplemental restraint system.

 Safety Belt 

The safety belt warning indicator illuminates when the ignition switch 
is in the ON position and the driver's safety belt is unfastened. The safety 
belt warning indicator will remain illuminated until the driver's safety belt 
is fastened or approximately 60 seconds have elapsed.

 Fuel Door 

A fuel door orientation symbol is printed on the instrument cluster to 
remind the driver which side of the vehicle the fuel door is on.

 High Beam 

The high beam indicator illuminates when the high beam headlamps are 
on. The indicator does not illuminate when the headlamp switch (11654) is in 
the low beam or OFF position.

 LH/RH Turn 

The LH and RH turn signal indicators flash when the multi-function 
switch (13K359) is moved up or down. Both turn indicators flash when the 
hazard flasher warning switch is activated.

 Heated Back Window Light 

The heated back window indicator illuminates when the heated back 
window switch and light (18C621) is on.

Component Tests 

 Fuel Gauge 

Remove the instrument cluster. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Using a jumper, connect the battery positive terminal to the fuel gauge 
"+" terminal and the battery negative terminal to the fuel gauge "-" terminal.

Connect one lead of a Rotunda Instrument Gauge System Tester 014-R1063 
or equivalent to the "F-U" terminal of the fuel gauge (9280), and connect the 
other lead to the "-" terminal of the fuel gauge.

Adjust the instrument gauge system tester to the resistances shown in 
the illustration.

[FIGURE: K20419A.gif]

If the fuel gauge does not operate as specified, replace the fuel 
gauge. If the fuel gauge is OK, return to the Pinpoint Test.

 Fuel Level Sensor

removal procedure.

Measure the resistance between terminal A and terminal B of the fuel 
level sensor.

 Connector Shown From Component Side 

[FIGURE: K20418A.gif]

Adjust the fuel tank float to the following positions:

[FIGURE: K20424A.gif]

If the resistances are not as specified, replace the fuel level sensor. 
If the fuel level sensor is OK, return to the Pinpoint Test.

 Engine Coolant Temperature Gauge 

Remove the instrument cluster. Refer to the procedure in this section.

Using a jumper, connect the battery positive terminal to the instrument 
cluster temperature gauge "+" terminal and the battery negative terminal to 
the engine coolant temperature gauge "-" terminal.

Connect one lead of a Rotunda Instrument Gauge System Tester 014-R1063 
or equivalent to the "U" terminal of the engine coolant temperature gauge 
(10883), and connect the other lead to the "-" terminal of the engine coolant 
temperature gauge.

Adjust the instrument gauge system tester to the resistances shown in 
the illustration.

[FIGURE: K20420A.gif]

replace the engine coolant temperature gauge. If the engine coolant 
temperature gauge is OK, return to the Pinpoint Test.

 Water Temperature Indicator Sender Unit

Disconnect the water temperature indicator sender unit connector.

indicator sender unit (10884) and ground.

Start the engine.

Temperature °C (°F)

Resistance Ohms

49.8-50.2 (89.7-154.3)

189.4-259.6

114.7-115.3 (206.5-271.5)

24.2-28.1

indicator sender unit. If the resistance is OK, return to the Pinpoint Test.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Speedometer System Noisy 

Applying heavy amounts of lubricant to the cable core will only stop 
the noise temporarily unless the actual source of noise is found and 
corrected. If the speedometer gear (17271) or speedometer head are replaced, 
ensure that the square drive holes contain a sufficient amount of Speedometer 
Cable Grease E6TZ-19581-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESF-M1C160-A. If not, apply a 4.6mm (3/16 inch) diameter ball of this damping 
grease into the drive holes as required.

================================================================================
PAGE 3250
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster — Conventional

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Drive and Driven Gears Damaged 

A speedometer gear (17271) with two or three adjoining teeth badly 
scored is indicative of improper assembly procedure. The gear should be 
inserted in the transaxle while twisting the speedometer gear assembly back 
and forth. This will ensure initial gear engagement and prevent gear damage. 
Never use force.

Whenever a speedometer drive gear (17285) is replaced, a new 
speedometer gear should also be installed, regardless of its apparent 
condition.

================================================================================

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster — Conventional

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Instrument Cluster Lenses

Clean the instrument cluster main lens (10887) with a high quality 
glass cleaner and a lint-free cloth. Ensure that the instrument cluster main 
lens is clear and free of streaks before assembly. Inspect the lens surface 
for cracks and scratches. Replace the instrument cluster main lens if the lens 
surface is cracked or scratched excessively.

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Speedometer Calibration

The speed indication is biased high, except on police vehicles with 
certified calibration speedometers (17255). As a general rule, the indicated 
speed is equal to or greater than the actual speed. This is intended to 
protect the consumer against violating speed laws. Most customer concerns are 
related to speedometers reading too high at true speeds between 80 - 105 km/h 
(50-65 mph). In this speed range, the worst case errors may indicate a speed 
that is 10 percent greater than true speed.

The speedometer head is an instrument which processes information sent 
to it by the rotating speedometer cable (17260). If the system components send 
the wrong number of revolutions per mile to the speedometer head, an 
inaccurate speed reading and amount of distance traveled will be displayed. 
Since there is no error in the fixed gear ratio of the speedometer head 
odometer, start by checking the accuracy of the odometer even if the customer 
concern indicates a speed accuracy problem. Odometer accuracy can be checked 
by using roads established at mile increments or a known local course. If 
roads with mile markers are used, a five mile stretch is recommended to allow 
for inaccuracies. If an error is greater than 3.75 percent, a change to the 
speedometer drive/driven gear selection, tire size, or tire inflation may need 
attention. The odometer should be checked again to verify any corrective 
action. If the indicated speed error exceeds 10 percent between 80 km/h and 96 
km/h (50-60 mph), replace the speedometer.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Horn System

The horn system consists of:

horn (13833)

horn switches

horn relay and bracket (13853)

Horn circuit power is fed from the 15 A STOP fuse to the switched side 
of the horn relay. The steering wheel mounted horn switches are connected to 
the control side of the horn relay which turns the horn relay on when either 
horn switch is depressed.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Chime/Buzzer Systems

The warning chime/buzzer system produces a repetitive chime for the 
following warnings:

Key-in-ignition warning

Safety belt warning

Headlamp switch on warning

================================================================================
PAGE 3267
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-09: Gauges, Warning Devices — Chime/Buzzer System

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Key-in-Ignition Warning

The warning chime sounds when the key is in the ignition switch lock 
cylinder in the LOCK or ACC position, and either front door is opened. The 
chime will continue until either the ignition key is removed or both doors are 
closed.

================================================================================
PAGE 3268
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-09: Gauges, Warning Devices — Chime/Buzzer System

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Belt Warning

The warning chime sounds when the ignition switch (11572) is in the ON 
position and the driver's safety belt is unfastened. The chime will continue 
until the driver's safety belt is fastened or approximately four to eight 
seconds have elapsed.

================================================================================
PAGE 3269
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-09: Gauges, Warning Devices — Chime/Buzzer System

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Passive Restraint System Warnings

When the passive restraint system is operating properly, the air bag 
warning indicator will illuminate for approximately six seconds whenever the 
ignition switch (11572) is turned to the ON position. If the warning indicator 
does not illuminate, flashes, or remains lit continuously, refer to Section 01-20B .

================================================================================
PAGE 3270
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-09: Gauges, Warning Devices — Chime/Buzzer System

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamp Switch On Warning

The warning chime sounds when the parking lamps (13200) and/or 
headlamps (13008) are on when the ignition key has been removed, and either 
front door (20124) is opened. The warning chime will continue until either 
both front doors are closed or the headlamp switch (11654) is turned off.

================================================================================

================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 13-09: Gauges, Warning Devices — Chime/Buzzer System

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Timer System

The timer system is incorporated into the central processing unit (CPU) 
(warning chime module). It limits the duration of the safety belt warning 
chime to approximately six seconds and the indicator lamp to approximately 60 
seconds.

Section 14-00: Battery and Charging System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charging System 

The charging system is a negative ground system consisting of a 
generator (GEN) (10346) with an internal electronic voltage regulator (VR) 
(10316), a battery (10655), a charge indicator lamp, battery ground cable 
(14301), battery to starter relay cable (14300), and the necessary electrical 
wiring. Refer to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for 
schematics and locations of wiring harnesses.

================================================================================
PAGE 3281
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 14-00: Battery and Charging System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Generator with Integral Voltage Regulator — Internal 
Fan and Regulator Type

The generator (GEN) (10346) is mounted on the front of the engine 
(6007) and is driven by the generator/water pump drive belt.

[FIGURE: J4628C.gif]

The generator produces alternating current (AC) which is changed to 
direct current (DC) by the rectifier (10304) for distribution to the vehicle 
electrical system.

There are three terminals on the generator for connection to the 
vehicle electrical system. 

The B-(battery) terminal is on the back of the generator and the L- and 
S-terminals are on its side. The L- and S-terminals have identification marks 
on the generator housing.

[FIGURE: J4632B.gif]

A charging system indicator lamp in the instrument cluster (10849) is 
used to indicate when a charging system malfunction occurs. 

The charging system indicator lamp should illuminate when the ignition 
key is turned to the ON position, and then go out when the engine is started 
and the charging system begins to operate. If the charging system indicator 
lamp illuminates during driving or stays on when the key is removed from the 
ignition switch (11572), a charging system malfunction is indicated.

[FIGURE: J5281D.gif]

A maintenance-free, 12 volt storage battery (10655) is used to start 
the vehicle and supplies extra electrical power at times of high system 
current demand.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Inspection and Verification 

 WARNING: HYDROGEN AND OXYGEN GASES ARE PRODUCED DURING NORMAL BATTERY OPERATION. 
THIS GAS MIXTURE CAN EXPLODE IF FLAMES, SPARKS OR LIGHTED TOBACCO ARE BROUGHT 
NEAR THE BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR USING A BATTERY IN AN ENCLOSED SPACE, 
ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION, PROTECT YOUR FACE AND SHIELD YOUR EYES. 

 WARNING: KEEP OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. BATTERIES CONTAIN SULFURIC ACID. AVOID 
CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES, OR CLOTHING. ALSO, SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN WORKING NEAR 
THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE SPLASHING OF THE ACID SOLUTION. IN 
CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES, OR CLOTHING, FLUSH IMMEDIATELY WITH 
WATER FOR A MINIMUM OF FIFTEEN MINUTES. IF ACID IS SWALLOWED, DRINK LARGE 
QUANTITIES OF MILK OR WATER, FOLLOWED BY MILK OF MAGNESIA, A BEATEN EGG, OR 
VEGETABLE OIL. CALL A PHYSICIAN IMMEDIATELY. 

Before performing charging or starting system tests on the vehicle, 
note the complaint (such as slow cranking, battery (10655) discharged, wet top 
of battery, charging system indicator does not illuminate or always 
illuminated and proceed to the Symptom Chart.

Section 14-00: Battery and Charging System — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests 

 Battery 

 Capacity Testing 

To perform this test, use a high-rate discharge tester, Rotunda 
Alternator, Regulator, Battery and Starter Tester (ARBST) 010-00725 or 
equivalent, in conjunction with Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053 or 
equivalent. 

Turn the Alternator, Regulator, Battery and Starter Tester (ARBST) 
010-00725 on. Connect the positive test lead to the positive battery post and 
the negative test lead to the negative battery post.

Initiate test by pushing the battery test button on the ARBST unit. The 
test will be performed automatically.

If battery tests good, it has a good output capacity and will readily 
accept a charge.

If battery tests bad, it is defective and must be replaced.

If battery test result is charge and retest, charge the battery to 
capacity and repeat procedure.

If the battery (10655) is found to be discharged only, check for a loose 
drive belt (8620), loose electrical connection, charging system performance, 
and perform a battery drain test.

 Base Voltage Test 

 NOTE: Prior to running this test, turn the headlamps on for 10-15 seconds to 
remove any surface charge from the battery. Then, wait until the voltage 
stabilizes prior to performing the base voltage test.

With the ignition OFF and no electrical loads on, connect the negative 
(-) lead of Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent, to the 
battery ground cable clamp.

Connect the positive (+) lead of the multimeter to the 
battery to starter relay cable clamp. 

Read and record the battery voltage shown on the multimeter. This is 
called base voltage and will be used in later tests. 

 No-Load Test 

Connect Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent, to 
monitor engine speed.

Connect the leads of Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or 
equivalent, across the battery terminals.

Read the voltage (base voltage). 

Start the engine (6007).

Run the engine at 1500 rpm with no electrical load. 

Read the voltage. The voltage should be in the range of 14.1 to 14.7 
volts. If the voltage increase is less than 2.5 volts above the base voltage, 
perform the Load Test. If there is no voltage increase or the voltage increase 
is greater than 2.5 volts, service or replace the generator (GEN) (10346). 
Refer to Section 14-02 for the service or replacement procedure.

 Load Test 

With the engine running, turn the air conditioner on (if equipped), 
turn the blower motor on high speed, and turn the headlamps on high beam.

Increase the engine speed to approximately 2000 rpm. The voltage should 
increase a minimum of 0.5 volts above the base voltage. Refer to the Bench 
Test procedures to check the generator if the voltage does not increase as 
specified.

If the voltage increased as specified, the charging system is operating 
normally. Proceed to the battery capacity testing.

 Drain Testing 

 With Clamp On DC Ammeter Test Procedure 

Turn the ignition OFF and make sure there are no electrical loads on. 

 NOTE: Do not start vehicle with clip on cable. 

Clamp the meter clip securely around the battery to starter relay cable 
(14300) or battery ground cable (14301).

The current reading (current drain) should be less than 0.05 amps. If 
it exceeds 0.05 amps it indicates a constant current drain which could cause a 
discharged battery. Possible sources of current drain are vehicle lamps that 
do not shut off properly.

If the drain is not caused by a vehicle lamp, remove the fuses from the 
interior fuse junction panel, one at a time, until the cause of the drain is 
located. If drain is still undetermined, remove fuses one at a time at the 
main fuse junction panel to find the problem circuit.

 With Voltmeter Test Procedure 

This test requires a Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053 or 
equivalent. 

Turn the ignition OFF and make sure there are no electrical loads on.

Check the battery voltage. If the voltage is under 11.5 volts, charge 
the battery to above 11.5 volts. 

Disconnect the battery ground cable. 

 CAUTION: Do not crank the engine, it could destroy the multimeter. 

Connect the multimeter as shown. 

[FIGURE: J5306C.gif]

Set Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053 to the DC amp scale to 
measure a direct current drain.

The current reading (current drain) should be less than 0.05 amps. If 
the reading exceeds 0.05 amps it indicates a constant current drain, which 
could cause a discharged battery. Possible sources of current drain are 
vehicle lamps that do not turn off. If the problem is not a lamp, remove the 
fuses from the interior fuse junction panel one at a time until the cause of 
the drain is located. If drain is still undetermined, remove fuses one at a 
time at the main fuse junction panel to find the problem circuit. 

 Electronic Drains Which Shut Off When the Battery Cable Is Disconnected 

Repeat Steps 1 through 5 of the Battery Drain Test With Multimeter. 

Without starting engine, turn ignition ON for a moment and then OFF. 

Connect Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053 or equivalent and read 
the amperage.

The current reading (current drain) should be less than 0.05 amps. If 
it exceeds 0.05 amps after a few minutes, and if this drain did not show in 
previous tests, the drain is most likely caused by a malfunctioning electronic 
component. As in previous tests, remove the fuses in the main fuse junction 
panel one at a time to locate the problem circuit. 

 Generator On-Vehicle Tests 

 Load Test 

Connect the leads of Rotunda Alternator, Regulator, Battery and Starter 
Tester (ARBST) 010-00725 or equivalent to the vehicle as shown, observing 
proper polarity.

[FIGURE: J5268A.gif]

Turn ARBST unit on.

Turn all electrical accessories off.

Initiate test by pushing the charging system test button on ARBST unit.

Start the engine and run at approximately 2000 RPM. Test will be 
performed automatically.

Return the engine to idle and second part of test will be performed 
automatically.

The ARBST unit will give peak amperage reading, peak voltage reading 
and diode pattern condition at conclusion of test.

If the peak amperage output is within 10 percent of the generator's 
rated output of 60 amps then the generator is functioning properly.

If the amperage output is below 60 amps then proceed with the next test.

 No-Load Test 

 CAUTION: Do not ground the B-terminal. 

With the ignition switch (11572) in the ON position and the engine not 
running, verify that the voltage at the generator wiring connector terminals 
are as follows: 

B-terminal= Approximately 12 volts

L-terminal= Approximately 1 volt

S-terminal= Approximately 12 volts

[FIGURE: J5269A.gif]

Start the engine.

With the engine running and at normal curb idle, verify that the 
voltage at the generator wiring connector terminals is as follows: 

 GENERATOR VOLTAGE SPECIFICATIONS 

Generator Terminal

Ignition ON/ Engine Off

14.1 - 14.7 volts

If the voltages are as specified, check the wiring harness between the 
battery and the B-terminal. If the voltages are below specification, check the 
wiring harness. If the wiring harness is in good condition, refer to Generator 
Bench Tests in this section.

 Generator Bench Tests 

Refer to the Removal and Installation procedures in Section 14-02 to 
remove the generator from the vehicle. After removal, disassemble the 
generator as outlined in Section 14-02 and perform the Generator Bench Tests 
procedures.

 Stator and Coil Grounded Test 

Inspect the stator laminations for indications of overheating. 

If burn spots are evident, replace the stator and coil (10336). 

Use Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent, to check 
for continuity between each of the three coil leads and the stator.

[FIGURE: J5314D.gif]

If there is continuity, replace the stator and coil.

 Stator and Coil Open Test 

Use Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent, to check 
for continuity between the coil leads.

[FIGURE: J5313D.gif]

If there is no continuity, replace the stator and coil.

 Generator Rotor Open or Short Test 

Use Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent, to measure 
the resistance between the two slip rings. 

[FIGURE: J5311D.gif]

If the resistance is not between 3.2-3.5 ohms, replace the generator 
rotor (10335).

Use Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent, to check 
for continuity between each slip ring and the rotor core.

[FIGURE: J5312D.gif]

If there is continuity, replace the generator rotor.

Check the color and condition of the slip rings. 

If the slip rings are dark or grooved, clean them with fine emery paper. 

 Brushes 

Inspect the generator brushes (10347) for wear.

[FIGURE: J5310C.gif]

If the generator brushes are worn down to the wear limit line, replace 
the generator brushes as follows:

Unsolder the pigtails from the voltage regulator (VR) (10316). 

Remove the generator brushes. 

Solder the new brush pigtails to the voltage regulator.

Use a spring pressure gauge to push each generator brush into its 
holder until the tip of the generator brush projects 2mm (0.079 inch) and read 
the pressure.

[FIGURE: J5264A.gif]

If the spring force is not between 2.9-4.3 N (10.6-15.6 oz), replace the 
generator brush spring (10349).

 Rectifier 

Use Rotunda 88 Digital Multimeter 105-R0053, or equivalent, in the 
diode test mode to check for continuity between the following terminals of the 
rectifier (10304):

Section 14-01: Battery

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Battery 

The original equipment battery (10655) is a maintenance-free 12 volt,

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Battery

 WARNING: HYDROGEN AND OXYGEN GASES ARE PRODUCED DURING NORMAL BATTERY OPERATION. 
THIS GAS MIXTURE CAN EXPLODE IF FLAMES, SPARKS, OR LIGHTED TOBACCO ARE BROUGHT 
NEAR THE BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR USING A BATTERY IN AN ENCLOSED SPACE, 
ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION AND SHIELD YOUR FACE AND PROTECT YOUR EYES. 

 WARNING: KEEP BATTERIES OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN. BATTERIES CONTAIN SULFURIC 
ACID. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN OR EYES. ALSO, SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN WORKING 
NEAR THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE SPLASHING OF THE ACID SOLUTION. 
IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES, OR CLOTHING, FLUSH IMMEDIATELY WITH 
WATER FOR A PERIOD OF 15 MINUTES AND GET PROMPT MEDICAL ATTENTION. IF ACID IS 
SWALLOWED, CALL A PHYSICIAN IMMEDIATELY. 

Keep the battery (10655), particularly the top, clean and dry. If 
electrolyte is evident on the top of the battery, clean it off immediately. 
Even a weak electrolyte quickly attacks and corrodes the cable connections, 
battery hold down clamp (10718) and battery mounting clamp bolts (10756). Use 
a rag soaked in a weak solution of water and ammonia to counteract the action 
of spilled electrolyte.

================================================================================
PAGE 3295
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 14-01: Battery

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Battery Charging 

Before recharging a discharged battery (10655), inspect for the 
following conditions and service as necessary: 

Loose drive belt (8620). 

Pinched or grounded generator wiring. 

Loose wiring connections at the generator (GEN) (10346). 

Loose or corroded connections at the battery or starter motor engine 
ground. 

Excessive battery drain due to lamps left on by mistake, damaged or 
misadjusted switches, etc. 

 Maintenance-Free Batteries 

Cold batteries do not readily accept a charge. Allow batteries to warm 
up to approximately 5°C (41°F), before 
charging. The warm-up period may require four to eight hours at room 
temperature, depending on the initial temperature of the battery and its size. 

A battery that has been completely discharged may initially be slow to 
accept a charge, and in some cases may not accept a charge at the normal 
charger setting. Charging a battery in such a condition may be started by 
using the dead battery switch on chargers so equipped. 

To determine whether a battery is accepting a charge, follow the 
charger manufacturer's instructions for use of the dead battery switch. If the 
dead battery switch is the spring-loaded type, it should be held in the ON 
position for up to three minutes.

After releasing the dead battery switch and with the charger still on, 
measure battery voltage. If it shows 12 volts or higher, the battery is 
accepting a charge and is capable of being recharged. However, it may require 
up to two hours of charging with abattery colder than 5°C (41°
F) before the charge rate is high enough to show on the 
charger ammeter. It has been found that all non-damaged batteries can be 
charged by this procedure. If a battery cannot be charged by this procedure, 
it should be replaced.

A rapid recharge procedure has been developed for recharging batteries 
that have passed the Load Test and only need a recharge. This can be due to 
in-service no-start battery failures (vehicle will not crank due to low 
battery state of charge), or battery discharged in vehicle due to key-off 
loads. Refer to Section 14-00 for the load test procedure.

The battery can be rapidly recharged by using either of the following 
methods:

Perform a 2-hour charge using 20A constant current (manual setting on 
charger).

Perform a 2-hour charge using a constant potential (automatic setting 
on charger).

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Battery Cleaning 

Clean the battery (10655) and terminals with an acid-neutralizing 
solution such as a weak solution of ammonia and water. 

Clean the battery cable clamps and battery terminals with a terminal 
cleaning brush. 

Replace the battery ground cable (14301) and battery to starter relay 
cable (14300) if worn or frayed. 

Test the battery to determine if it should be: 

placed back in service. 

recharged before being placed back in service. 

replaced with a Motorcraft or equivalent battery.

Clean the battery tray (10732) with a wire brush and scraper.

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Tools 

Use the proper tools to help prevent personal injury and damage to the 
battery (10655), battery ground cable (14301), battery to starter relay cable 
(14300), and thebattery hold down clamp (10718).

Tools and equipment manufactured for servicing batteries have insulated 
parts to help prevent arcing should the tool be dropped or placed accidentally 
between a terminal and some other conducting surface.

 Pliers 

Battery pliers have jaws designed specifically for securely gripping 
battery cable clamps. Take care when removing or replacing battery clamp so 
that the battery terminal is not subjected to excessive lateral or twisting 
forces. Such forces could cause major damage to the internal components of the 
battery and could also cause leakage at the terminals.

 Clamp Puller 

Use a battery clamp puller to remove a battery cable clamp from a 
battery terminal. Jaws grip the underside of the battery clamp and pull the 
battery clamp up by means of pressure exerted against the top of the battery 
terminal. Proper use of this tool avoids the damaging lateral or twisting 
forces that result from using a pry bar or pliers.

[FIGURE: J5258A.gif]

 Clamp Spreader 

The battery clamp spreader is used to expand the battery cable clamp 
after it has been removed from the battery terminal and the battery cable 
clamp bolt has been loosened. The battery cable clamp can then be easily 
placed in its correct position on the battery terminal.

[FIGURE: J5259A.gif]

 Terminal Cleaning Brush 

The terminal cleaning brush is designed with two parts to clean both 
the tapered battery terminal and the mating surface of the battery cable clamp.

[FIGURE: J5260B.gif]

 Carrier 

 WARNING: GRIP THE SIDE WALLS RATHER THAN THE END WALLS, BECAUSE THE SIDE WALLS 
HAVE ADDITIONAL STRENGTH DUE TO INNER CELL PARTITIONS. THIS IS PARTICULARLY 
IMPORTANT WITH POLYPROPYLENE-CASE BATTERIES WHICH HAVE FLEXIBLE END WALLS. 
GRIPPING THE END WALLS ON THIS TYPE OF BATTERY COULD CAUSE THE ELECTROLYTE TO 
SPEW FROM SOME OF THE CELLS AND POSSIBLY CAUSE PERSONAL INJURY AND DAMAGE TO 
THE VEHICLE. 

Use a suitable battery carrier for lifting and transporting the battery.

[FIGURE: J5261A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Generator

The generator (GEN) (10346) produces an output current and has an 
integral voltage regulator (VR) (10316). The generator is mounted on the front 
of the engine (6007) and is driven by the generator/water pump drive belt.

[FIGURE: J4628D.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3303
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 14-02: Generator, Integral Regulator — Internal Fan and Regulator Type

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Voltage Regulator

The integral voltage regulator (VR) (10316) varies the rotor field 
excitation according to the electric current demand of the vehicle. The 
current demand of the vehicle is sampled through the S-terminal on the 
generator (GEN) (10346).

The voltage regulator is not adjustable. The voltage regulator 
automatically reduces regulated voltage when the ambient temperature 
increases, so that battery charging voltage is maintained at the proper level.

The voltage regulator limits charging system voltage to an operating 
range of 14.1 to 14.7 volts.

================================================================================
PAGE 3304
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 14-02: Generator, Integral Regulator — Internal Fan and Regulator Type

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Generator Circuit 

 Circuit Description 

[FIGURE: J4632C.gif]

 Battery Positive Voltage (B+) Output 

The generator output is supplied through the battery positive voltage (B+
) output connection to the battery and electrical system. This 
connection is the B-terminal, located on the back of the generator (GEN) 
(10346). 

 'L' Circuit 

The 'L' (lamp) circuit is used to turn on the voltage regulator (VR) 
(10316). This circuit is powered up with the ignition switch (11572) in the ON 
position. This circuit is also used to turn the charging system indicator lamp 
on if there is a fault in the charging system operation or associated wiring 
circuits. 

 'S' Circuit 

The 'S' (sensing) circuit is used to sense the battery voltage. This 
voltage is used by the voltage regulator to determine the generator output. 
This circuit is also used to supply power to the stator and coil (10336). This 
circuit is connected back to the load distribution point and is a protected 
circuit.

 Assembly 

Assemble the rectifier, stator and coil, and voltage regulator.

 CAUTION: Use only rosin-core solder. Do not apply soldering heat for longer than 
four seconds. Hold the stator and coil leads with a pair of needlenose pliers 
which will act as a heat sink to protect the diodes. 

Solder the voltage regulator leads. 

Solder the stator and coil leads.

Install the shield onto the voltage regulator. 

Install the stator and coil, along with the rectifier and voltage

Place the generator rotor into the generator front housing.

generator pulley nut. Tighten the generator pulley nut to 59-78 Nm
 (43-58 lb-ft). 

Use a stiff wire or straightened paper clip to retain the brushes in the 
voltage regulator (VR) (10316).

 Brushes

Remove the four generator front housing capscrews.

[FIGURE: J4646D.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not apply direct heat to the generator rear housing and bearing. 
Excessive heat could cause the generator rear bearing grease to melt. 

 NOTE: Do not apply the soldering iron for more than four minutes. Do not heat 
the generator rear housing and bearing to temperatures higher than 50-60°
C (122-140°F). 

Use a 200-watt soldering iron to heat the generator rear housing and 
bearing to allow the generator rear bearing (10A304) to be removed from the 
generator rear housing. 

[FIGURE: J4642B.gif]

Use a flat-blade screwdriver to separate the generator front housing 
from the stator and coil.

[FIGURE: J4647B.gif]

Be careful not to lose the stopper ring that fits in the groove of the 
generator rotor shaft. 

[FIGURE: J3808H.gif]

Remove the generator front housing and generator rotor (10335) from the 
generator rear housing and bearing.

Remove the B-terminal nut and insulator.

[FIGURE: J4648B.gif]

Remove the rectifier screw. 

Remove the two voltage regulator screws.

[FIGURE: J4643D.gif]

Use a flat-blade screwdriver to separate the stator and coil from the 
generator rear housing.

[FIGURE: J3793E.gif]

Remove the stator and coil, along with the voltage regulator (VR) 
(10316) and rectifier (10304), from the generator rear housing.

 CAUTION: To avoid overheating and damage to the rectifier, work quickly while 
soldering. Do not apply the soldering iron for more than five seconds at a 
time. 

Unsolder the stator and coil leads from the generator rear housing.

Unsolder the voltage regulator leads. 

Separate the rectifier, stator and coil, and voltage regulator. 

Remove the two shields from the voltage regulator.

[FIGURE: J5346A.gif]

Remove the solder from the voltage regulator and remove the generator 
brushes (10347).

[FIGURE: J5347A.gif]

Refer to Section 14-00 for the diagnosis and testing procedures. 

 Assembly 

Solder the generator brush into the voltage regulator.

Assemble the rectifier, stator and coil, and voltage regulator.

 CAUTION: Use only rosin-core solder. Do not apply soldering heat for longer than 
four seconds. Hold the stator and coil leads with a pair of needlenose pliers 
which will act as a heat sink to protect the diodes. 

Solder the voltage regulator leads. 

Solder the stator and coil leads.

Install the shield onto the voltage regulator. 

Install the stator and coil, along with the rectifier and voltage 
regulator, to the generator rear housing. 

Position the stator and coil in the generator rear housing so that one 
of the shallow ridges in the lamination lines up with the case bolt holes.

[FIGURE: J3813A.gif]

Install the rectifier screw. 

Install the two generator regulator screws.

Install the insulator and the B-terminal nut. 

Use a stiff wire or straightened paper clip to retain the brushes in the 
voltage regulator.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Generator

 CAUTION: When rebuilding a generator (GEN) (10346), use only high temperature 
generator front bearings (10A303) or generator rear bearings (10A304). Use of 
standard parts will result in generator failure. 

The following procedures outline Cleaning and Inspection of internal 
generator components. Refer to Section 14-00 for diagnosis and testing 
procedures of individual generator components.

 Generator Rotor 

Wipe thegenerator rotor (10335) with a clean cloth. Do not clean with 
solvent. Inspect the generator rotor shaft surface for roughness or severe 
chatter marks. Replace the generator rotor if the generator rotor shaft is not 
smooth. Check all wire leads on the generator rotor for poor solder 
connections or burned insulation. Resolder poor connections and replace the 
generator rotor if signs of burned insulation exist.

 Stator and Coil 

Wipe the stator and coil (10336) with a clean cloth. Do not clean with 
solvent. Check all wire leads on the stator and coil for poor solder 
connections or burned insulation. Resolder poor connections and replace the 
stator and coil if signs of burned insulation exist.

 Generator Bearings 

Wipe the generator front bearing and generator rear bearing with a 
clean cloth. Do not clean with solvent. Rotate the generator front bearing and 
generator rear bearing. Check for scraping noise, looseness, or roughness. 
Inspect the rollers and cages for damage or lost lubricant. Replace the 
generator front bearing or generator rear bearing if these conditions exist. 
Refer to the Front Bearing Replacement 
and Rear Bearing Replacement 
disassembly and assembly procedures in this section.

 Generator Brushes 

Replace the generator brushes (10347) if the generator brushes are at 
or are worn shorter than the wear limit line of 8mm (0.3 inch).

[FIGURE: J5310D.gif]

 Rectifier 

Wipe the rectifier (10304) with a clean cloth. Do not clean with 
solvent. Check all wire leads on the rectifier for poor solder connections or 
burned insulation. Resolder poor connections and replace the rectifier if 
signs of burned insulation exist.

Section 15-00: Audio Systems — Service

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Radio Reception 

 Antenna Position 

The stereo feature of some FM radio stations has a range of only about 
32 km (20 miles). This means that in areas of poor reception such as near tall 
buildings or hills, antenna position is important. The antenna achieves its 
maximum efficiency at the fully extended position and even then it will be 
necessary to tune the strongest stations for best reception. The radio chassis 
(18806) automatically tunes to the exact frequency of any given station, 
eliminating the need for manual fine tuning.

 Antennas and Mobility 

Although an automobile radio chassis will give outstanding mobile 
reception, it cannot provide the continuous reception of home audio 
components. The home receiver is not limited by certain geographical effects 
and vehicle operating conditions as is the mobile unit. For example, for the 
best FM reception, the automobile antenna should be designed like a TV antenna 
and pointed in the direction of the station. The best AM antenna is a long 
piece of wire; the higher the wire, the better the reception. However, because 
of design necessity, the automobile antenna is restricted in size, height, and 
direction and must receive both AM and FM stations. This means that a limited 
amount of the station's signal reaches the vehicle radio chassis. Extend the 
antenna fully for the best radio reception.

 Tuning 

Fine tuning is not required for the radio chassis.

 Tone Control 

Favoring the rear radio speakers (18808) in noisy areas will help to 
reduce noise.

 FM Flutter 

FM flutter can best be described as repeated pops and hissing bursts 
heard through the radio speakers during an otherwise good broadcast. Usually 
this condition exists while traveling in the fringe area of the station. 
Flutter will become more severe approximately 40 km (25 miles) away from the 
station. The signal loss increases the greater the distance away from the 
station, until finally noise takes over and reception becomes impossible. 
Flutter may also be noticed near the station because of the line-of-sight 
characteristics of FM radio waves. Flutter can occur when a building or large 
structure is between the antenna and the station being received. Some of the 
FM signal bends around the structure. In some of these areas, almost no FM 
signal can be detected. If the vehicle is parked in one of these areas only 
noise can be heard through the radio speakers, but by moving the vehicle 
(sometimes only inches) the station reception returns to normal. Flutter will 
not occur on the AM band because AM radio waves are much longer than FM waves.

 FM Multi-Path Cancellation 

Another effect caused by the line-of-sight characteristic of FM radio 
waves is called cancellation. This condition exists when the radio waves are 
reflected from objects or structures. The reflected signal cancels the normal 
signal, causing the antenna to pick up noise and distortion. Cancellation 
effects are most prominent in metropolitan areas but can also become quite 
severe in hilly terrain and below grade roadways. 

 FM Strong Signal Capture and AM Overloading 

FM capture is an unusual condition that occurs when traveling in the 
vicinity of a broadcast tower. If listening to a weak FM station when passing 
its broadcast tower, a stronger station may interfere without changing the 
radio chassis dial. When passing the tower, the station may switch back and 
forth a few times before returning to the station originally tuned. When 
several broadcast towers are present (common in metropolitan areas) several 
stations may overload the radio chassis resulting in considerable station 
changing, mixing, and distortion. This condition is localized and will not 
harm the radio chassis. Some overloading may also be noticed on the AM band, 
but usually to a lesser degree. 

 Receiving FM Stereo 

Because more data is carried in FM stereo waves than in monaural FM 
broadcasts, flutter, cancellation, and capture are even more noticeable. When 
diagnosing an FM stereo concern, tune to the strongest FM stereo station. 

 Stereo Indicator Inoperative or Flickering (AM and FM Reception Are OK) 

Verify that the station the customer is listening to is broadcasting an 
FM stereo signal. 

A weak or distant signal may cause the stereo indicator to flicker. 
Tune the radio chassis to a nearby FM stereo station. If the reception is 
good, but the stereo indicator is still intermittent, remove the radio chassis 
for service.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Radio Tests 

Internal diagnostic examination of the radio chassis (18806) should be 
left to the authorized radio service center. However, the automotive 
technician should be able to analyze and isolate radio reception conditions to 
the proper area or component causing the condition. All radio problem 
conditions can be isolated to one of six general areas:

Antenna system

Radio chassis

Speaker system

Radio noise suppression equipment

Radio amplifier (18B849)

Wiring

 Interfering Noises 

The vehicle ignition system is a possible source of radio interference. 
This high-voltage switching system produces a radio frequency electromagnetic 
field that radiates at AM, FM, and CB frequencies. Components have been 
designed into the vehicle to minimize this concern. Vehicle electrical 
accessories and owner add-on accessories may also contribute to radio 
interference. Furthermore, there are many noise sources which are external to 
the vehicle. These include power lines, communication systems, ignition 
systems of other vehicles, neon signs, etc. 

Noise or static may result from many causes. Two of the most common 
sources of radio noise are listed below: 

 Ignition Noise 

The most effective method of evaluating ignition noise is to compare 
the radio performance with the engine (6007) on versus engine off. If ignition 
noise is present with the engine running: 

Check to see that the spark plug wires are the suppressor type and that 
the spark plugs (12405) are the correct resistor type. 

If so equipped, check to see that the carbon center insert in the 
distributor cap (12106) is secure. 

Check the distributor cap and the distributor rotor electrodes for 
silicone grease which may cause ignition noise on FM. This noise is 
characterized by a "motor boat" type sound on weak to moderate strength 
stations. The noise can only be eliminated by replacing the distributor cap and 
distributor rotor (12200) without grease. 

 Missing or Poor Grounds 

Check radio frequency interference suppression bond grounding 
effectiveness by electrically bonding metal parts to ensure proper ground, 
such as between the tail pipe and body, or between the fender and engine, 
while the radio chassis is playing and the engine is running. Listen for a 
decrease in the objectionable radio noise. If a reduction in radio noise is 
noted, first try tightening body and exhaust system clamps and brackets. Then, 
if necessary, install a new radio frequency interference suppression bond 
(19A095) between the two metal parts to ensure proper ground. 

 Missing or Damaged Noise Suppression Components 

Noise suppression components may be malfunctioning or missing, causing 
distortion, interference, and flutter. 

 Sound Distortion, Premium Sound 

If sound distortion or erratic operation from the radio speakers 
(18808) is encountered on vehicles, refer to Diagnosis and Testing in this 
section.

the station is tuned, depress and hold a memory button. When the memory button 
is depressed, the station's sound will be interrupted. Depress the button for 
approximately two seconds. When the station's sound returns, the button is 
"set" and may be released. This process is repeated for each memory button. 
Turn the radio off, then on. Depress each station recall button and verify 
that the stations indicated are the same as the stations stored above. 

 Is the memory test OK?

Yes

No

Section 15-00: Audio Systems — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Component Tests

 Radio Antenna 

 NOTE: Many customers do not understand the limitations of FM reception. Refer 
the customer to the Owner Guide for information about the limitations of FM 
radio chassis performance.

If AM reception is extremely poor and FM reception "splits" or appears 
to have trouble holding stations, ensure that the antenna, cable, and antenna 
connectors are properly mated. If the antenna connectors are properly mated 
but the reception is still poor, replace the antenna cable. 

If only FM reception is poor, it is unlikely that the antenna cable is 
at fault. Remove the radio chassis (18806) for service. 

With the antenna cable installed on the vehicle and unplugged from the 
radio chassis, check the resistance with ohmmeter test probes contacting the 
antenna, antenna base, and antenna cable; resistance should be less than 5 
ohms between the antenna cable plug (at the tip where it inserts into the 
radio chassis) and the antenna, and between the antenna base and the antenna 
cable plug outside shield. The resistance should be greater than 10,000 ohms 
between the cable plug tip and shield. If results are satisfactory, the 
antenna and cable are in good condition. If not, check the antenna cable and 
antenna separately.

PAGE 3326
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 15-00: Audio Systems — Service

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cassette Tape Player Head

 CAUTION: The use of other cassette cleaners is not recommended. Damage to the 
cassette tape player could result. 

The playback head, capstans, and pinch rollers may accumulate an oxide 
residue as the tape passes through the components while playing. Depending on 
the quality of the tape used, more or less oxide will accumulate. Oxide 
accumulation can cause weak or wavering sound and damage to the tape cartridge 
and/or cassette tape player.

It is recommended for best performance that the cassette tape player be 
cleaned after every 10-12 hours of playing time with a Ford Cassette Cleaning 
Cartridge or equivalent.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Sound Systems

The Electronic Search Radio (ESR) type of radio chassis (18806) with 
four speakers is standard.

Volume is set from 0 to 30. Bass, Treble, Fade and Balance are set from 
-7 to +7.

The Electronic Search Radio (ESR) type radio has a programmable maximum 
power-on volume preset. The factory power-on volume preset is set at 10. If 
the volume is adjusted to a higher setting, the preset will reset to 10 the 
next time the vehicle is shut off and restarted. The max power-on volume 
preset can be changed by selecting the new volume and simultaneously pressing 
the 2 and 3 buttons.

There are two radio options: 

Electronic Search Radio Chassis (ESR).

Electronic Search Cassette Radio Chassis (ESC).

 Electronic Search Radio Chassis (ESR) Controls 

Refer to the Audio System Operating Guide for complete operating 
guidelines.

Section 15-02: Antenna

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Antenna

The antenna is mounted at the top of the left front body upper pillar 
(02505) between the left front door (20125) and the windshield glass (03100). 
The whip-type antenna is extended by pulling it upward from its base. 

The antenna base is mounted to the front body upper pillar by two 
screws. On the underside of the antenna base, a long plastic tube insulates 
the antenna lead from the surrounding sheet metal. The plastic insulating tube 
also serves as a drain to direct water down through the front body upper 
pillar to a drain hole on the underside of the body.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Antenna 

 Fixed 

 Removal 

Remove the instrument cluster. Refer to Section 13-01 for the removal 
procedure.

Unhook the antenna from the wiring harness retainer (14A163) behind the 
instrument cluster.

Remove the radio chassis (18806). Refer to Section 15-01 for the 
removal procedure.

Remove the antenna lead from the heater (18478) and wiring harness 
retainer.

Remove the two antenna base screws, securing the antenna base to the 
front body upper pillar (02505).

[FIGURE: L5832B.gif]

Pull the antenna, antenna base, insulating tube, and antenna lead up to 
expose the old antenna lead.

[FIGURE: L9225A.gif]

Cut the old antenna lead near the antenna base. 

Tape the new antenna lead to the old antenna lead for use in feeding 
the new antenna lead through the vehicle.

 Installation 

Insert the antenna lead and insulating tube down through the front body 
upper pillar while pulling the new antenna lead through with the old antenna 
lead.

Pull the interior end of the old antenna lead to feed the new antenna 
lead into the vehicle interior.

Install and tighten the two antenna base screws to secure the antenna 
base to the front body upper pillar. Ensure that the drain tube end fits into 
the drain hole.

Reroute the antenna lead into its wiring harness retainer located on the 
heater and behind the instrument cluster.

Install the radio chassis. Refer to the installation procedure in 
 Section 15-01 .

Install the instrument cluster. Refer to the installation procedure in 
 Section 13-01 .

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamps

 Aerodynamic 

The aerodynamically styled headlamps (13008) are bracket-mounted 
between the radiator grille (8200) and the front turn signal lamp. The 
headlamp is attached to the mounting bracket with two headlamp adjusting 
screws (13032) and a tension spring. These screws are also used to adjust the 
horizontal and vertical aim of the headlamps.

The contoured headlamp lens is attached to a plastic reflector that 
also serves as the headlamp bulb housing. The headlamp bulb is a high 
intensity halogen type with an integral socket and electrical connector. The 
headlamp bulb is installed in the back of the headlamp and is secured in 
position with a spring clip. Once locked in place, a dust boot installed on 
the headlamp housing/reflector prevents the entry of contaminants into the 
headlamp.

 Front Exterior Lamps 

[FIGURE: GK2081A.gif]

 Daytime Running Lamps 

Vehicles sold in Canada incorporate a daytime running lamp (DRL) system.

Refer to Section 17-04 for information concerning the DRL system.

================================================================================
PAGE 3345
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamp Switch 

The headlamp switch is part of the multi-function switch (13K359) 
mounted on the steering column. The headlamp switch is on the left side of the 
steering column and is serviced with the multi-function switch as an assembly. 
The headlamps (13008) turn on when the rotary switch at the end of the stalk 
is rotated two detents counterclockwise. Rotating this headlamp switch to the 
first detent will illuminate the parking lamps, side marker lamps, tail lamps 
and rear license plate lamps.

[FIGURE: K21113B.gif]

The headlamp switch stalk itself provides two additional functions: 

High beam. 

Flash-to-pass. 

[FIGURE: K21114B.gif]

When the headlamp switch is pushed toward the instrument panel (04320), 
the high beam headlamps turn on and remain on until the headlamp switch is 
pulled rearward to the low beam position. The high beam headlamp circuit also 
illuminates the high beam indicator in the instrument cluster. The 
flash-to-pass function allows the headlamps to operate independent of the 
rotary headlamp switch. When the headlamp switch is pulled toward the driver, 
the high beams will turn on. Releasing the headlamp switch allows spring 
pressure to return the headlamp switch to the OFF position.

 Headlamps On Warning Chime 

The headlamps on warning chime is incorporated in the central 
processing unit (CPU) with an audible warning system and timing circuit. It 
provides a warning when the headlamps are on with the front door (20124) open.

 Light Switch Rheostat Resistor 

Instrument panel/cluster illumination is controlled by the light switch 
rheostat resistor (11691), which is located on the lower RH side of the 
instrument panel. The light switch rheostat resistor adjusts the brightness of 
the displays on the instrument panel.

Instrument panel/cluster illumination will not operate when the 
headlamp switch is in the OFF position.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Brake On/Off (BOO) Switch 

The brake on/off (BOO) switch illuminates the rear lamps and the rear 
hi-mount lamp (13A613). The BOO switch also sends braking information to the 
powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650).

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps —Parking, Rear and Marker

The parking, side marker rear lamps (13404), and license plate lamp 
circuits are controlled by the headlamp switch. When the headlamp switch is 
rotated to the first detent, only the parking and side marker lamps, rear 
lamps, and rear license plate lamps are illuminated. The front parking lamps 
are incorporated within the headlamp housing.

When the headlamp switch is rotated to the second detent, the parking 
lamps, side marker lamps, rear lamps and license plate lamps remain on, and 
the headlamps (13008) are illuminated. 

 Rear Exterior Lamps 

[FIGURE: GK2080A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Stoplamps

The rear lamp (13404) is a lens and housing assembly containing the 
backup lamp, the side marker lamp, the turn signal lamp, and the 
tail/stoplamp. The lens is bonded to the rear lamp housing and the assembly is 
attached to the body with two screws. The wiring from the rear lamp individual 
bulbs is contained in a single electrical connector that joins the body wiring 
harness.

Lamp, Rear Hi-Mount 

The rear hi-mount lamp (13A613) is mounted inside the vehicle on the 
liftgate. The two-piece rear hi-mount lamp is attached to the center of the 
liftgate with two nuts.

Lamps, License 

The two rear license plate lamps are installed in the liftgate above 
the license plate. Each license plate lamp has two screws that attach the lens 
to the housing assembly. The wiring from the license plate lamps extends into 
the liftgate where it joins the liftgate harness.
