DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps, Backup

The backup lamp system consists of a backup lamp switch (15520) (on 
manual transaxle vehicles), or a park/neutral position switch (PNP switch) 
(7A247) (on automatic transaxle vehicles) and two backup lamp bulbs located at 
the rear of the vehicle. 

When the backup lamp switch (on manual transaxle vehicles) or the PNP 
switch (on automatic transaxle vehicles) is activated, current is directed to 
the backup lamps. The backup lamps will indicate that the vehicle is engaged 
in the reverse gear. 

When the transaxle is shifted to any other gear position, the backup 
lamps are turned off.

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turn Signals

To operate the turn signals, the ignition switch (11572) must be in the 
ON position. Move the turn signal switch stalk in the desired direction (down 
for left, and up for right) to activate the turn signals. The turn signal 
switch lever will remain in position without manual effort until the turn is 
completed. Turning thesteering wheel (3600) will automatically cancel the turn 
signal. If the turn signal continues to flash, pull the turn signal switch 
lever back to the OFF position. 

[FIGURE: K21115A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turn Signal and Hazard Lamps

The hazard lamps are operated independently from the ignition switch 
(11572). All turn signal lamps can be made to flash at the same time by 
depressing the hazard flasher switch. Flashing is discontinued when the hazard 
flasher switch is depressed a second time.

Hazard Flasher Switch

The hazard flasher switch is located in the center of the upper 
steering column shroud (3530) on top of the steering column, and is an 
integral part of the multi-function switch (13K359).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Indicator Flasher

The turn signal and the hazard flasher switches use the same indicator 
flasher (13350).

The indicator flasher is located in the passenger compartment under the 
instrument panel (04320) in the upper LH corner. It is suspended from a 
bracket that also holds the horn relay. The indicator flasher cover is formed 
to lock the horn relay and bracket (13853) in place when it is installed on 
the bracket.

lamp relay, and fog lamp relay.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Headlamp Bulb 

 Removal 

 WARNING: THE HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB CONTAINS GAS UNDER PRESSURE. THE HEADLAMP 
BULB MAY SHATTER IF THE GLASS ENVELOPE IS SCRATCHED OR THE BULB IS DROPPED. 
HANDLE THE HEADLAMP BULB CAREFULLY. GRASP THE HEADLAMP BULB ONLY BY ITS BASE. 
AVOID TOUCHING THE GLASS ENVELOPE. KEEP THE HEADLAMP BULB OUT OF THE REACH OF 
CHILDREN. 

 NOTE: A correctly aimed headlamp (13008) should not require reaiming after 
replacement of the headlamp bulb. The headlamp bulb should not be removed from 
the headlamp until just before a replacement headlamp bulb is to be installed. 
Removal of the headlamp bulb for an extended period of time may affect 
headlamp performance. Contaminants (dust, moisture, smoke, etc.) may enter the 
headlamp where they can settle on the lens and reflector. Never turn on the 
headlamps with the headlamp bulb removed from the headlamp.

 NOTE: In the following illustrations, the engine air cleaner (ACL) (9600) and 
the air cleaner to intake manifold tube (9B697) were removed for clarity. The 
engine air cleaner and air cleaner to intake manifold tube do not need to be 
removed to perform the procedure.

Lift the lock tab and disconnect the headlamp bulb electrical connector 
from the headlamp bulb.

[FIGURE: K20476A.gif]

Turn the dust boot retaining ring counterclockwise to remove.

[FIGURE: K20477B.gif]

Remove the dust boot.

[FIGURE: K20478A.gif]

Unlatch the spring clip which retains the headlamp bulb and pivot it 
clear of the headlamp bulb.

[FIGURE: K20479A.gif]

Remove the headlamp bulb by pulling the headlamp bulb straight back and 
out of the headlamp housing. Do not rotate the headlamp bulb.

[FIGURE: K20480B.gif]

 Installation 

 WARNING: THE HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB CONTAINS GAS UNDER PRESSURE. THE HEADLAMP 
BULB MAY SHATTER IF THE GLASS ENVELOPE IS SCRATCHED OR THE BULB IS DROPPED. 
HANDLE THE HEADLAMP BULB CAREFULLY. GRASP THE HEADLAMP BULB ONLY BY ITS BASE. 
AVOID TOUCHING THE GLASS ENVELOPE. KEEP THE HEADLAMP BULB OUT OF THE REACH OF 
CHILDREN. 

Align the tabs on the headlamp bulb flange with the slots in the 
headlamp and install the headlamp bulb.

Pivot the spring clip over the headlamp bulb and latch it into the 
headlamp.

Install the dust boot onto the headlamp.

Install the dust boot retaining ring and turn clockwise.

Connect the headlamp electrical connector.

Turn the headlamps on and check for proper operation.

ADJUSTMENTS

Headlamp 

Headlamp aim adjustment should be made with Rotunda Optical Headlamp 
Aimer 196-00001 or equivalent. Follow the manufacturer's instructions for 
proper use. 

All headlamp adjustments should be made with the fuel tank (9002) half 
full, the vehicle unloaded and the cargo area empty except for the spare tire 
and the jacking equipment. Also, check the tires and adjust them to the 
recommended inflation pressure. 

The horizontal aim headlamp adjusting screw is located on the inboard 
side of the headlamp (13008). The vertical aim headlamp adjusting screw is 
located on the outboard side of the headlamp. Both the horizontal headlamp 
adjusting screw and the vertical headlamp adjusting screw are accessible at 
the top of the headlamp.

ADJUSTMENTS

Brake On/Off (BOO) Switch 

Disconnect the brake on/off (BOO) switch electrical connector. 

Loosen the BOO switch nuts. 

Connect Rotunda 73 Digital Multimeter 105-R0051 or equivalent across 
the BOO switch terminals. 

Position the BOO switch until the Rotunda 73 Digital Multimeter 
105-R0051 or equivalent indicates continuity. 

Carefully move the BOO switch toward the brake pedal (2455) until the 
Rotunda 73 Digital Multimeter 105-R0051 or equivalent indicates the BOO switch 
is open (infinite resistance). 

Rotate the BOO switch toward the brake pedal one-half additional turn 
and tighten the BOO switch nuts.Instrument panel (04320)

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Interior Lighting

The interior lighting system consists of the dome lamp, luggage 
compartment lamp, and two courtesy lamp switches.

================================================================================
PAGE 3404
================================================================================
1997 Aspire

Section 17-02: Lighting, Interior

1997 Aspire Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamp, Dome

Dome lamp operation depends on the position of the dome lamp switch and 
the two courtesy lamp switches. The dome lamp switch has three positions: 

ON — allows illumination of the dome lamp miniature 
bulb with the doors closed. 

DOOR — connects the dome lamp miniature bulb to the 
courtesy lamp switches, allowing illumination of the dome lamp miniature bulb 
only when a door is opened. 

OFF — keeps the dome lamp miniature bulb off when a 
door is open.

The two courtesy lamp switches are located on the center body pillars 
at the base of the door openings. The courtesy lamp switches activate the dome 
lamp when either front door is opened and the dome lamp switch is on DOOR.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps

 Luggage Compartment 

Illumination of the luggage compartment lamp miniature bulb depends on 
the position of the luggage compartment lamp switch and the liftgate switch. 
The two-position luggage compartment lamp switch allows the luggage 
compartment miniature bulb to remain off when the liftgate is opened. In the 
ON position, the luggage compartment miniature bulb turns on and remains on 
whenever the liftgate is opened. The liftgate switch is an integral part of 
the liftgate latch.

Section 17-04: Lamps, Daytime Running

1997 Aspire (Canada Only) Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Daytime Running Lamp (DRL) System 

Vehicles sold in Canada incorporate a daytime running lamp (DRL) 
system. The DRL control module operates the headlamps (13008) when the 
ignition switch (11572) is in the ON position, the headlamp switch is in the 
OFF position, and the parking brake is not engaged. Although this system uses 
the high-beam filament of the headlamp bulb (13007), it also has a voltage 
dropping DRL resistor to dim the headlamps for daytime operation. This allows 
the flash-to-pass function during daytime operation. 

The control module for the daytime running lamp (DRL) system is 
integrated into the central processing unit (CPU). The CPU is located behind 
the (LH) cowl side trim panel (02345).

The daytime running lamp (DRL) resistor is located in the engine 
compartment at the top center of the bulkhead. 

The daytime running lamp (DRL) control relay is located in the 
passenger compartment under the LH side of the instrument panel (04320)

[FIGURE: GK2175A.gif]
